**Robert Preston Meservey** (June 8, 1918 – March 21, 1987) was an American stage and screen actor, best known for his role as Professor Harold Hill in the 1957 musical _[The Music Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Music\_Man "The Music Man")_, for which he received the [Tony Award for Best Actor in a Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Musical "Tony Award for Best Actor in a Musical"). He reprised the role in the [1962 film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Music_Man_(1962_film) "The Music Man (1962 film)"), and received a [Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Motion Picture Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actor_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Motion Picture Musical or Comedy") nomination.

Preston made his Broadway debut in _[The Male Animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Male\_Animal "The Male Animal")_ in 1952. He won two [Tony Awards for Best Actor in a Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Musical "Tony Award for Best Actor in a Musical") for _The Music Man_ (1957) and _[I Do! I Do!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Do!\_I\_Do!\_(musical) "I Do! I Do! (musical)")_ (1967) and was Tony-nominated for _[Mack and Mabel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mack\_and\_Mabel "Mack and Mabel")_ (1975). He co-starred alongside Steve McQueen in the [Sam Peckinpah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Peckinpah "Sam Peckinpah") film _[Junior Bonner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior\_Bonner "Junior Bonner")_ (1972). Preston collaborated twice with director [Blake Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake_Edwards "Blake Edwards"), first in _[S.O.B.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.O.B.\_(film) "S.O.B. (film)")_ (1981) and again in _[Victor/Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor/Victoria "Victor/Victoria")_ (1982), winning a [National Society of Film Critics Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Society_of_Film_Critics_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "National Society of Film Critics Award for Best Supporting Actor") for his turn in the former, whilst earning him nominations for both a [Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Motion Picture Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actor_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Motion Picture Musical or Comedy") and an [Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor"), as well as winning the [National Board of Review Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "National Board of Review Award for Best Supporting Actor"), for the latter.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-1)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Preston_(actor)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Preston was born Robert Preston Meservey in [Newton, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newton,_Massachusetts "Newton, Massachusetts"), the son of Ruth L. (née Rea) and Frank Wesley Meservey, a garment worker and a billing clerk for [American Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Express "American Express").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Ross-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-ancestry-4) His family moved to [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") in his youth; he graduated from [Abraham Lincoln High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln_High_School_(Los_Angeles,_California) "Abraham Lincoln High School (Los Angeles, California)") in January 1935.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Preston_(actor)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 1938–1942: Career beginnings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Preston_(actor)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1938–1942: Career beginnings")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/Dorothy_Lamour_and_Robert_Preston_in_%27Typhoon%27%2C_1940_%282%29.jpg/250px-Dorothy_Lamour_and_Robert_Preston_in_%27Typhoon%27%2C_1940_%282%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dorothy_Lamour_and_Robert_Preston_in_'Typhoon',_1940_(2).jpg)

Advertisement for _[Typhoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoon\_(1940\_film) "Typhoon (1940 film)")_ (1940) featuring Preston and [Dorothy Lamour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Lamour "Dorothy Lamour")

Preston appeared in a stock company production of [_Julius Caesar_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julius_Caesar_(play) "Julius Caesar (play)") and a Pasadena Playhouse production of _[Idiot's Delight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idiot's\_Delight\_(play) "Idiot's Delight (play)")._ A [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures") attorney liked his work and recruited him to the studio.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-6) The _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ reported that Preston's mother was employed by [Decca Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decca_Records "Decca Records"), [Bing Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing_Crosby "Bing Crosby")'s label, and was acquainted with Crosby's brother Everett, a [talent agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talent_agent "Talent agent"); she convinced him to watch one of Preston's performances at the Pasadena Playhouse. The result was a contract with the Crosby agency and a movie deal with [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures"), Crosby's studio. Preston made his screen debut in 1938, in the crime dramas _[King of Alcatraz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_of\_Alcatraz "King of Alcatraz")_ (1938)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) and _[Illegal Traffic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal\_Traffic "Illegal Traffic")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-8)

The studio ordered Preston to stop using his family name of Meservey.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Mano-9) As Robert Preston, the name by which he was known for his entire professional career, he appeared in many Hollywood films, predominantly but not exclusively [Westerns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_(genre) "Western (genre)"). He was Digby Geste in the sound remake of _[Beau Geste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beau\_Geste\_(1939\_film) "Beau Geste (1939 film)")_ (1939) with [Gary Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Cooper "Gary Cooper") and [Ray Milland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Milland "Ray Milland"), and Dick Allen in the Cecil B DeMille epic _[Union Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union\_Pacific\_(film) "Union Pacific (film)")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) Although not awarded until 2002 due to World War II, the film was the first winner of the [Palme d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palme_d'Or "Palme d'Or") for 1939. He was featured in _[North West Mounted Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North\_West\_Mounted\_Police\_(film) "North West Mounted Police (film)")_ (1940), also with Cooper. He played a Los Angeles police detective in the noir _[This Gun for Hire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This\_Gun\_for\_Hire "This Gun for Hire")_ (1942).

### 1942–1945: Military service

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Preston_(actor)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1942–1945: Military service")]

[![Image 9: icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/99/Question_book-new.svg/60px-Question_book-new.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Question_book-new.svg)This section **does not [cite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources") any [sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")**. [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") interrupted Preston's Paramount assignments.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) Following the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, he joined the [United States Army Air Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Air_Forces "United States Army Air Forces") and served as an [intelligence officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence_officer "Intelligence officer") in the [U.S. 9th Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Forces_Central#History "United States Air Forces Central") with the [386th Bombardment Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/386th_Bombardment_Group "386th Bombardment Group") (Medium). At the end of the war in Europe, the 386th and Captain Robert Meservey, an S-2 Officer (intelligence), were stationed in [Sint-Truiden, Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sint-Truiden "Sint-Truiden"). Meservey's job had been receiving intelligence reports from 9th Air Force headquarters and briefing the bomber crews on what to expect in accomplishing their missions.

### 1947–1956: Return to acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Preston_(actor)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 1947–1956: Return to acting")]

When Preston resumed his movie career in 1947, it was as a freelance character actor, accepting roles for Paramount, [RKO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RKO_Radio_Pictures "RKO Radio Pictures"), [Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer "Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer"), and various independent producers. Although Preston appeared in many films during this period, he never achieved major stardom. In an interview from 1984, he recalled, "I played the lead in all the 'B' pictures and the villain in all the epics. After a while, it was clear to me I had sort of reached what I was going to be in movies."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Richards-10) During the 1950s, Preston found additional roles in television.

### 1957–1979: _The Music Man_ and acclaim

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Preston_(actor)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1957–1979: The Music Man and acclaim")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/Gregory_Peck%2C_Joan_Bennett%2C_Robert_Preston_The_Macomber_Affair.jpg/250px-Gregory_Peck%2C_Joan_Bennett%2C_Robert_Preston_The_Macomber_Affair.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gregory_Peck,_Joan_Bennett,_Robert_Preston_The_Macomber_Affair.jpg)

[Gregory Peck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregory_Peck "Gregory Peck"), [Joan Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Bennett "Joan Bennett") and Preston in _[The Macomber Affair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Macomber\_Affair "The Macomber Affair")_ (1947)

Preston is probably best known for his performance as Professor Harold Hill in [Meredith Willson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meredith_Willson "Meredith Willson")'s musical _The Music Man_ (1957).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) He had appeared on stage, but it was his first musical.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-:0-11) "They'd run through all the musical comedy people before they cast me", he remembered years later.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Richards-10) He won a [Tony Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award "Tony Award") for his performance.

He appeared on the cover of _Time_ on July 21, 1958.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Time-12)

In 1961, Preston was asked to make a recording as part of a program by the [President's Council on Physical Fitness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President's_Council_on_Physical_Fitness "President's Council on Physical Fitness") to encourage schoolchildren to do more daily exercise. The song, _[Chicken Fat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicken\_Fat\_(song) "Chicken Fat (song)")_, composed by Meredith Willson and performed by Preston with full orchestral accompaniment, was recorded during sessions for _The Music Man_ soundtrack. The recording was distributed by [Capitol Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitol_Records "Capitol Records") to elementary schools across the nation and played for students as they performed [calisthenics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calisthenics "Calisthenics").

In 1962, Preston starred opposite Shirley Jones in the film version of _The Music Man_, although, surprisingly, he was not the studio’s first choice despite his success on Broadway. Warner Brothers wanted to cast [Frank Sinatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Sinatra "Frank Sinatra") as the fast-talking Harold Hill, but playwright Willson insisted that Preston be cast.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-:0-11)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-13)

He played an important supporting role as wagonmaster Roger Morgan, in the MGM epic [_How the West Was Won_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_the_West_Was_Won_(film) "How the West Was Won (film)") (1962).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/Robert_Preston_Mary_Martin_Ido%21_Ido%21_1966.jpg/250px-Robert_Preston_Mary_Martin_Ido%21_Ido%21_1966.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Robert_Preston_Mary_Martin_Ido!_Ido!_1966.jpg)

Preston and [Mary Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Martin "Mary Martin") in the Broadway play _[I Do! I Do!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Do!\_I\_Do! "I Do! I Do!")_ (1966)

In 1966, Preston was the male half of the two-character musical _[I Do! I Do!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Do!\_I\_Do! "I Do! I Do!")_ with [Mary Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Martin "Mary Martin"), for which he won his second Tony Award.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) In 1964 he starred in the title role in the musical _[Ben Franklin in Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben\_Franklin\_in\_Paris "Ben Franklin in Paris")_,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) and he originated the role of [Henry II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_II_of_England "Henry II of England") in the stage production of _[The Lion in Winter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lion\_in\_Winter "The Lion in Winter")_, whom [Peter O'Toole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_O'Toole "Peter O'Toole") portrayed in the film version, receiving an Academy Award nomination. In 1974, he starred alongside [Bernadette Peters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernadette_Peters "Bernadette Peters") in [Jerry Herman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Herman "Jerry Herman")'s Broadway musical _[Mack & Mabel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mack\_&\_Mabel "Mack & Mabel")_ as [Mack Sennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mack_Sennett "Mack Sennett"), the famous [silent film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silent_film "Silent film") director.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) That same year, the film version of _[Mame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mame\_(film) "Mame (film)"),_ another Jerry Herman musical, was released with Preston starring, alongside [Lucille Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucille_Ball "Lucille Ball"), in the role of Beauregard Burnside.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7)

In 1978, Preston starred in another musical that did not make it to Broadway, _The Prince of Grand Street,_ in which he played a matinee idol of New York's Yiddish theater who refused to renounce the roles he had played in his youth, despite having aged out of them. With a libretto and songs by [Bob Merrill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Merrill "Bob Merrill") and direction by [Gene Saks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Saks "Gene Saks"), the show folded during its [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston") tryout.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-14) In 1979, Preston portrayed a [snake-handling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake_handling_in_Christianity "Snake handling in Christianity") family [patriarch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriarch "Patriarch") Hadley Chisholm in a [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") Western [miniseries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miniseries "Miniseries"), _[The Chisholms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chisholms "The Chisholms")_, with [Rosemary Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosemary_Harris "Rosemary Harris") as his wife, Minerva. The story chronicled the Chisholm family losing their land in [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia") and migrating to the west to begin a new life. When CBS continued the saga as a weekly series the following year, Preston reprised his role, but his character died in the fifth episode. The series, which also featured co-stars [Ben Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Murphy "Ben Murphy"), [Brett Cullen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Cullen "Brett Cullen"), and James Van Patten, lasted only four more episodes after Preston's departure.

### Later career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Preston_(actor)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Later career")]

Preston's other film roles during the 1970s included Ace Bonner in [Sam Peckinpah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Peckinpah "Sam Peckinpah")'s _[Junior Bonner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior\_Bonner "Junior Bonner")_ (1972), Joseph Dobbs in the mystery _[Child's Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child's\_Play\_(1972\_film) "Child's Play (1972 film)")_, directed by [Sidney Lumet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidney_Lumet "Sidney Lumet"), and "Big Ed" Bookman in _[Semi-Tough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-Tough "Semi-Tough")_ (1977). He appeared in [Blake Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake_Edwards "Blake Edwards")' Hollywood satire, _[S.O.B.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.O.B.\_(film) "S.O.B. (film)")_ (1981) and Edwards' _[Victor/Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor/Victoria "Victor/Victoria")_ (1982), for which he was nominated for an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") as [Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) His last role in a theatrical film was in _[The Last Starfighter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Starfighter "The Last Starfighter")_ (1984) as an interstellar [military recruiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_recruiter "Military recruiter") called "Centauri". Preston said that he based his approach to the character of Centauri on that which he had taken to Professor Harold Hill. Indeed, the role of Centauri was written for him with his performance as Harold Hill in mind.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Plummer-15) On television, Preston starred in the well-received [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS")[whodunit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whodunit "Whodunit")_[Rehearsal for Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rehearsal\_for\_Murder "Rehearsal for Murder")_ (1982), as a playwright attempting to solve the murder of his fiancée. He portrayed an aging gunfighter in _September Gun_ (1983), a CBS TV Western film opposite [Patty Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patty_Duke "Patty Duke") and [Christopher Lloyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Lloyd "Christopher Lloyd"). In 1985, he starred in another well-received TV movie [_Finnegan, Begin Again_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnegan_Begin_Again "Finnegan Begin Again") with [Mary Tyler Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Tyler_Moore "Mary Tyler Moore"), for [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) Preston's final role was in the CBS TV film _Outrage!_ (1986); he appeared as a grief-stricken father who seeks justice for the brutal rape and murder of his daughter.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Page-16)

## Personal life and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Preston_(actor)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life and death")]

Preston married actress [Catherine Craig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_Craig "Catherine Craig") in 1940.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-17) Preston was diagnosed with [lung cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung_cancer "Lung cancer") in 1986; he died of the disease on March 21, 1987 in [Montecito, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montecito,_California "Montecito, California").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Page-16)

**Robert Preston Meservey** (June 8, 1918 – March 21, 1987) was an American stage and screen actor, best known for his role as Professor Harold Hill in the 1957 musical _[The Music Man](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Music\_Man "The Music Man")_, for which he received the [Tony Award for Best Actor in a Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Musical "Tony Award for Best Actor in a Musical"). He reprised the role in the [1962 film adaptation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Music_Man_(1962_film) "The Music Man (1962 film)"), and received a [Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Motion Picture Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actor_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Motion Picture Musical or Comedy") nomination.

Preston made his Broadway debut in _[The Male Animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Male\_Animal "The Male Animal")_ in 1952. He won two [Tony Awards for Best Actor in a Musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award_for_Best_Actor_in_a_Musical "Tony Award for Best Actor in a Musical") for _The Music Man_ (1957) and _[I Do! I Do!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Do!\_I\_Do!\_(musical) "I Do! I Do! (musical)")_ (1967) and was Tony-nominated for _[Mack and Mabel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mack\_and\_Mabel "Mack and Mabel")_ (1975). He co-starred alongside Steve McQueen in the [Sam Peckinpah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Peckinpah "Sam Peckinpah") film _[Junior Bonner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior\_Bonner "Junior Bonner")_ (1972). Preston collaborated twice with director [Blake Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake_Edwards "Blake Edwards"), first in _[S.O.B.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.O.B.\_(film) "S.O.B. (film)")_ (1981) and again in _[Victor/Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor/Victoria "Victor/Victoria")_ (1982), winning a [National Society of Film Critics Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Society_of_Film_Critics_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "National Society of Film Critics Award for Best Supporting Actor") for his turn in the former, whilst earning him nominations for both a [Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Motion Picture Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actor_%E2%80%93_Motion_Picture_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actor – Motion Picture Musical or Comedy") and an [Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor"), as well as winning the [National Board of Review Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Board_of_Review_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "National Board of Review Award for Best Supporting Actor"), for the latter.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-1)

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Preston_(actor)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Preston was born Robert Preston Meservey in [Newton, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newton,_Massachusetts "Newton, Massachusetts"), the son of Ruth L. (née Rea) and Frank Wesley Meservey, a garment worker and a billing clerk for [American Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Express "American Express").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Ross-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-ancestry-4) His family moved to [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles") in his youth; he graduated from [Abraham Lincoln High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abraham_Lincoln_High_School_(Los_Angeles,_California) "Abraham Lincoln High School (Los Angeles, California)") in January 1935.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-5)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Preston_(actor)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### 1938–1942: Career beginnings

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Preston_(actor)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1938–1942: Career beginnings")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e5/Dorothy_Lamour_and_Robert_Preston_in_%27Typhoon%27%2C_1940_%282%29.jpg/250px-Dorothy_Lamour_and_Robert_Preston_in_%27Typhoon%27%2C_1940_%282%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Dorothy_Lamour_and_Robert_Preston_in_'Typhoon',_1940_(2).jpg)

Advertisement for _[Typhoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoon\_(1940\_film) "Typhoon (1940 film)")_ (1940) featuring Preston and [Dorothy Lamour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Lamour "Dorothy Lamour")

Preston appeared in a stock company production of [_Julius Caesar_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Julius_Caesar_(play) "Julius Caesar (play)") and a Pasadena Playhouse production of _[Idiot's Delight](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Idiot's\_Delight\_(play) "Idiot's Delight (play)")._ A [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures") attorney liked his work and recruited him to the studio.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-6) The _[Los Angeles Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los\_Angeles\_Times "Los Angeles Times")_ reported that Preston's mother was employed by [Decca Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decca_Records "Decca Records"), [Bing Crosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bing_Crosby "Bing Crosby")'s label, and was acquainted with Crosby's brother Everett, a [talent agent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Talent_agent "Talent agent"); she convinced him to watch one of Preston's performances at the Pasadena Playhouse. The result was a contract with the Crosby agency and a movie deal with [Paramount Pictures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount_Pictures "Paramount Pictures"), Crosby's studio. Preston made his screen debut in 1938, in the crime dramas _[King of Alcatraz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King\_of\_Alcatraz "King of Alcatraz")_ (1938)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) and _[Illegal Traffic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Illegal\_Traffic "Illegal Traffic")_.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-8)

The studio ordered Preston to stop using his family name of Meservey.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Mano-9) As Robert Preston, the name by which he was known for his entire professional career, he appeared in many Hollywood films, predominantly but not exclusively [Westerns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Western_(genre) "Western (genre)"). He was Digby Geste in the sound remake of _[Beau Geste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beau\_Geste\_(1939\_film) "Beau Geste (1939 film)")_ (1939) with [Gary Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gary_Cooper "Gary Cooper") and [Ray Milland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_Milland "Ray Milland"), and Dick Allen in the Cecil B DeMille epic _[Union Pacific](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Union\_Pacific\_(film) "Union Pacific (film)")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) Although not awarded until 2002 due to World War II, the film was the first winner of the [Palme d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palme_d'Or "Palme d'Or") for 1939. He was featured in _[North West Mounted Police](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/North\_West\_Mounted\_Police\_(film) "North West Mounted Police (film)")_ (1940), also with Cooper. He played a Los Angeles police detective in the noir _[This Gun for Hire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/This\_Gun\_for\_Hire "This Gun for Hire")_ (1942).

### 1942–1945: Military service

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Preston_(actor)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1942–1945: Military service")]

[![Image 9: icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/en/thumb/9/99/Question_book-new.svg/60px-Question_book-new.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Question_book-new.svg)This section **does not [cite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citing_sources "Wikipedia:Citing sources") any [sources](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Verifiability "Wikipedia:Verifiability")**. [World War II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/World_War_II "World War II") interrupted Preston's Paramount assignments.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) Following the Japanese attack on Pearl Harbor, he joined the [United States Army Air Forces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Army_Air_Forces "United States Army Air Forces") and served as an [intelligence officer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence_officer "Intelligence officer") in the [U.S. 9th Air Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Air_Forces_Central#History "United States Air Forces Central") with the [386th Bombardment Group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/386th_Bombardment_Group "386th Bombardment Group") (Medium). At the end of the war in Europe, the 386th and Captain Robert Meservey, an S-2 Officer (intelligence), were stationed in [Sint-Truiden, Belgium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sint-Truiden "Sint-Truiden"). Meservey's job had been receiving intelligence reports from 9th Air Force headquarters and briefing the bomber crews on what to expect in accomplishing their missions.

### 1947–1956: Return to acting

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Preston_(actor)&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 1947–1956: Return to acting")]

When Preston resumed his movie career in 1947, it was as a freelance character actor, accepting roles for Paramount, [RKO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RKO_Radio_Pictures "RKO Radio Pictures"), [Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer "Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer"), and various independent producers. Although Preston appeared in many films during this period, he never achieved major stardom. In an interview from 1984, he recalled, "I played the lead in all the 'B' pictures and the villain in all the epics. After a while, it was clear to me I had sort of reached what I was going to be in movies."[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Richards-10) During the 1950s, Preston found additional roles in television.

### 1957–1979: _The Music Man_ and acclaim

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Preston_(actor)&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 1957–1979: The Music Man and acclaim")]

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/Gregory_Peck%2C_Joan_Bennett%2C_Robert_Preston_The_Macomber_Affair.jpg/250px-Gregory_Peck%2C_Joan_Bennett%2C_Robert_Preston_The_Macomber_Affair.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Gregory_Peck,_Joan_Bennett,_Robert_Preston_The_Macomber_Affair.jpg)

[Gregory Peck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gregory_Peck "Gregory Peck"), [Joan Bennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joan_Bennett "Joan Bennett") and Preston in _[The Macomber Affair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Macomber\_Affair "The Macomber Affair")_ (1947)

Preston is probably best known for his performance as Professor Harold Hill in [Meredith Willson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meredith_Willson "Meredith Willson")'s musical _The Music Man_ (1957).[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) He had appeared on stage, but it was his first musical.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-:0-11) "They'd run through all the musical comedy people before they cast me", he remembered years later.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Richards-10) He won a [Tony Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Award "Tony Award") for his performance.

He appeared on the cover of _Time_ on July 21, 1958.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Time-12)

In 1961, Preston was asked to make a recording as part of a program by the [President's Council on Physical Fitness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President's_Council_on_Physical_Fitness "President's Council on Physical Fitness") to encourage schoolchildren to do more daily exercise. The song, _[Chicken Fat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicken\_Fat\_(song) "Chicken Fat (song)")_, composed by Meredith Willson and performed by Preston with full orchestral accompaniment, was recorded during sessions for _The Music Man_ soundtrack. The recording was distributed by [Capitol Records](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitol_Records "Capitol Records") to elementary schools across the nation and played for students as they performed [calisthenics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calisthenics "Calisthenics").

In 1962, Preston starred opposite Shirley Jones in the film version of _The Music Man_, although, surprisingly, he was not the studio’s first choice despite his success on Broadway. Warner Brothers wanted to cast [Frank Sinatra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Sinatra "Frank Sinatra") as the fast-talking Harold Hill, but playwright Willson insisted that Preston be cast.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-:0-11)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-13)

He played an important supporting role as wagonmaster Roger Morgan, in the MGM epic [_How the West Was Won_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/How_the_West_Was_Won_(film) "How the West Was Won (film)") (1962).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/55/Robert_Preston_Mary_Martin_Ido%21_Ido%21_1966.jpg/250px-Robert_Preston_Mary_Martin_Ido%21_Ido%21_1966.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Robert_Preston_Mary_Martin_Ido!_Ido!_1966.jpg)

Preston and [Mary Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Martin "Mary Martin") in the Broadway play _[I Do! I Do!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Do!\_I\_Do! "I Do! I Do!")_ (1966)

In 1966, Preston was the male half of the two-character musical _[I Do! I Do!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/I\_Do!\_I\_Do! "I Do! I Do!")_ with [Mary Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Martin "Mary Martin"), for which he won his second Tony Award.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) In 1964 he starred in the title role in the musical _[Ben Franklin in Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben\_Franklin\_in\_Paris "Ben Franklin in Paris")_,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) and he originated the role of [Henry II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henry_II_of_England "Henry II of England") in the stage production of _[The Lion in Winter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Lion\_in\_Winter "The Lion in Winter")_, whom [Peter O'Toole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_O'Toole "Peter O'Toole") portrayed in the film version, receiving an Academy Award nomination. In 1974, he starred alongside [Bernadette Peters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bernadette_Peters "Bernadette Peters") in [Jerry Herman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jerry_Herman "Jerry Herman")'s Broadway musical _[Mack & Mabel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mack\_&\_Mabel "Mack & Mabel")_ as [Mack Sennett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mack_Sennett "Mack Sennett"), the famous [silent film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silent_film "Silent film") director.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) That same year, the film version of _[Mame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mame\_(film) "Mame (film)"),_ another Jerry Herman musical, was released with Preston starring, alongside [Lucille Ball](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lucille_Ball "Lucille Ball"), in the role of Beauregard Burnside.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7)

In 1978, Preston starred in another musical that did not make it to Broadway, _The Prince of Grand Street,_ in which he played a matinee idol of New York's Yiddish theater who refused to renounce the roles he had played in his youth, despite having aged out of them. With a libretto and songs by [Bob Merrill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bob_Merrill "Bob Merrill") and direction by [Gene Saks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene_Saks "Gene Saks"), the show folded during its [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston") tryout.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-14) In 1979, Preston portrayed a [snake-handling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake_handling_in_Christianity "Snake handling in Christianity") family [patriarch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patriarch "Patriarch") Hadley Chisholm in a [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") Western [miniseries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Miniseries "Miniseries"), _[The Chisholms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Chisholms "The Chisholms")_, with [Rosemary Harris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rosemary_Harris "Rosemary Harris") as his wife, Minerva. The story chronicled the Chisholm family losing their land in [Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia "Virginia") and migrating to the west to begin a new life. When CBS continued the saga as a weekly series the following year, Preston reprised his role, but his character died in the fifth episode. The series, which also featured co-stars [Ben Murphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ben_Murphy "Ben Murphy"), [Brett Cullen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brett_Cullen "Brett Cullen"), and James Van Patten, lasted only four more episodes after Preston's departure.

### Later career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Preston_(actor)&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Later career")]

Preston's other film roles during the 1970s included Ace Bonner in [Sam Peckinpah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sam_Peckinpah "Sam Peckinpah")'s _[Junior Bonner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junior\_Bonner "Junior Bonner")_ (1972), Joseph Dobbs in the mystery _[Child's Play](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child's\_Play\_(1972\_film) "Child's Play (1972 film)")_, directed by [Sidney Lumet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sidney_Lumet "Sidney Lumet"), and "Big Ed" Bookman in _[Semi-Tough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-Tough "Semi-Tough")_ (1977). He appeared in [Blake Edwards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blake_Edwards "Blake Edwards")' Hollywood satire, _[S.O.B.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S.O.B.\_(film) "S.O.B. (film)")_ (1981) and Edwards' _[Victor/Victoria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Victor/Victoria "Victor/Victoria")_ (1982), for which he was nominated for an [Academy Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award "Academy Award") as [Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) His last role in a theatrical film was in _[The Last Starfighter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Last\_Starfighter "The Last Starfighter")_ (1984) as an interstellar [military recruiter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Military_recruiter "Military recruiter") called "Centauri". Preston said that he based his approach to the character of Centauri on that which he had taken to Professor Harold Hill. Indeed, the role of Centauri was written for him with his performance as Harold Hill in mind.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Plummer-15) On television, Preston starred in the well-received [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS")[whodunit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whodunit "Whodunit")_[Rehearsal for Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rehearsal\_for\_Murder "Rehearsal for Murder")_ (1982), as a playwright attempting to solve the murder of his fiancée. He portrayed an aging gunfighter in _September Gun_ (1983), a CBS TV Western film opposite [Patty Duke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patty_Duke "Patty Duke") and [Christopher Lloyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Lloyd "Christopher Lloyd"). In 1985, he starred in another well-received TV movie [_Finnegan, Begin Again_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finnegan_Begin_Again "Finnegan Begin Again") with [Mary Tyler Moore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Tyler_Moore "Mary Tyler Moore"), for [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Larkin50-7) Preston's final role was in the CBS TV film _Outrage!_ (1986); he appeared as a grief-stricken father who seeks justice for the brutal rape and murder of his daughter.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Page-16)

## Personal life and death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Robert_Preston_(actor)&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Personal life and death")]

Preston married actress [Catherine Craig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catherine_Craig "Catherine Craig") in 1940.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-17) Preston was diagnosed with [lung cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung_cancer "Lung cancer") in 1986; he died of the disease on March 21, 1987 in [Montecito, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montecito,_California "Montecito, California").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Preston_(actor)#cite_note-Page-16)

# Top-20 actors (male) 1960-1970

![Image 3: Richard Burton](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BZTg2MWQ2YjctYTEwZC00OTAyLWI2YmYtMTgwOTM1NTZlY2UyXkEyXkFqcGc@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg) [](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000009/?ref_=ls_i_1)  

 #### [1. Richard Burton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000009/?ref_=ls_t_1) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Director

[Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061184/?ref_=ls_knf_1)

Probably best-remembered for his turbulent personal life with Elizabeth Taylor (whom he married twice), Richard Burton was nonetheless also regarded as an often brilliant British actor of the post-WWII period.  
  
Burton was born Richard Walter Jenkins in 1925 into a Welsh (Cymraeg)-speaking family in Pontrhydyfen to Edith Maude (Thomas) and Richard Walter Jenkins, a coal miner. The twelfth of thirteen children, his mother died while he was a toddler and his father later abandoned the family, leaving him to be raised by an elder sister, Cecilia. An avid fan of Shakespeare, poetry and reading, he once said "home is where the books are". He received a scholarship to Oxford University to study acting and made his first stage appearance in 1944.  
  
His first film appearances were in routine British movies such as [Woman of Dolwyn (1949)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0041579/?ls), [Waterfront Women (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0043121/?ls) and [Green Grow the Rushes (1951)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0043601/?ls). Then he started to appear in Hollywood movies such as [My Cousin Rachel (1952)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0044937/?ls), [The Robe (1953)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0046247/?ls) and [Alexander the Great (1956)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048937/?ls), added to this he was also spending considerable time in stage productions, both in the UK and USA, often to splendid reviews. The late 1950s was an exciting and inventive time in UK cinema, often referred to as the "British New Wave", and Burton was right in the thick of things, and showcased a sensational performance in [Look Back in Anger (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051879/?ls). He also appeared with a cavalcade of international stars in the World War II magnum opus [The Longest Day (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056197/?ls), and then onto arguably his most "notorious" role as that of Marc Antony opposite [Elizabeth Taylor](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000072/?ls) in the hugely expensive [Cleopatra (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056937/?ls). This was, of course, the film that kick-started their fiery and passionate romance (plus two marriages), and the two of them appeared in several productions over the next few years including [The V.I.P.s (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057634/?ls), [The Sandpiper (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059674/?ls), the dynamic [Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061184/?ls) and [The Taming of the Shrew (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061407/?ls), as well as box office flops like [The Comedians (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061502/?ls). Burton did better when he was off on his own giving higher caliber performances, such as those in [Becket (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057877/?ls), the film adaptation of the [Tennessee Williams](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0931783/?ls) play [The Night of the Iguana (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0058404/?ls), the brilliant espionage thriller [The Spy Who Came in from the Cold (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059749/?ls) and alongside [Clint Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000142/?ls) in the World War II action adventure film [Where Eagles Dare (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065207/?ls).  
  
His audience appeal began to decline somewhat by the end of the 1960s as fans turned to younger, more virile male stars, however Burton was superb in [Anne of the Thousand Days (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064030/?ls) as King Henry VIII, he put on a reasonable show in the boring [Raid on Rommel (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067650/?ls), was over the top in the awful [Villain (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067952/?ls), gave sleepwalking performances in [Hammersmith Is Out (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068674/?ls) and [Bluebeard (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068294/?ls), and was wildly miscast in the ludicrous [The Assassination of Trotsky (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068226/?ls).  
  
By the early 1970s, quality male lead roles were definitely going to other stars, and Burton found himself appearing in some movies of dubious quality, just to pay the bills and support family, including [Divorce His - Divorce Hers (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0069980/?ls) (his last on-screen appearance with Taylor), [The Klansman (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0071721/?ls), [Brief Encounter (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0071247/?ls), [Jackpot (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0198158/?ls) (which was never completed) and [Exorcist II: The Heretic (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0076009/?ls). However, he won another Oscar nomination for his excellent performance as a concerned psychiatrist in [Equus (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0075995/?ls). He appeared with fellow acting icons [Richard Harris](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001321/?ls) and [Roger Moore](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000549/?ls) in [The Wild Geese (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0078492/?ls) about mercenaries in South Africa. While the film had a modest initial run, over the past thirty-five years it has picked up quite a cult following. His final performances were as the wily inquisitor "O'Brien" in the most recent film version of George Orwell's dystopian [1984 (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0087803/?ls), in which he won good reviews, and in the TV mini series [Ellis Island (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0086705/?ls). He passed away on August 5, 1984 in Celigny, Switzerland from a cerebral hemorrhage.

 #### [2. Sidney Poitier](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001627/?ref_=ls_t_2) 

    *   Actor
    *   Director
    *   Producer

[In the Heat of the Night (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061811/?ref_=ls_knf_2)

Sidney Poitier was a native of Cat Island, Bahamas, although born, two months prematurely, in Miami during a visit by his parents, Evelyn (Outten) and Reginald James Poitier. He grew up in poverty as the son of farmers, with his father also driving a cab in Nassau. Sidney had little formal education and at the age of 15 was sent to Miami to live with his brother, in order to forestall a growing tendency toward delinquency. In the U.S., he experienced the racial chasm that divides the country, a great shock to a boy coming from a society with a majority of African descent.  
  
At 18, he went to New York, did menial jobs and slept in a bus terminal toilet. A brief stint in the Army as a worker at a veterans' hospital was followed by more menial jobs in Harlem. An impulsive audition at the American Negro Theatre was rejected so forcefully that Poitier dedicated the next six months to overcoming his accent and improving his performing skills. On his second try, he was accepted. Spotted in rehearsal by a casting agent, he won a bit part in the Broadway production of "Lysistrata", for which he earned good reviews. By the end of 1949, he was having to choose between leading roles on stage and an offer to work for [Darryl F. Zanuck](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0953123/?ls) in the film [No Way Out (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0042792/?ls). His performance as a doctor treating a white bigot got him plenty of notice and led to more roles. Nevertheless, the roles were still less interesting and prominent than those white actors routinely obtained. But seven years later, after turning down several projects he considered demeaning, Poitier got a number of roles that catapulted him into a category rarely if ever achieved by an African-American man of that time, that of leading man. One of these films, [The Defiant Ones (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051525/?ls), earned Poitier his first Academy Award nomination as Best Actor. Five years later, he won the Oscar for [Lilies of the Field (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057251/?ls), the first African American to win for a leading role.  
  
He remained active on stage and screen as well as in the burgeoning Civil Rights movement. His roles in [Guess Who's Coming to Dinner (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061735/?ls) and [To Sir, with Love (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0062376/?ls) were landmarks in helping to break down some social barriers between blacks and whites. Poitier's talent, conscience, integrity, and inherent likability placed him on equal footing with the white stars of the day. He took on directing and producing chores in the 1970s, achieving success in both arenas.

 #### [3. Burt Lancaster](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000044/?ref_=ls_t_3) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Additional Crew

[From Here to Eternity (1953)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0045793/?ref_=ls_knf_3)

Burt Lancaster, one of five children, was born in Manhattan, to Elizabeth (Roberts) and James Henry Lancaster, a postal worker. All his grandparents were immigrants from the north of Ireland. He was a tough street kid who took an early interest in gymnastics. He joined the circus as an acrobat and worked there until he was injured. In the Army during WWII he was introduced to the USO and to acting. His first film was [The Killers (1946)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0038669/?ls), and that made him a star. He was a self-taught actor who learned the business as he went along. He set up his own production company in 1948 with [Harold Hecht](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0372959/?ls) and [James Hill](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0384343/?ls) to direct his career. He played many different roles in pictures as varied as [The Crimson Pirate (1952)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0044517/?ls), [From Here to Eternity (1953)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0045793/?ls), [Elmer Gantry (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0053793/?ls) and [Atlantic City (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080388/?ls).  
  
His production company, Hecht-Hill-Lancaster, produced such films as [Paddy Chayefsky](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0154665/?ls)'s [Marty (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048356/?ls) (Oscar winner 1955) and [The Catered Affair (1956)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0049061/?ls). In the 1980s he appeared as a supporting player in a number of movies, such as [Local Hero (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0085859/?ls) and [Field of Dreams (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097351/?ls). However, it will be the sound of his voice, the way that he laughed, and the larger-than-life characters he played that will always be remembered.

[Million Dollar Baby (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0405159/?ref_=ls_knf_4)

Clinton Eastwood Jr. was born May 31, 1930 in San Francisco, to Clinton Eastwood Sr., a bond salesman and later manufacturing executive for Georgia-Pacific Corporation, and [Ruth Wood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2503495/?ls) (née Margret Ruth Runner), a housewife turned IBM clerk. He grew up in nearby Piedmont. At school Clint took interest in music and mechanics, but was an otherwise bored student; this resulted in being held back a grade.  
  
In 1949, the year he graduated from high school, his parents and younger sister Jeanne moved to Seattle. Clint spent a couple years in the Pacific Northwest himself, operating log broncs in Springfield, Oregon, with summer gigs life-guarding in Renton, Washington. Returning to California in 1951, he did a two-year stint at Fort Ord Military Reservation and later enrolled at L.A. City College, but dropped out to pursue acting.  
  
During the mid-1950s he landed uncredited bit parts in such Z movies as [Revenge of the Creature (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048554/?ls) and [Tarantula (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048696/?ls) while digging swimming pools and driving a garbage truck to supplement his income. In 1958, he landed his first consequential acting role in the long-running TV show [Rawhide (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0052504/?ls) with [Eric Fleming](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0281661/?ls). Although only a secondary player the first seven seasons, he was promoted to series star when Fleming departed--both literally and figuratively--in its final year, along the way becoming a recognizable face to television viewers around the country.  
  
Eastwood's big-screen breakthrough came as The Man with No Name in [Sergio Leone](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001466/?ls)'s trilogy of excellent spaghetti westerns: [A Fistful of Dollars (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0058461/?ls), [For a Few Dollars More (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059578/?ls), and [The Good, the Bad and the Ugly (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0060196/?ls). The movies were shown exclusively in Italy during their respective copyright years with [Enrico Maria Salerno](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0758066/?ls) providing the voice of Eastwood's character, finally getting American distribution in 1967-68. As the last film racked up respectable grosses, Eastwood, 37, rose from a barely registering actor to sought-after commodity in just a matter of months. Again a success was the late-blooming star's first U.S.-made western, [Hang 'Em High (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061747/?ls). He followed that up with the lead role in [Coogan's Bluff (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0062824/?ls) (the loose inspiration for the TV series [McCloud (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065317/?ls)), before playing second fiddle to [Richard Burton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000009/?ls) in the World War II epic [Where Eagles Dare (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065207/?ls) and [Lee Marvin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001511/?ls) in the bizarre musical [Paint Your Wagon (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064782/?ls). In [Two Mules for Sister Sara (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065134/?ls) and [Kelly's Heroes (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065938/?ls), Eastwood leaned in an experimental direction by combining tough-guy action with offbeat humor.  
  
1971 proved to be his busiest year in film. He starred as a sleazy Union soldier in [The Beguiled (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0066819/?ls) to critical acclaim, and made his directorial debut with the classic erotic thriller [Play Misty for Me (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067588/?ls). His role as the hard edge police inspector in [Dirty Harry (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0066999/?ls), meanwhile, boosted him to cultural icon status and helped popularize the loose-cannon cop genre. Eastwood put out a steady stream of entertaining movies thereafter: the westerns [Joe Kidd (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068768/?ls), [High Plains Drifter (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068699/?ls) and [The Outlaw Josey Wales (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0075029/?ls) (his first of six onscreen collaborations with then live-in love [Sondra Locke](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0516800/?ls)), the Dirty Harry sequels [Magnum Force (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0070355/?ls) and [The Enforcer (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0074483/?ls), the action-packed road adventures [Thunderbolt and Lightfoot (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0072288/?ls) and [The Gauntlet (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0076070/?ls), and the prison film [Escape from Alcatraz (1979)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0079116/?ls). He branched out into the comedy genre in 1978 with [Every Which Way But Loose (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0077523/?ls), which became the biggest hit of his career up to that time; taking inflation into account, it still is. In short, [The Eiger Sanction (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0072926/?ls) notwithstanding, the 1970s were nonstop success for Eastwood.  
  
Eastwood kicked off the 1980s with [Any Which Way You Can (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080377/?ls), the blockbuster sequel to Every Which Way but Loose. The fourth Dirty Harry film, [Sudden Impact (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0086383/?ls), was the highest-grossing film of the franchise and spawned his trademark catchphrase: "Make my day." He also starred in [Bronco Billy (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080472/?ls), [Firefox (1982)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0083943/?ls), [Tightrope (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0088272/?ls), [City Heat (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0087062/?ls), [Pale Rider (1985)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0089767/?ls) and [Heartbreak Ridge (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0091187/?ls), all of which were solid hits, with [Honkytonk Man (1982)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0084088/?ls) being his only commercial failure of the period. In 1988, he did his fifth and final Dirty Harry movie, [The Dead Pool (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094963/?ls). Although it was a success overall, it did not have the box office punch the previous films had. About this time, with outright bombs like [Pink Cadillac (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0098097/?ls) and [The Rookie (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0100514/?ls), it seemed Eastwood's star was declining as it never had before. He then started taking on low-key projects, directing [Bird (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094747/?ls), a biopic of [Charlie Parker](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0662127/?ls) that earned him a Golden Globe, and starring in and directing [White Hunter Black Heart (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0100928/?ls), an uneven, loose biopic of [John Huston](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001379/?ls) (both films had a limited release).  
  
Eastwood bounced back big time with his dark western [Unforgiven (1992)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0105695/?ls), which garnered the then 62-year-old his first ever Academy Award nomination (Best Actor), and an Oscar win for Best Director. Churning out a quick follow-up hit, he took on the secret service in [In the Line of Fire (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0107206/?ls), then accepted second billing for the first time since 1970 in the interesting but poorly received [A Perfect World (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0107808/?ls) with [Kevin Costner](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000126/?ls). Next was a love story, [The Bridges of Madison County (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0112579/?ls), where Eastwood surprised audiences with a sensitive performance alongside none other than [Meryl Streep](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000658/?ls). But it soon became apparent he was going backwards after his brief revival. Subsequent films were credible, but nothing really stuck out. [Absolute Power (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0118548/?ls) and [Space Cowboys (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0186566/?ls) did well enough, while [True Crime (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0139668/?ls) and [Blood Work (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0309377/?ls) were received badly, as was [Midnight in the Garden of Good and Evil (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0119668/?ls), which he directed but didn't appear in.  
  
Eastwood surprised again in the mid-2000s, returning to the top of the A-list with [Million Dollar Baby (2004)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0405159/?ls). Also starring [Hilary Swank](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005476/?ls) and [Morgan Freeman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000151/?ls), the hugely successful drama won four Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Director for Eastwood. He scored his second Best Actor nomination, too. His next starring vehicle, [Gran Torino (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1205489/?ls), earned almost $30 million in its opening weekend and was his highest grosser unadjusted for inflation. 2012 saw him in a rare lighthearted movie, [Trouble with the Curve (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2083383/?ls), as well as a reality show, [Mrs. Eastwood & Company (2012)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2305717/?ls).  
  
Between acting jobs, he chalked up an impressive list of credits behind the camera. He directed [Mystic River (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0327056/?ls) (in which [Sean Penn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000576/?ls) and [Tim Robbins](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000209/?ls) gave Oscar-winning performances), [Flags of Our Fathers (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0418689/?ls), [Letters from Iwo Jima (2006)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0498380/?ls) (nominated for the Best Picture Oscar), [Changeling (2008)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0824747/?ls) (a vehicle for [Angelina Jolie](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001401/?ls)), [Invictus (2009)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1057500/?ls) (again with Freeman), [Hereafter (2010)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1212419/?ls), [J. Edgar (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1616195/?ls), [Jersey Boys (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1742044/?ls), [American Sniper (2014)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt2179136/?ls) (2014's top box office champ), [Sully (2016)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3263904/?ls) (starring [Tom Hanks](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000158/?ls) as hero pilot [Chesley Sullenberger](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm3314810/?ls)) and [The 15:17 to Paris (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt6802308/?ls). Back on screens after a considerable absence, he played an unlikely drug courier in [The Mule (2018)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt7959026/?ls), which reached the top of the box office with a nine-figure gross, then directed [Richard Jewell (2019)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt3513548/?ls). At age 91, Eastwood made history as the oldest actor to star above the title in a movie with the release of [Cry Macho (2021)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt1924245/?ls).  
  
Away from the limelight, Eastwood has led an aberrant existence and is described by biographer [Patrick McGilligan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0569292/?ls) as a cunning manipulator of the media. His convoluted slew of partners and children are now somewhat factually acknowledged, but for the first three decades of his celebrity, his personal life was kept top secret, and several of his families were left out of the official narrative. The actor refuses to disclose his exact number of offspring even to this day. He had a longtime relationship with similarly abstruse co-star Locke (who died aged 74 in 2018, though for her entire public life she masqueraded about being younger), and has fathered at least eight children by at least six different women in an unending string of liaisons, many of which overlapped. He has been married only twice, however, with a mere three of his progeny coming from those unions.  
  
His known children are: [Laurie Murray](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm15158933/?ls) (b. 1954), whose mother is unidentified; [Kimber Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0247761/?ls) (b. 1964) with stuntwoman [Roxanne Tunis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0876651/?ls); [Kyle Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0247762/?ls) (b. 1968) and [Alison Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002055/?ls) (b. 1972) with his first ex-wife, [Margaret Neville Johnson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1527881/?ls); [Scott Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2207222/?ls) (b. 1986) and [Kathryn Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1828228/?ls) (b. 1988) with stewardess Jacelyn Reeves; [Francesca Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0247754/?ls) (b. 1993) with actress [Frances Fisher](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0004920/?ls); and [Morgan Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1765859/?ls) (b. 1996) with his second ex-wife, [Dina Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0247753/?ls). The entire time that he lived with Locke she was legally married to sculptor [Gordon Anderson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0026770/?ls).  
  
Eastwood has real estate holdings in Bel-Air, La Quinta, Carmel-by-the-Sea, Cassel (in remote northern California), Idaho's Sun Valley and Kihei, Hawaii.

 #### [5. Max von Sydow](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001884/?ref_=ls_t_5) 

    *   Actor
    *   Legal
    *   Director

[Flash Gordon (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080745/?ref_=ls_knf_5)

Max von Sydow was born Carl Adolf von Sydow on April 10, 1929 in Lund, Skåne, Sweden, to a middle-class family. He was the son of Baroness Maria Margareta (Rappe), a teacher, and Carl Wilhelm von Sydow, an ethnologist and folklore professor. His surname traces back to his partial German ancestry.  
  
When he was in high school, he and a few fellow students, including [Yvonne Lombard](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0518337/?ls), started a theatre club which encouraged his interest in acting. After conscription, he began to study at the Royal Dramatic Theatre's acting school (1948-1951), together with [Lars Ekborg](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0252299/?ls), [Margaretha Krook](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0472234/?ls) and [Ingrid Thulin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0862026/?ls). His first role was as Nils the crofter in [Alf Sjöberg](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0803549/?ls)'s [Only a Mother (1949)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0041155/?ls). After graduation, he worked at the city theatres in Norrköping and Malmö.  
  
His work in the movies by [Ingmar Bergman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000005/?ls) (especially [The Seventh Seal (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050976/?ls), including the iconic scenes in which he plays chess with Death) made him well-known internationally, and he started to get offers from abroad. His career abroad began with him playing Jesus in [The Greatest Story Ever Told (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059245/?ls); [Hawaii (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0060491/?ls) and [The Quiller Memorandum (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0060880/?ls). Since then, his career includes very different kind of characters, like Karl Oskar Nilsson in [The Emigrants (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067919/?ls); Father Lankester Merrin in [The Exorcist (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0070047/?ls); Joubert the assassin in [Three Days of the Condor (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0073802/?ls), Emperor Ming in [Flash Gordon (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080745/?ls); the villain Ernst Stavro Blofeld in the [Never Say Never Again (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0086006/?ls); Liet-Kynes in [Dune (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0087182/?ls) the artist Frederick in [Hannah and Her Sisters (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0091167/?ls); Lassefar in [Pelle the Conqueror (1987)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0093713/?ls), for which he received his first Academy Award nomination; Dr. Peter Ingham in [Awakenings (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0099077/?ls); Lamar Burgess in [Minority Report (2002)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0181689/?ls) and The Renter in [Extremely Loud & Incredibly Close (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0477302/?ls), which earned him his second Academy Award nomination.  
  
He became one of Sweden's most admired and professional actors, and is the only male Swedish actor to receive an Oscar nomination. He was nominated twice: for [Pelle the Conqueror (1987)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0093713/?ls) in 1988 and for [Extremely Loud & Incredibly Close (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0477302/?ls) in 2012. He received the Guldbagge Award for Best Director in his directing debut, the drama film [Ved vejen (1988)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0096368/?ls). In 2016, he joined the sixth season of the HBO series [Game of Thrones (2011)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0944947/?ls) as the Three-eyed Raven, which earned him his Primetime Emmy Award nomination.  
  
Max von Sydow died on March 8, 2020, in Provence, France, and was survived by his wife Catherine Brelet and four children. He was 90.

![Image 8: Gregory Peck](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BYWU1YTkwOGEtZTdjOC00ZDEyLThkZWUtMzY4ZjYzYWQyM2FlXkEyXkFqcGc@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg) [](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000060/?ref_=ls_i_6)  

 #### [6. Gregory Peck](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000060/?ref_=ls_t_6) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Additional Crew

[To Kill a Mockingbird (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056592/?ref_=ls_knf_6)

Eldred Gregory Peck was born on April 5, 1916 in La Jolla, California, to Bernice Mae (Ayres) and Gregory Pearl Peck, a chemist and druggist in San Diego. He had Irish (from his paternal grandmother), English, and some German, ancestry. His parents divorced when he was five years old. An only child, he was sent to live with his grandmother. He never felt he had a stable childhood. His fondest memories are of his grandmother taking him to the movies every week and of his dog, which followed him everywhere. He studied pre-med at UC-Berkeley and, while there, got bitten by the acting bug and decided to change the focus of his studies. He enrolled in the Neighborhood Playhouse in New York and debuted on Broadway after graduation. His debut was in [Emlyn Williams](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0930539/?ls)' play "The Morning Star" (1942). By 1943, he was in Hollywood, where he debuted in the RKO film [Days of Glory (1944)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0036748/?ls).  
  
Stardom came with his next film, [The Keys of the Kingdom (1944)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0036983/?ls), for which he was nominated for an Academy Award. Peck's screen presence displayed the qualities for which he became well known. He was tall, rugged and heroic, with a basic decency that transcended his roles. He appeared in [Alfred Hitchcock](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000033/?ls)'s [Spellbound (1945)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0038109/?ls) as an amnesia victim accused of murder. In [The Yearling (1946)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0039111/?ls), he was again nominated for an Academy Award and won the Golden Globe. He was especially effective in westerns and appeared in such varied fare as [David O. Selznick](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006388/?ls)'s critically blasted [Duel in the Sun (1946)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0038499/?ls), the somewhat better received [Yellow Sky (1948)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0040978/?ls) and the acclaimed [The Gunfighter (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0042531/?ls). He was nominated again for the Academy Award for his roles in [Gentleman's Agreement (1947)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0039416/?ls), which dealt with anti-Semitism, and [Twelve O'Clock High (1949)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0041996/?ls), a story of high-level stress in an Air Force bomber unit in World War II.  
  
With a string of hits to his credit, Peck made the decision to only work in films that interested him. He continued to appear as the heroic, larger-than-life figures in such films as [Captain Horatio Hornblower (1951)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0043379/?ls) and [Moby Dick (1956)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0049513/?ls). He worked with [Audrey Hepburn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000030/?ls) in her debut film, [Roman Holiday (1953)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0046250/?ls). Peck finally won the Oscar, after four nominations, for his performance as lawyer Atticus Finch in [To Kill a Mockingbird (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056592/?ls). In the early 1960s, he appeared in two darker films than he usually made, [Cape Fear (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0055824/?ls) and [Captain Newman, M.D. (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056903/?ls), which dealt with the way people live. He also gave a powerful performance as Captain Keith Mallory in [The Guns of Navarone (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054953/?ls), one of the biggest box-office hits of that year.  
  
In the early 1970s, he produced two films, [The Trial of the Catonsville Nine (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0069406/?ls) and [The Dove (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0071438/?ls), when his film career stalled. He made a comeback playing, somewhat woodenly, Robert Thorn in the horror film [The Omen (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0075005/?ls). After that, he returned to the bigger-than-life roles he was best known for, such as [MacArthur (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0076342/?ls) and the monstrous Nazi Dr. Josef Mengele in the huge hit [The Boys from Brazil (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0077269/?ls). In the 1980s, he moved into television with the miniseries [The Blue and the Gray (1982)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0083387/?ls) and [The Scarlet and the Black (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0086251/?ls). In 1991, he appeared in the remake of his 1962 film, playing a different role, in [Martin Scorsese](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000217/?ls)'s [Cape Fear (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0101540/?ls). He was also cast as the progressive-thinking owner of a wire and cable business in [Other People's Money (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0102609/?ls).  
  
In 1967, Peck received the Academy's [Jean Hersholt](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0380965/?ls) Humanitarian Award. He was also been awarded the US Presidential Medal of Freedom. Always politically progressive, he was active in such causes as anti-war protests, workers' rights and civil rights. In 2003, his Peck's portrayal of Atticus Finch was named the greatest film hero of the past 100 years by the American Film Institute. Gregory Peck died at age 87 on June 12, 2003 in Los Angeles, California.
