![Image 9: John Wayne in El Dorado (1966)](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BZTQ5NjBjNzUtNmU3My00ZWViLTk5MDYtM2YzM2MxYzk3MDU0XkEyXkFqcGc@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg) [](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000078/?ref_=ls_i_7)  

 #### [7. John Wayne](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000078/?ref_=ls_t_7) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Property Department

[True Grit (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065126/?ref_=ls_knf_7)

John Wayne was born Marion Robert Morrison in Iowa, to Mary Alberta (Brown) and Clyde Leonard Morrison, a pharmacist. He was of English, Scottish, Ulster-Scots, and Irish ancestry.  
  
Clyde developed a lung condition that required him to move his family from Iowa to the warmer climate of southern California, where they tried ranching in the Mojave Desert. Until the ranch failed, Marion and his younger brother [Robert E. Morrison](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0607300/?ls) swam in an irrigation ditch and rode a horse to school. When the ranch failed, the family moved to Glendale, California, where Marion delivered medicines for his father, sold newspapers and had an Airedale dog named "Duke" (the source of his own nickname). He did well at school both academically and in football. When he narrowly failed admission to Annapolis he went to USC on a football scholarship 1925-7. [Tom Mix](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0594291/?ls) got him a summer job as a prop man in exchange for football tickets. On the set he became close friends with director [John Ford](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000406/?ls) for whom, among others, he began doing bit parts, some billed as [John Wayne](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000078/?ls). His first featured film was [Men Without Women (1930)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0021140/?ls). After more than 70 low-budget westerns and adventures, mostly routine, Wayne's career was stuck in a rut until Ford cast him in [Stagecoach (1939)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0031971/?ls), the movie that made him a star. He appeared in nearly 250 movies, many of epic proportions. From 1942-43 he was in a radio series, "The Three Sheets to the Wind", and in 1944 he helped found the Motion Picture Alliance for the Preservation of American Ideals, a Conservative political organization, later becoming its President. His conservative political stance was also reflected in [The Alamo (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0053580/?ls), which he produced, directed and starred in. His patriotic stand was enshrined in [The Green Berets (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0063035/?ls) which he co-directed and starred in. Over the years Wayne was beset with health problems. In September 1964 he had a cancerous left lung removed; in 1977 when Star Wars: Episode IV - A New Hope was being made, John Waynes archive voice was used for the character Garindan ezz Zavor, later in March 1978 there was heart valve replacement surgery; and in January 1979 his stomach was removed. He received the Best Actor nomination for [Sands of Iwo Jima (1949)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0041841/?ls) and finally got the Oscar for his role as one-eyed Rooster Cogburn in [True Grit (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065126/?ls). A Congressional Gold Medal was struck in his honor in 1979. He is perhaps best remembered for his parts in Ford's cavalry trilogy - [Fort Apache (1948)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0040369/?ls), [She Wore a Yellow Ribbon (1949)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0041866/?ls) and [Rio Grande (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0042895/?ls).

 #### [8. Sean Connery](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000125/?ref_=ls_t_8) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Director

[Dr. No (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0055928/?ref_=ls_knf_8)

The tall, handsome and muscular Scottish actor Sean Connery is best known as the original actor to portray James Bond in the hugely successful movie franchise, starring in seven films between 1962 and 1983. Some believed that such a career-defining role might leave him unable to escape it, but he proved the doubters wrong, becoming one of the most notable film actors of his generation, with a host of great movies to his name. This arguably culminated in his greatest acclaim in 1988, when Connery won the Academy Award for Best Supporting Actor for his role as an Irish cop in [The Untouchables (1987)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0094226/?ls), stealing the thunder from the movie's principal star [Kevin Costner](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000126/?ls). Connery was polled as "The Greatest Living Scot" and "Scotland's Greatest Living National Treasure." In 1989, he was proclaimed "Sexiest Man Alive" by People magazine, and in 1999, at age 69, he was proclaimed "Sexiest Man of the Century."  
  
Thomas "Sean" Connery was born on August 25, 1930 in Fountainbridge, Edinburgh. His mother, Euphemia Maclean, was a cleaning lady, and his father, Joseph Connery, was a factory worker and truck driver. He also had a brother, [Neil Connery](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0175227/?ls), a plasterer in Edinburgh, who was eight years younger. Before going into acting, Sean had many different jobs, such as a milkman, lorry driver, a laborer, artist's model for the Edinburgh College of Art, coffin polisher and bodybuilder. He also joined the Royal Navy, but was later discharged because of medical problems. At the age of 23, he had a choice between becoming a professional soccer player or an actor, and even though he showed much promise in the sport, he chose acting and said it was one of his more intelligent decisions.  
  
[No Road Back (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050772/?ls) was Sean's first major movie role, and it was followed by several made-for-TV movies such as [Anna Christie (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0313207/?ls), [Macbeth (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0400618/?ls) and [Anna Karenina (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0267267/?ls) as well as guest appearances on TV series, and also films such as [Hell Drivers (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051713/?ls), [Another Time, Another Place (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051364/?ls), [Darby O'Gill and the Little People (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0052722/?ls) and [The Frightened City (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054898/?ls). In 1962 he appeared in [The Longest Day (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056197/?ls) with a host of other stars.  
  
His big breakthrough came in 1962 when he landed the role of secret agent James Bond in [Dr. No (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0055928/?ls). He played James Bond in six more films: [From Russia with Love (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057076/?ls), [Goldfinger (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0058150/?ls), [Thunderball (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059800/?ls), [You Only Live Twice (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0062512/?ls), [Diamonds Are Forever (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0066995/?ls) and [Never Say Never Again (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0086006/?ls).  
  
After and during the success of the Bond films, he maintained a successful career as an actor and has appeared in films, including [Alfred Hitchcock](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000033/?ls)'s [Marnie (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0058329/?ls), [The Hill (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059274/?ls), [Murder on the Orient Express (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0071877/?ls), [The Man Who Would Be King (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0073341/?ls), [The Wind and the Lion (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0073906/?ls), [Time Bandits (1981)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0081633/?ls), [Highlander (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0091203/?ls), [The Name of the Rose (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0091605/?ls), [Indiana Jones and the Last Crusade (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097576/?ls), [The Hunt for Red October (1990)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0099810/?ls), [Rising Sun (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0107969/?ls), [The Rock (1996)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0117500/?ls), [Finding Forrester (2000)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0181536/?ls) and [The League of Extraordinary Gentlemen (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0311429/?ls).  
  
Sean married actress [Diane Cilento](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0162283/?ls) in 1962 and they had Sean's only child, [Jason Connery](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001064/?ls), born on January 11, 1963. The couple announced their separation in February 1971 and filed for divorce 2½ years later. Sean then dated [Jill St. John](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001762/?ls), [Lana Wood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0939836/?ls), [Magda Konopka](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0465260/?ls) and [Carole Mallory](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0540098/?ls). In 1975 he married [Micheline Roquebrune](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1315689/?ls) and they stayed married, despite Sean's well-documented love affair with [Lynsey de Paul](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0210880/?ls) in the late '80s. Sean had three stepchildren through his marriage to Micheline, who was one year his senior. He is also a grandfather. His son, Jason and Jason's ex-wife, actress [Mia Sara](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000214/?ls) had a son, [Dashiell Connery](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2330321/?ls), in 1997.  
  
Sean Connery died at the age of 90 on October 31, 2020, in Nassau, the Bahamas, where he resided for many years.

 #### [9. Peter O'Toole](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000564/?ref_=ls_t_9) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Soundtrack

[Lawrence of Arabia (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056172/?ref_=ls_knf_9)

A leading man of prodigious talents, [Peter O'Toole](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000564/?ls) was born and raised in Leeds, Yorkshire, England, the son of Constance Jane Eliot (Ferguson), a Scottish nurse, and Patrick Joseph O'Toole, an Irish metal plater, football player and racecourse bookmaker. Upon leaving school, he decided to become a journalist, beginning as a newspaper copy boy. Although he succeeded in becoming a reporter, he discovered the theater and made his stage debut at age 17. He served as a radioman in the Royal Navy for two years, then attended the Royal Academy of Dramatic Arts, where his classmates included [Albert Finney](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001215/?ls), [Alan Bates](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000869/?ls) and [Richard Harris](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001321/?ls).  
  
O'Toole spent several years on-stage at the Bristol Old Vic, then made an inconspicuous film debut in the Disney classic [Kidnapped (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0053994/?ls). In 1962, he was chosen by [David Lean](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000180/?ls) to play [T.E. Lawrence](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0493042/?ls) in Lean's epic drama [Lawrence of Arabia (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056172/?ls). The role made O'Toole an international superstar and received him his first Academy Award nomination for Best Actor in a Leading Role. In 1963, he played Hamlet under [Laurence Olivier](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000059/?ls)'s direction in the premiere production of the Royal National Theater. He continued successfully in artistically rich films as well as less artistic but commercially rewarding projects. He received Academy Award nominations (but no Oscar) for seven different films.  
  
However, medical problems (originally thought to have been brought on by his drinking but which turned out to be stomach cancer) threatened to destroy his career and life in the 1970s. He survived by giving up alcohol and, after serious medical treatment, returned to films with triumphant performances in [The Stunt Man (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0081568/?ls) and [My Favorite Year (1982)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0084370/?ls). His youthful beauty lost to time and drink, O'Toole has found meaningful roles increasingly difficult to come by, though he remained one of the greatest actors of his generation. He had two daughters, Pat and [Kate O'Toole](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002347/?ls), from his marriage to actress [Siân Phillips](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0680795/?ls). He also had a son, [Lorcan O'Toole](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1574372/?ls), by model Karen Brown.  
  
On December 14, 2013, Peter O'Toole died at age 81 in London, England.

![Image 12: Charles Bronson](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BYWVjNDExMTgtMGE2OS00ZWNiLWIwNjYtMmI1ZDYwMTg1OWE2XkEyXkFqcGc@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg) [](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000314/?ref_=ls_i_10)  

 #### [10. Charles Bronson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000314/?ref_=ls_t_10) 

    *   Actor

[Death Wish (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0071402/?ref_=ls_knf_10)

The archetypal screen tough guy with weatherbeaten features--one film critic described his rugged looks as "a [Clark Gable](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000022/?ls) who had been left out in the sun too long"--Charles Bronson was born Charles Buchinsky, one of 15 children of struggling parents in Pennsylvania. His mother, Mary (Valinsky), was born in Pennsylvania, to Lithuanian parents, and his father, Walter Buchinsky, was a Lithuanian immigrant coal miner.  
  
He completed high school and joined his father in the mines (an experience that resulted in a lifetime fear of being in enclosed spaces) and then served in WW II. After his return from the war, Bronson used the GI Bill to study art (a passion he had for the rest of his life), then enrolled at the Pasadena Playhouse in California. One of his teachers was impressed with the young man and recommended him to director [Henry Hathaway](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0368871/?ls), resulting in Bronson making his film debut in [You're in the Navy Now (1951)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0044224/?ls).  
  
He appeared on screen often early in his career, though usually uncredited. However, he made an impact on audiences as the evil assistant to [Vincent Price](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001637/?ls) in the 3-D thriller [House of Wax (1953)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0045888/?ls). His sinewy yet muscular physique got him cast in action-type roles, often without a shirt to highlight his manly frame. He received positive notices from critics for his performances in [Vera Cruz (1954)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0047647/?ls), [Target Zero (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048698/?ls) and [Run of the Arrow (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050915/?ls). Indie director [Roger Corman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000339/?ls) cast him as the lead in his well-received low-budget gangster flick [Machine-Gun Kelly (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051887/?ls), then Bronson scored the lead in his own TV series, [Man with a Camera (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051293/?ls). The 1960s proved to be the era in which Bronson made his reputation as a man of few words but much action.  
  
Director [John Sturges](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0836328/?ls) cast him as half Irish/half Mexican gunslinger Bernardo O'Reilly in the smash hit western [The Magnificent Seven (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054047/?ls), and hired him again as tunnel rat Danny Velinski for the WWII POW big-budget epic [The Great Escape (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057115/?ls). Several more strong roles followed, then once again he was back in military uniform, alongside [Lee Marvin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001511/?ls) and [Ernest Borgnine](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000308/?ls) in the testosterone-filled [The Dirty Dozen (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061578/?ls).  
  
European audiences had taken a shine to his minimalist acting style, and he headed to the Continent to star in several action-oriented films, including [Guns for San Sebastian (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0062713/?ls) (aka "Guns for San Sebastian"), the cult western [Once Upon a Time in the West (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064116/?ls) (aka "Once Upon a Time in The West"), [Rider on the Rain (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064791/?ls) (aka "Rider On The Rain") and, in one of the quirkier examples of international casting, alongside Japansese screen legend [Toshirō Mifune](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001536/?ls) in the western [Red Sun (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067770/?ls) (aka "Red Sun").  
  
American audiences were by now keen to see Bronson back on US soil, and he returned triumphantly in the early 1970s to take the lead in more hard-edged crime and western dramas, including [The Valachi Papers (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068341/?ls) and the revenge western [Chato's Land (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0066907/?ls). After nearly 25 years as a working actor, he became an 'overnight" sensation. Bronson then hooked up with British director [Michael Winner](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0935382/?ls) to star in several highly successful urban crime thrillers, including [The Mechanic (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068931/?ls) and [The Stone Killer (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0070736/?ls). He then scored a solid hit as a Colorado melon farmer-done-wrong in [Richard Fleischer](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0281507/?ls)'s [Mr. Majestyk (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0071866/?ls). However, the film that proved to be a breakthrough for both Bronson and Winner came in 1974 with the release of the controversial [Death Wish (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0071402/?ls) (written with [Henry Fonda](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000020/?ls) in mind, who turned it down because he was disgusted by the script).  
  
The US was at the time in the midst of rising street crime, and audiences flocked to see a story about a mild-mannered architect who seeks revenge for the murder of his wife and rape of his daughter by gunning down hoods, rapists and killers on the streets of New York City. So popular was the film that it spawned four sequels over the next 20 years.  
  
Action fans could not get enough of tough guy Bronson, and he appeared in what many fans--and critics--consider his best role: Depression-era street fighter Chaney alongside [James Coburn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000336/?ls) in [Hard Times (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0073092/?ls). That was followed by the somewhat slow-paced western [Breakheart Pass (1975)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0072735/?ls) (with wife [Jill Ireland](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0409866/?ls)), the light-hearted romp (a flop) [From Noon Till Three (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0074553/?ls) and as Soviet agent Grigori Borsov in director [Don Siegel](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0796923/?ls)'s Cold War thriller [Telefon (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0076804/?ls).  
  
Bronson remained busy throughout the 1980s, with most of his films taking a more violent tone, and he was pitched as an avenging angel eradicating evildoers in films like the [10 to Midnight (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0085121/?ls), [The Evil That Men Do (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0087222/?ls), [Assassination (1987)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0092585/?ls) and [Kinjite: Forbidden Subjects (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097670/?ls). Bronson jolted many critics with his forceful work as murdered United Mine Workers leader Jock Yablonski in the TV movie [Act of Vengeance (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0090588/?ls), gave a very interesting performance in the [Sean Penn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000576/?ls)-directed [The Indian Runner (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0102116/?ls) and surprised everyone with his appearance as compassionate newspaper editor Francis Church in the family film [Yes Virginia, There Is a Santa Claus (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0103305/?ls).  
  
Bronson's final film roles were as police commissioner Paul Fein in a well-received trio of crime/drama TV movies [Family of Cops (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0113024/?ls), [Breach of Faith: A Family of Cops II (1997)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0118770/?ls) and [Family of Cops III: Under Suspicion (1999)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0184456/?ls). Unfortunately, ill health began to take its toll; he suffered from Alzheimer's disease for the last few years of his life, and finally passed away from pneumonia at Los Angeles' Cedars-Sinai Medical Center in August 2003.  
  
Bronson was a true icon of international cinema; critics had few good things to say about his films, but he remained a fan favorite in both the US and abroad for 50 years, a claim few other film legends can make.

 #### [11. Rex Harrison](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001322/?ref_=ls_t_11) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Soundtrack

[My Fair Lady (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0058385/?ref_=ls_knf_11)

Rex Harrison was born Reginald Carey Harrison in Huyton, Lancashire, England, to Edith Mary (Carey) and William Reginald Harrison, a cotton broker. He changed his name to Rex as a young boy, knowing it was the Latin word for "King". Starting out on his theater career at age 18, his first job at the Liverpool Rep Theatre was nearly his last - dashing across the stage to say his one line, made his entrance and promptly blew it. Fates were kind, however, and soon he began landing roles in the West End. "French Without Tears", a play by [Terence Rattigan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0711905/?ls), proved to be his breakthrough role. Soon he was being called the "greatest actor of light comedy in the world". Having divorced his first wife Collette Thomas in 1942, he married German actress [Lilli Palmer](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0658339/?ls). The two began appearing together in many plays and British films. He attained international fame when he portrayed the King in [Anna and the King of Siam (1946)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0038303/?ls), his first American film. After a sex scandal, in which actress [Carole Landis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0484808/?ls) apparently committed suicide because he ended their affair, the relationship with wife Lilli became strained. Rex (by this time known as "Sexy Rexy" for his philandering ways and magnetic charm) began a relationship with British actress [Kay Kendall](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0447608/?ls) and divorced Lilli to marry the terminally ill Kay with hopes of a re-marriage to Palmer upon Kay's death. The death of Kay affected Harrison greatly and Lilli never returned to him. During this time Rex was offered the defining role of his career: Professor Henry Higgins in the original production of "My Fair Lady". He won the Tony for the play and an Oscar for the film version. In 1962 Harrison married actress [Rachel Roberts](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0731499/?ls). This union and the one following it to Elizabeth Harris (Richard's ex) also ended in divorce. In 1978 Rex met and married Mercia Tinker. He and Mercia remained happily married until his death in 1990. She was also with him in 1989 when he was granted his much-deserved and long awaited knighthood at Buckingham Palace. Rex Harrison died of pancreatic cancer three weeks after his last stage appearance, as Lord Porteous in [W. Somerset Maugham](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0560857/?ls)'s "The Circle".

![Image 14: Paul Newman in Bicentennial Minutes (1974)](https://m.media-amazon.com/images/M/MV5BMzBmYzE4NmItODdjZS00Mjk2LWEzNjctNTJkZGNlMWY1M2I5XkEyXkFqcGc@._V1_QL75_UX60_CR0,0,60,60_.jpg) [](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000056/?ref_=ls_i_12)  

 #### [12. Paul Newman](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000056/?ref_=ls_t_12) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Director

[The Hustler (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054997/?ref_=ls_knf_12)

Screen legend, superstar, and the man with the most famous blue eyes in movie history, Paul Leonard Newman was born on January 26, 1925, in Cleveland Heights, Ohio, the second son of Arthur Sigmund Newman (died 1950) and Theresa Fetsko (died 1982). His elder brother was [Arthur S. Newman Jr.](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0627983/?ls), named for their father, a Jewish businessman who owned a successful sporting goods store and was the son of emigrants from Poland and Hungary. Newman's mother (born Terézia Fecková, daughter of Stefan Fecko and Mária Polenak) was a Roman Catholic Slovak from Homonna, Pticie (former Austro-Hungarian Empire), who became a practicing Christian Scientist. She and her brother, Newman's uncle Joe, had an interest in the creative arts, and it rubbed off on him. He acted in grade school and high school plays. The Newmans were well-to-do and Paul Newman grew up in affluent Shaker Heights. Before he became an actor, Newman ran the family sporting goods store in Cleveland, Ohio.  
  
By 1950, the 25-year-old Newman had been kicked out of Ohio University, where he belonged to the Phi Kappa Tau fraternity, for unruly behavior (denting the college president's car with a beer keg), served three years in the United States Navy during World War II as a radio operator, graduated from Ohio's Kenyon College, married his first wife, Jacqueline "Jackie" Witte (born 1929), and had his first child, Scott. That same year, his father died. When he became successful in later years, Newman said if he had any regrets it would be that his father was not around to witness his success. He brought Jackie back to Shaker Heights and he ran his father's store for a short period. Then, knowing that wasn't the career path he wanted to take, he moved Jackie and Scott to New Haven, Connecticut, where he attended Yale University's School of Drama.  
  
While doing a play there, Newman was spotted by two agents, who invited him to come to New York City to pursue a career as a professional actor. After moving to New York, he acted in guest spots for various television series and in 1953 came a big break. He got the part of understudy of the lead role in the successful Broadway play "Picnic". Through this play, he met actress Joanne Woodward (born 1930), who was also an understudy in the play. While they got on very well and there was a strong attraction, Newman was married and his second child, Susan, was born that year. During this time, Newman was accepted into the much admired and popular New York Actors Studio, although he did not actually audition.  
  
In 1954, a film Newman was very reluctant to do was released, [The Silver Chalice (1954)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0047494/?ls). He considered his performance in this costume epic to be so bad that he took out a full-page ad in a trade paper apologizing for it to anyone who might have seen it. He had always been embarrassed about the film and reveled in making fun of it. He immediately wanted to return to the stage, and performed in "The Desperate Hours". In 1956, he got the chance to redeem himself in the film world by portraying boxer [Rocky Graziano](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0337200/?ls) in [Somebody Up There Likes Me (1956)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0049778/?ls), and critics praised his performance. In 1957, with a handful of films to his credit, he was cast in [The Long, Hot Summer (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051878/?ls), co-starring [Joanne Woodward](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0940946/?ls).  
  
During the shooting of this film, they realized they were meant to be together and by now, so did his then-wife Jackie, who gave Newman a divorce. He and Woodward wed in Las Vegas in January 1958. They went on to have three daughters together and raised them in Westport, Connecticut. In 1959, Newman received his first Academy Award nomination for Best Actor, in [Cat on a Hot Tin Roof (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051459/?ls). The 1960s would bring Newman into superstar status, as he became one of the most popular actors of the decade, and garnered three more Best Actor Oscar nominations, for [The Hustler (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054997/?ls), [Hud (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057163/?ls) and [Cool Hand Luke (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061512/?ls). In 1968, his debut directorial effort [Rachel, Rachel (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0063483/?ls) was given good marks, and although the film and Woodward were nominated for Oscars, Newman was not nominated for Best Director. However, he did win a Golden Globe Award for his direction.  
  
1969 brought the popular screen duo of Newman and [Robert Redford](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000602/?ls) together for the first time when [Butch Cassidy and the Sundance Kid (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064115/?ls) was released. It was a box office smash. Through the 1970s, Newman had hits and misses from such popular films as [The Sting (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0070735/?ls) and [The Towering Inferno (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0072308/?ls) to lesser known films as [The Life and Times of Judge Roy Bean (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068853/?ls) to a cult classic [Slap Shot (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0076723/?ls). After the death of his only son, Scott, in 1978, Newman's personal life and film choices moved in a different direction. His acting work in the 1980s and on is what is often most praised by critics today. He became more at ease with himself and it was evident in [The Verdict (1982)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0084855/?ls) for which he received his sixth Best Actor Oscar nomination and, in 1987, finally received his first Oscar for [The Color of Money (1986)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0090863/?ls), almost thirty years after Woodward had won hers. Friend and director of [Somebody Up There Likes Me (1956)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0049778/?ls), [Robert Wise](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0936404/?ls) accepted the award on Newman's behalf as the actor did not attend the ceremony.  
  
Paul used his fame for good. He was dedicated to civil rights-attending the March on Washington in August 1963-women’s rights, and gay rights. He used his platform to advocate for equal pay for his female co-stars and was a vocal political advocate committed to ending the nuclear arms race and determined to elect opponents of war and militarism.  
  
A passionate race car driver since the early 1970s (despite being color-blind), he was co-founder of Newman-Haas racing in 1982. He was as well known for his philanthropic ways and highly successful business ventures as he was for his legendary actor status. Newman also founded "Newman's Own", a successful line of food products that gives away all the profits to good causes. Since 1982, Paul and Newman’s Own Foundation have given away over $600M to good causes. He also founded The Hole in the Wall Gang Camp in Ashford, Connecticut, now part of SeriousFun Children's Network, which create medically inclusive camp experiences for children with serious illness.  
  
Newman's marriage to Woodward lasted a half-century. Connecticut was their primary residence after leaving Hollywood and moving East in 1960. Renowned for his sense of humor, in 1998 he quipped that he was a little embarrassed to see his salad dressing grossing more than his movies. During his later years, he still attended races, was much involved in his charitable organizations, and in 2006, he opened a restaurant adjacent to the Westport Country Playhouse (since closed.) Paul established Newman’s Own Foundation in 2005 to ensure the continuation of his philanthropic legacy. His first of its kind food company and its innovative "100% for Purpose" business model are still going strong. In 2007, while the public was largely unaware of the serious illness from which he was suffering, Newman made some headlines when he said he was losing his invention and confidence in his acting abilities and that acting was "pretty much a closed book for me". A smoker for many years, Newman died on September 26, 2008, aged 83, from lung cancer.

 #### [13. Alain Delon](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001128/?ref_=ls_t_13) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Writer

[The Leopard (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057091/?ref_=ls_knf_13)

Alain Fabien Maurice Marcel Delon was born in Sceaux, Hauts-de-Seine, France, to Édith (Arnold) and Fabien Delon. His father was of French and Corsican Italian descent, and his mother was of French and German ancestry. His parents divorced early on, and Delon had a stormy childhood, being frequently expelled from school.  
  
In 1953/1954 he served with the French Marines in Indochina. In the mid-'50s he worked at various odd jobs including waiter, salesman and porter in Les Halles market. He decided to try an acting career and in 1957 made his film debut in [Yves Allégret](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001905/?ls)'s [Send a Woman When the Devil Fails (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050871/?ls). He declined an offer of a contract from producer [David O. Selznick](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006388/?ls), and in 1960 he received international recognition for his role in [Luchino Visconti](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0899581/?ls)'s [Rocco and His Brothers (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054248/?ls). In 1961 he appeared on the stage in "'Tis a Pity She's a Whore", directed by Visconti, in Paris. In 1964 he formed his own production company, Delbeau Productions, and he produced a short film directed by [Guy Gilles](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0318875/?ls). In 1968 he found himself involved in murder, drug and sex scandal that indirectly implicated major politicians and show-business personalities, but he was eventually cleared of all charges. In the late 1960s he formed another company. Adel Film, and the next year he began producing features. In 1981 he directed his first film, [To Kill a Cop (1981)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0082935/?ls).  
  
Delon was a sensation early in his career; he came to embody the young, energetic, often morally corrupted man. With his breathtaking good looks he was also destined to play tender lovers and romantic heroes, and he was a French embodiment of the type created in America by [James Dean](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000015/?ls). His first outstanding success came with the role of the parasite Tom Ripley in 'Rene Clement''s sun-drenched thriller [Purple Noon (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054189/?ls). Delon presented a psychological portrait of a murderous young cynic who attempts to take on the identity of his victim. A totally different role was offered to him by Visconti in [Rocco and His Brothers (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054248/?ls). In this film Delon plays the devoted Rocco, who accepts the greatest sacrifices to save his shiftless brother Simon.  
  
After several other films in Italy, Delon returned to the criminal genre with [Jean Gabin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0300064/?ls) in [Any Number Can Win (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057344/?ls). This work, a classic example of the genre, was distinguished not only by a soundly worked-out screenplay, but also by the careful production and the excellent performances of both Delon and Gabin. It was only in the late 1960s that the sleek and lethal Delon came to epitomize the calm, psychopathic hoodlum, staring into the camera like a cat assessing a mouse. His tough, ruthless side was first used to real effect by [Jean-Pierre Melville](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0578483/?ls) in [Le Samouraï (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0062229/?ls). In 1970 he had a huge success in the bloodstained [Borsalino (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065486/?ls)--which he also produced--playing a small-time gangster in the 1930s who, with [Jean-Paul Belmondo](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000901/?ls), becomes king of the Marseilles underworld. Delon later won critical acclaim for his roles, against type, in [Joseph Losey](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0521334/?ls)'s [Mr. Klein (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0074916/?ls) in which he played (brilliantly) the icily sinister title role, and the art-movie [Swann in Love (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0088315/?ls). He has an older son [Anthony Delon](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0217670/?ls) (who has also acted in a number of movies) from his first marriage to [Nathalie Delon](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0217677/?ls), and has a young son and daughter, Alain-Fabien and Anouchka with Rosalie.

 #### [15. Walter Matthau](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000527/?ref_=ls_t_15)

[The Odd Couple (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0063374/?ref_=ls_knf_15)

Walter Matthau was best known for starring in many films which included [Charade (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056923/?ls), [The Odd Couple (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0063374/?ls), [Grumpy Old Men (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0107050/?ls), and [Dennis the Menace (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0106701/?ls). He often worked with Jack Lemmon and the two were Hollywood's craziest stars.  
  
He was born Walter Jake Matthow in New York City, New York on October 1, 1920. His mother was an immigrant from Lithuania and his father was a Russian Jewish peddler and electrician from Kiev, Ukraine. As a young boy, Matthau attended a Jewish non-profit sleep-away camp. He also attended Surprise Lake Camp. His high school was Seward Park High School.  
  
During World War II, Matthau served in the U.S. Army Air Forces with the Eighth Air Force in Britain as a Consolidated B-24 Liberator radioman-gunner, in the same 453rd Bombardment Group as James Stewart. He was based at RAF Old Buckenham, Norfolk during this time. He reached the rank of staff sergeant and became interested in acting.  
  
Matthau appeared in the pilot of [Mister Peepers (1952)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0044279/?ls) alongside Wally Cox. He later appeared in the Elia Kazan classic, [A Face in the Crowd (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050371/?ls), opposite Patricia Neal and Andy Griffith, and then appeared in [Lonely Are the Brave (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056195/?ls), with Kirk Douglas, a film Douglas has often described as his personal favorite. Matthau then appeared in [Charade (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056923/?ls) with Audrey Hepburn and Cary Grant. In 1968, Matthau made his big screen appearance as Oscar Madison in [The Odd Couple (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0063374/?ls) alongside Jack Lemmon. The two were also in the sequel ([The Odd Couple II (1998)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0120773/?ls)) as well as [Grumpy Old Men (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0107050/?ls) and [Grumpier Old Men (1995)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0113228/?ls). Matthau was in [Dennis the Menace (1993)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0106701/?ls), alongside Mason Gamble. On July 1, 2000, Matthau died of a heart attack in Los Angeles, California. He was 79 years old.

 #### [16. Anthony Quinn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000063/?ref_=ls_t_16) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Director

[Zorba the Greek (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057831/?ref_=ls_knf_16)

Anthony Quinn was born Antonio Rodolfo Quinn Oaxaca (some sources indicate Manuel Antonio Rodolfo Quinn Oaxaca) on April 21, 1915, in Chihuahua, Mexico, to Manuela (Oaxaca) and Francisco Quinn, who became an assistant cameraman at a Los Angeles (CA) film studio.  
  
After starting life in extremely modest circumstances in Mexico, his family moved to Los Angeles, where he grew up in the Boyle Heights and Echo Park neighborhoods. He played in the band of evangelist [Aimee Semple McPherson](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm2492420/?ls) as a youth and as a deputy preacher. He attended Polytechnic High School and later Belmont High, but eventually dropped out. The young Quinn boxed (which stood him in good stead as a stage actor, when he played Stanley Kowalski in "A Streetcar Named Desire" to rave reviews in Chicago), then later studied architecture under [Frank Lloyd Wright](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0942394/?ls) at the great architect's studio, Taliesin, in Arizona. Quinn was close to Wright, who encouraged him when he decided to give acting a try. Made his credited film debut in [Parole! (1936)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0028087/?ls). After a brief apprenticeship on stage, Quinn hit Hollywood in 1936 and picked up a variety of small roles in several films at Paramount, including an Indian warrior in [The Plainsman (1936)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0028108/?ls), which was directed by the man who later became his father-in-law, [Cecil B. DeMille](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001124/?ls).  
  
As a contract player at Paramount, Quinn's roles were mainly ethnic types, such as an Arab chieftain in the [Bing Crosby](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001078/?ls)-[Bob Hope](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001362/?ls) comedy, [Road to Morocco (1942)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0035262/?ls). As a Mexican national, he was exempt from the draft. With many other actors in military service during WWII, he was able to move up into better supporting roles. He married DeMille's daughter [Katherine DeMille](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0218490/?ls), which afforded him entrance to the top circles of Hollywood society. He became disenchanted with his career and did not renew his Paramount contract despite the advice of others, including his father-in-law, with whom he did not get along (whom Quinn reportedly felt had never accepted him due to his Mexican roots; the two men were also on opposite ends of the political spectrum) but they eventually were able to develop a civil relationship. Quinn returned to the stage to hone his craft. His portrayal of Stanley Kowalski in "A Streetcar Named Desire" in Chicago and on Broadway (where he replaced the legendary [Marlon Brando](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000008/?ls), who is forever associated with the role) made his reputation and boosted his film career when he returned to the movies.  
  
Brando and [Elia Kazan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001415/?ls), who directed "Streetcar" on Broadway and on film ([A Streetcar Named Desire (1951)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0044081/?ls)), were crucial to Quinn's future success. Kazan, knowing the two were potential rivals due to their acclaimed portrayals of Kowalski, cast Quinn as Brando's brother in his biographical film of Mexican revolutionary [Emiliano Zapata](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0953176/?ls), [Viva Zapata! (1952)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0045296/?ls). Quinn won the Best Supporting Actor Academy Award for 1952, making him the first Mexican to win an Oscar. It was not to be his lone appearance in the winner's circle: he won his second Supporting Actor Oscar in 1957 for his portrayal of [Paul Gauguin](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1917169/?ls) in [Vincente Minnelli](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0591486/?ls)'s biographical film of [Vincent van Gogh](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0994883/?ls), [Lust for Life (1956)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0049456/?ls), opposite [Kirk Douglas](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000018/?ls). Over the next decade Quinn lived in Italy and became a major figure in world cinema, as many studios shot films in Italy to take advantage of the lower costs ("runaway production" had battered the industry since its beginnings in the New York/New Jersey area in the 1910s). He appeared in several Italian films, giving one of his greatest performances as the circus strongman who brutalizes the sweet soul played by [Giulietta Masina](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0556399/?ls) in her husband [Federico Fellini](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000019/?ls)'s masterpiece [La Strada (1954)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0047528/?ls). He met his second wife, Jolanda Addolori, a wardrobe assistant, while he was in Rome filming [Barabbas (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0055774/?ls).  
  
Alternating between Europe and Hollywood, Quinn built his reputation and entered the front rank of character actors and character leads. He received his third Oscar nomination (and first for Best Actor) for [George Cukor](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002030/?ls)'s [Wild Is the Wind (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051193/?ls). He played a Greek resistance fighter against the Nazi occupation in the monster hit [The Guns of Navarone (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054953/?ls) and received kudos for his portrayal of a once-great boxer on his way down in [Rod Serling](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0785245/?ls)'s [Requiem for a Heavyweight (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056406/?ls). He went back to playing ethnic roles, such as an Arab warlord in [David Lean](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000180/?ls)'s masterpiece [Lawrence of Arabia (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056172/?ls), and he played the eponymous lead in the "sword-and-sandal" blockbuster [Barabbas (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0055774/?ls). Two years later, he reached the zenith of his career, playing Zorba the Greek in the film of the same name (a.k.a. [Zorba the Greek (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057831/?ls)), which brought him his fourth, and last, Oscar nomination as Best Actor. The 1960s were kind to him: he played character leads in such major films as [The Shoes of the Fisherman (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0258962/?ls) and [The Secret of Santa Vittoria (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064952/?ls). However, his appearance in the title role in the film adaptation of [John Fowles](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0288826/?ls)' novel, [The Magus (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0063260/?ls), did nothing to save the film, which was one of that decade's notorious turkeys.  
  
In the 1960s, Quinn told Life magazine that he would fight against typecasting. Unfortunately, the following decade saw him slip back into playing ethnic types again, in such critical bombs as [The Greek Tycoon (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0077636/?ls). He starred as the Hispanic mayor of a southwestern city on the short-lived television series [The Man and the City (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0066683/?ls), but his career lost its momentum during the 1970s. Aside from playing a thinly disguised [Aristotle Onassis](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1238516/?ls) in the cinematic roman-a-clef [The Greek Tycoon (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0077636/?ls), his other major roles of the decade were as Hamza in the controversial [The Message (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0074896/?ls) (a.k.a. "Mohammad, Messenger of God"); as the Italian patriarch in [The Inheritance (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0074487/?ls); yet another Arab in [Caravans (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0077296/?ls); and as a Mexican patriarch in [The Children of Sanchez (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0077326/?ls). In 1983, he reprised his most famous role, Zorba the Greek, on Broadway in the revival of the musical "Zorba" for 362 performances (opposite [Lila Kedrova](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0444321/?ls), who had also appeared in the film, and won an Oscar for Best Supporting Actress for her performance). His career slowed during the 1990s but he continued to work steadily in films and television, including an appearance with frequent film co-star [Maureen O'Hara](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000058/?ls) in [Only the Lonely (1991)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0102598/?ls).  
  
Quinn lived out the latter years of his life in Bristol, Rhode Island, where he spent most of his time painting and sculpting. Beginning in 1982, he held numerous major exhibitions in cities such as Vienna, Paris, and Seoul. He died in a hospital in Boston at age 86 from pneumonia and respiratory failure linked to his battle with throat cancer.

Alec Guinness was an English actor of stage and screen, his career spanning over sixty years. His best known screen works are his starring roles in several of the Ealing comedies between 1949 and 1957 (most notably as eight members of the same family in [Kind Hearts and Coronets (1949)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0041546/?ls), his Oscar-nominated turn as bank clerk turned bullion robber in [The Lavender Hill Mob (1951)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0044829/?ls), an inventor who never gives up in [The Man in the White Suit (1951)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0044876/?ls), and as one of five oddball criminals planning a bank robbery in [The Ladykillers (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048281/?ls)); his six collaborations over 38 years with director [David Lean](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000180/?ls): Herbert Pocket in [Great Expectations (1946)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0038574/?ls), Fagin in [Oliver Twist (1948)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0040662/?ls), Col. Nicholson in [The Bridge on the River Kwai (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050212/?ls), (for which he won the Academy Award for Best Actor), Prince Faisal in [Lawrence of Arabia (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056172/?ls), General Yevgraf Zhivago in [Doctor Zhivago (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059113/?ls), and Professor Godbole in [A Passage to India (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0087892/?ls); his role as Obi-Wan Kenobi in [George Lucas](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000184/?ls)' original Star Wars trilogy (for which he received an Academy Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor); and his starring role as George Smiley in the television adaptations of [John le Carré](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0494170/?ls)'s [Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy (1979)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080297/?ls) and [Smiley's People (1982)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0083480/?ls).  
  
His gallery of notable characters (both fictional and historical) also includes Prime Minister Benjamin Disraeli in [The Mudlark (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0042757/?ls), an enterprising rogue in [The Promoter (1952)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0045056/?ls), a sleuthing priest in [The Detective (1954)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0046970/?ls), an eccentric London artist in [The Horse's Mouth (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051739/?ls) (for which he was Oscar-nominated as a screenwriter), a wayward Scottish army officer in [Tunes of Glory (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0054412/?ls), the ghost of Jacob Marley in [Scrooge (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0066344/?ls), King Charles I in [Cromwell (1970)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065593/?ls), the title role in [Hitler: The Last Ten Days (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0070184/?ls), a blind butler in [Murder by Death (1976)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0074937/?ls), a survivor of the Titanic disaster in [Raise the Titanic (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0081400/?ls), and a return to Dickens' territory (and a final Oscar nomination) as William Dorrit in [Little Dorrit (1987)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0095530/?ls).  
  
In 1959, he was knighted by [Queen Elizabeth II](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0703070/?ls) for services to the arts. In 1980 he received the Academy Honorary Award for lifetime achievement.  
  
Guinness died on 5 August 2000, from liver cancer, at Midhurst in West Sussex.

[Lawrence of Arabia (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056172/?ref_=ls_knf_18)

[Omar Sharif](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001725/?ls), the Egyptian actor best known for playing Sherif Ali in [Lawrence of Arabia (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056172/?ls) and the title role in [Doctor Zhivago (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059113/?ls), was born Michel Demitri Shalhoub on April 10, 1932 in Alexandria, Egypt to Joseph Shalhoub, a lumber merchant, and his wife, Claire (Saada). Of Lebanese and Syrian extraction, the young Michel was raised Catholic. He was educated at Victoria College in Alexandria and took a degree in mathematics and physics from Cairo University with a major. Afterward graduating from university, he entered the family lumber business.  
  
Before making his English-language film debut with "Lawrence of Arabia", for which he earned a Best Supporting Actor Academy Award nomination and international fame, Sharif became a star in Egyptian cinema. His first movie was the Egyptian film [The Blazing Sun (1954)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0044429/?ls) ("The Blazing Sun") in 1953, opposite the renowned Egyptian actress [Faten Hamama](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0357303/?ls) whom he married in 1955. He converted to Islam to marry Hamama and took the name Omar al-Sharif. The couple had one child ([Tarek Sharif](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0788779/?ls), who was born in 1957 and portrayed the young Zhivago in the eponymous picture) and divorced in 1974. Sharif never remarried.  
  
Beginning in the 1960s, Sharif earned a reputation as one of the world's best known contract bridge players. In the 1970s and 1980s, he co-wrote a syndicated newspaper bridge column for the Chicago Tribune. Sharif also wrote several books on bridge and has licensed his name to a bridge computer game, "Omar Sharif Bridge", which has been marketed since 1992. Sharif told the press in 2006 that he no longer played bridge, explaining, "I decided I didn't want to be a slave to any passion any more except for my work. I had too many passions, bridge, horses, gambling. I want to live a different kind of life, be with my family more because I didn't give them enough time.".  
  
As an actor, Sharif had made a comeback in 2003 playing the title role of an elderly Muslim shopkeeper in the French film [Monsieur Ibrahim (2003)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0329388/?ls). For his performance, he won the Best Actor Award at the Venice Film Festival and the Best Actor César, France's equivalent of the Oscar, from the Académie des Arts et Techniques du Cinéma.  
  
Diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease in 2012, Sharif died of a heart attack on July 10, 2015, in Cairo, Egypt.

 #### [19. Henry Fonda](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000020/?ref_=ls_t_19) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Additional Crew

[12 Angry Men (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050083/?ref_=ls_knf_19)

This remarkable, soft-spoken American began in films as a diffident juvenile. With passing years, he matured into a star character actor who exemplified not only integrity and strength, but an ideal of the common man fighting against social injustice and oppression. He was born in Grand Island, Hall, Nebraska, the son of Herberta Elma (Jaynes) and William Brace Fonda, who was a commercial printer, and proprietor of the W. B. Fonda Printing Company in Omaha, Nebraska. His distant ancestors were Italians who had fled their country and moved to Holland, presumably because of political or religious persecution. In the mid-1600s, they crossed the Atlantic and settled in upstate New York where they founded a community with the Fonda name.  
  
Growing up, Henry developed an early interest in journalism after having a story published in a local newspaper. At the age of twelve, he helped in his father's printing business for $2 a week. Following graduation from high school in 1923, he got a part-time job in Minneapolis with the Northwestern Bell Telephone Company which allowed him at first to pursue journalistic studies at the University of Minnesota. As it became difficult to juggle his working hours with his academic roster, he obtained another position as a physical education instructor at $30 a week, including room and board. By this time, he had grown to a height of six foot one and was a natural for basketball.  
  
In 1925, having returned to Omaha, Henry reevaluated his options and came to the conclusion that journalism was not his forte, after all. For a while, he tried his hand at several temporary jobs, including as a mechanic and a window dresser. Then, despite opposition from his parents, Henry accepted an offer from Gregory Foley, director of the Omaha Playhouse, to play the title role in 'Merton of the Movies'. His father would not speak to him for a month. The play and its star received fairly good notices in the local press. It ran for a week, after which Henry observed "the idea of being Merton and not myself taught me that I could hide behind a mask". For the rest of the repertory season, Henry advanced to assistant director which enabled him to design and paint sets as well as act. A casual trip to New York, however, had already made him set his sights on Broadway.  
  
In 1928, he headed east and briefly played in summer stock before joining the University Players, a group of talented Princeton and Harvard graduates among whose number were such future luminaries as [James Stewart](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000071/?ls) (who would remain his closest lifelong friend), [Joshua Logan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0517597/?ls) and [Kent Smith](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0808949/?ls). Before long, Henry played leads opposite [Margaret Sullavan](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0837925/?ls), soon to become the first of his five wives. Both marriage and the players broke up four years later. In 1932, Henry found himself sharing a two-room New York apartment with Jimmy Stewart and Joshua Logan. For the next two years, he alternated scenic design with acting at various repertory companies. In 1934, he got a break of sorts, when he was given the chance to present a comedy sketch with [Imogene Coca](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0168042/?ls) in the Broadway revue New Faces. That year, he also hired [Leland Hayward](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0371770/?ls) as his personal management agent and this was to pay off handsomely.  
  
It was Hayward who persuaded the 29-year old to become a motion picture actor, despite initial misgivings and reluctance on Henry's part. Independent producer [Walter Wanger](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0911137/?ls), whose growing stock company was birthed at United Artists, needed a star for [The Farmer Takes a Wife (1935)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0026338/?ls). With both first choice actors [Gary Cooper](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000011/?ls) and [Joel McCrea](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0566948/?ls) otherwise engaged, Henry was the next available option. After all, he had just completed a successful run on Broadway in the stage version. The cheesy publicity tag line for the picture was "you'll be fonder of Fonda", but the film was an undeniable hit. Wanger, realizing he had a good thing going, next cast Henry in a succession of A-grade pictures which capitalized on his image as the sincere, unaffected country boy. Pick of the bunch were the Technicolor outdoor western [The Trail of the Lonesome Pine (1936)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0028401/?ls), the gritty Depression-era drama [You Only Live Once (1937)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0029808/?ls) (with Henry as a back-to-the-wall good guy forced into becoming a fugitive from the law by circumstance), the screwball comedy [The Moon's Our Home (1936)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0027979/?ls) (with ex-wife Sullavan), the excellent pre-civil war-era romantic drama [Jezebel (1938)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0030287/?ls) and the equally superb [Young Mr. Lincoln (1939)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0032155/?ls), in which Henry gave his best screen performance to date as the 'jackleg lawyer from Springfield'. Henry made two more films with director [John Ford](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000406/?ls): the pioneering drama [Drums Along the Mohawk (1939)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0031252/?ls) and [The Grapes of Wrath (1940)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0032551/?ls), with Henry as Tom Joad, often regarded his career-defining role as the archetypal grassroots American trying to stand up against oppression. It also set the tone for his subsequent career. Whether he played a lawman (Wyatt Earp in [My Darling Clementine (1946)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0038762/?ls)), a reluctant posse member ([The Ox-Bow Incident (1943)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0036244/?ls), a juror committed to the ideal of total justice in ([12 Angry Men (1957)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0050083/?ls)) or a nightclub musician wrongly accused of murder ([The Wrong Man (1956)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051207/?ls)), his characters were alike in projecting integrity and quiet authority. In this vein, he also gave a totally convincing (though historically inaccurate) portrayal in the titular role of [The Return of Frank James (1940)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0032983/?ls), a rare example of a sequel improving upon the original.  
  
Henry rarely featured in comedy, except for a couple of good turns opposite [Barbara Stanwyck](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001766/?ls) -- with whom he shared an excellent on-screen chemistry -- in [The Mad Miss Manton (1938)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0030396/?ls) and [The Lady Eve (1941)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0033804/?ls). He was also good value as a poker-playing grifter in the western comedy [A Big Hand for the Little Lady (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0060165/?ls). Finally, just to confound those who would typecast him, he gave a chilling performance as one of the coldest, meanest stone killers ever to roam the West, in [Sergio Leone](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001466/?ls)'s classic [Once Upon a Time in the West (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064116/?ls). Illness curtailed his work in the 1970s. His final screen role was as an octogenarian in [On Golden Pond (1981)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0082846/?ls), in which he was joined by his daughter Jane. It finally won him an Oscar on the heels of an earlier Honorary Academy Award. Too ill to attend the ceremony, he died soon after at the age of 77, having left a lasting legacy matched by few of his peers.

 #### [20. Spencer Tracy](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000075/?ref_=ls_t_20) 

    *   Actor
    *   Soundtrack

[Guess Who's Coming to Dinner (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061735/?ref_=ls_knf_20)

Spencer Tracy was the second son born on April 5, 1900, to truck salesman John Edward and Caroline Brown Tracy in Milwaukee, Wisconsin. While attending Marquette Academy, he and classmate [Pat O'Brien](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0002285/?ls) quit school to enlist in the Navy at the start of World War I. Tracy was still at Norfolk Navy Yard in Virginia at the end of the war. After playing the lead in the play "The Truth" at Ripon College he decided that acting might be his career.  
  
Moving to New York, Tracy and O'Brien, who'd also settled on a career on the stage, roomed together while attending the Academy of Dramatic Arts. In 1923 both got nonspeaking parts as robots in "R.U.R.", a dramatization of the groundbreaking science fiction novel by Czech author Karel Capek. Making very little money in stock, Tracy supported himself with jobs as bellhop, janitor and salesman until [John Ford](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000406/?ls) saw his critically acclaimed performance in the lead role in the play "The Last Mile" (later played on film by Clark Gable) and signed him for The William Fox Film Company's production of [Up the River (1930)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0021508/?ls). Despite appearing in sixteen films at that studio over the next five years, Tracy was never able to rise to full film star status there, in large part because the studio was unable to match his talents to suitable story material.  
  
During that period the studio itself floundered, eventually merging with [Darryl F. Zanuck](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0953123/?ls), Joseph Schenck and William Goetz's William 20th Century Pictures to become 20th Century-Fox). In 1935 Tracy signed with MGM under the aegis of [Irving Thalberg](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0856921/?ls) and his career flourished. He became the first actor to win back-to-back Best Actor Oscars for [Captains Courageous (1937)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0028691/?ls) and, in a project he initially didn't want to star in, [Boys Town (1938)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0029942/?ls).  
  
During Tracy's nearly forty-year film career, he was nominated for his performances in [San Francisco (1936)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0028216/?ls), [Father of the Bride (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0042451/?ls), [Bad Day at Black Rock (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0047849/?ls), [The Old Man and the Sea (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0052027/?ls), [Inherit the Wind (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0053946/?ls), [Judgment at Nuremberg (1961)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0055031/?ls), and [Guess Who's Coming to Dinner (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061735/?ls).  
  
Tracy had a brief romantic relationship with [Loretta Young](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0949835/?ls) in the mid-1930s, and a lifelong one with [Katharine Hepburn](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000031/?ls) beginning in 1942 after they were first paired in Woman of the Year by director George Stevens. Tracy's strong Roman Catholic beliefs precluded his divorcing wife Louise, though they mostly lived apart. Tracy suffered from severe alcoholism and diabetes (from the late 1940s), which led to his declining several tailor-made roles in films that would become big hits with other actors in those roles. Although his drinking problems were well known, he was considered peerless among his colleagues (Tracy had a well-deserved reputation for keeping co-stars on their toes for his oddly endearing scene-stealing tricks), and remained in demand as a senior statesman who nevertheless retained box office clout. Two weeks after completion of [Stanley Kramer](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0006452/?ls)'s [Guess Who's Coming to Dinner (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061735/?ls), during which he suffered from lung congestion, Spencer Tracy died of a heart attack.

 #### [1. Richard Burton](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000009/?ref_=ls_t_1) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Director

[Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061184/?ref_=ls_knf_1)

Probably best-remembered for his turbulent personal life with Elizabeth Taylor (whom he married twice), Richard Burton was nonetheless also regarded as an often brilliant British actor of the post-WWII period.  
  
Burton was born Richard Walter Jenkins in 1925 into a Welsh (Cymraeg)-speaking family in Pontrhydyfen to Edith Maude (Thomas) and Richard Walter Jenkins, a coal miner. The twelfth of thirteen children, his mother died while he was a toddler and his father later abandoned the family, leaving him to be raised by an elder sister, Cecilia. An avid fan of Shakespeare, poetry and reading, he once said "home is where the books are". He received a scholarship to Oxford University to study acting and made his first stage appearance in 1944.  
  
His first film appearances were in routine British movies such as [Woman of Dolwyn (1949)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0041579/?ls), [Waterfront Women (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0043121/?ls) and [Green Grow the Rushes (1951)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0043601/?ls). Then he started to appear in Hollywood movies such as [My Cousin Rachel (1952)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0044937/?ls), [The Robe (1953)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0046247/?ls) and [Alexander the Great (1956)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048937/?ls), added to this he was also spending considerable time in stage productions, both in the UK and USA, often to splendid reviews. The late 1950s was an exciting and inventive time in UK cinema, often referred to as the "British New Wave", and Burton was right in the thick of things, and showcased a sensational performance in [Look Back in Anger (1959)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051879/?ls). He also appeared with a cavalcade of international stars in the World War II magnum opus [The Longest Day (1962)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056197/?ls), and then onto arguably his most "notorious" role as that of Marc Antony opposite [Elizabeth Taylor](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000072/?ls) in the hugely expensive [Cleopatra (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0056937/?ls). This was, of course, the film that kick-started their fiery and passionate romance (plus two marriages), and the two of them appeared in several productions over the next few years including [The V.I.P.s (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057634/?ls), [The Sandpiper (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059674/?ls), the dynamic [Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf? (1966)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061184/?ls) and [The Taming of the Shrew (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061407/?ls), as well as box office flops like [The Comedians (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061502/?ls). Burton did better when he was off on his own giving higher caliber performances, such as those in [Becket (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057877/?ls), the film adaptation of the [Tennessee Williams](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0931783/?ls) play [The Night of the Iguana (1964)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0058404/?ls), the brilliant espionage thriller [The Spy Who Came in from the Cold (1965)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0059749/?ls) and alongside [Clint Eastwood](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000142/?ls) in the World War II action adventure film [Where Eagles Dare (1968)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0065207/?ls).  
  
His audience appeal began to decline somewhat by the end of the 1960s as fans turned to younger, more virile male stars, however Burton was superb in [Anne of the Thousand Days (1969)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0064030/?ls) as King Henry VIII, he put on a reasonable show in the boring [Raid on Rommel (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067650/?ls), was over the top in the awful [Villain (1971)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0067952/?ls), gave sleepwalking performances in [Hammersmith Is Out (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068674/?ls) and [Bluebeard (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068294/?ls), and was wildly miscast in the ludicrous [The Assassination of Trotsky (1972)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0068226/?ls).  
  
By the early 1970s, quality male lead roles were definitely going to other stars, and Burton found himself appearing in some movies of dubious quality, just to pay the bills and support family, including [Divorce His - Divorce Hers (1973)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0069980/?ls) (his last on-screen appearance with Taylor), [The Klansman (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0071721/?ls), [Brief Encounter (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0071247/?ls), [Jackpot (1974)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0198158/?ls) (which was never completed) and [Exorcist II: The Heretic (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0076009/?ls). However, he won another Oscar nomination for his excellent performance as a concerned psychiatrist in [Equus (1977)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0075995/?ls). He appeared with fellow acting icons [Richard Harris](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001321/?ls) and [Roger Moore](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000549/?ls) in [The Wild Geese (1978)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0078492/?ls) about mercenaries in South Africa. While the film had a modest initial run, over the past thirty-five years it has picked up quite a cult following. His final performances were as the wily inquisitor "O'Brien" in the most recent film version of George Orwell's dystopian [1984 (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0087803/?ls), in which he won good reviews, and in the TV mini series [Ellis Island (1984)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0086705/?ls). He passed away on August 5, 1984 in Celigny, Switzerland from a cerebral hemorrhage.

 #### [2. Sidney Poitier](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0001627/?ref_=ls_t_2) 

    *   Actor
    *   Director
    *   Producer

[In the Heat of the Night (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061811/?ref_=ls_knf_2)

Sidney Poitier was a native of Cat Island, Bahamas, although born, two months prematurely, in Miami during a visit by his parents, Evelyn (Outten) and Reginald James Poitier. He grew up in poverty as the son of farmers, with his father also driving a cab in Nassau. Sidney had little formal education and at the age of 15 was sent to Miami to live with his brother, in order to forestall a growing tendency toward delinquency. In the U.S., he experienced the racial chasm that divides the country, a great shock to a boy coming from a society with a majority of African descent.  
  
At 18, he went to New York, did menial jobs and slept in a bus terminal toilet. A brief stint in the Army as a worker at a veterans' hospital was followed by more menial jobs in Harlem. An impulsive audition at the American Negro Theatre was rejected so forcefully that Poitier dedicated the next six months to overcoming his accent and improving his performing skills. On his second try, he was accepted. Spotted in rehearsal by a casting agent, he won a bit part in the Broadway production of "Lysistrata", for which he earned good reviews. By the end of 1949, he was having to choose between leading roles on stage and an offer to work for [Darryl F. Zanuck](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0953123/?ls) in the film [No Way Out (1950)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0042792/?ls). His performance as a doctor treating a white bigot got him plenty of notice and led to more roles. Nevertheless, the roles were still less interesting and prominent than those white actors routinely obtained. But seven years later, after turning down several projects he considered demeaning, Poitier got a number of roles that catapulted him into a category rarely if ever achieved by an African-American man of that time, that of leading man. One of these films, [The Defiant Ones (1958)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0051525/?ls), earned Poitier his first Academy Award nomination as Best Actor. Five years later, he won the Oscar for [Lilies of the Field (1963)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0057251/?ls), the first African American to win for a leading role.  
  
He remained active on stage and screen as well as in the burgeoning Civil Rights movement. His roles in [Guess Who's Coming to Dinner (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0061735/?ls) and [To Sir, with Love (1967)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0062376/?ls) were landmarks in helping to break down some social barriers between blacks and whites. Poitier's talent, conscience, integrity, and inherent likability placed him on equal footing with the white stars of the day. He took on directing and producing chores in the 1970s, achieving success in both arenas.

 #### [3. Burt Lancaster](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000044/?ref_=ls_t_3) 

    *   Actor
    *   Producer
    *   Additional Crew

[From Here to Eternity (1953)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0045793/?ref_=ls_knf_3)

Burt Lancaster, one of five children, was born in Manhattan, to Elizabeth (Roberts) and James Henry Lancaster, a postal worker. All his grandparents were immigrants from the north of Ireland. He was a tough street kid who took an early interest in gymnastics. He joined the circus as an acrobat and worked there until he was injured. In the Army during WWII he was introduced to the USO and to acting. His first film was [The Killers (1946)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0038669/?ls), and that made him a star. He was a self-taught actor who learned the business as he went along. He set up his own production company in 1948 with [Harold Hecht](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0372959/?ls) and [James Hill](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0384343/?ls) to direct his career. He played many different roles in pictures as varied as [The Crimson Pirate (1952)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0044517/?ls), [From Here to Eternity (1953)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0045793/?ls), [Elmer Gantry (1960)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0053793/?ls) and [Atlantic City (1980)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0080388/?ls).  
  
His production company, Hecht-Hill-Lancaster, produced such films as [Paddy Chayefsky](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0154665/?ls)'s [Marty (1955)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0048356/?ls) (Oscar winner 1955) and [The Catered Affair (1956)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0049061/?ls). In the 1980s he appeared as a supporting player in a number of movies, such as [Local Hero (1983)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0085859/?ls) and [Field of Dreams (1989)](https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0097351/?ls). However, it will be the sound of his voice, the way that he laughed, and the larger-than-life characters he played that will always be remembered.
