## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anil_Kapoor&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Anil Surinder Kapoor was born into a [Punjabi Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Punjabi_Hindu "Punjabi Hindu") family[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-13) affiliated with the [Arya Samaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arya_Samaj "Arya Samaj")[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-14) on 24 December 1956[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-DOB-1)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-News18-15) in [Chembur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chembur "Chembur") to Nirmal Kapoor and film producer [Surinder Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surinder_Kapoor "Surinder Kapoor").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-18)[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-DOB-1)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-News18-15) The family belongs to the greater [Kapoor show business family.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapoor_family "Kapoor family") He is the second of four children. His elder brother, [Boney Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boney_Kapoor "Boney Kapoor") is a film producer and younger brother [Sanjay Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjay_Kapoor "Sanjay Kapoor") is an actor. Actress [Sridevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi "Sridevi") and the producer [Mona Shourie Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mona_Shourie_Kapoor "Mona Shourie Kapoor"), both Boney's wives, were his sisters-in-law, and Sandeep Marwah,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-19) founder of the [Noida Film City](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noida_Film_City "Noida Film City") and owner of Marwah Studios, is his brother-in-law. The film actors [Arjun Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjun_Kapoor "Arjun Kapoor"), Mohit Marwah and [Ranveer Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranveer_Singh "Ranveer Singh") are his nephews, while actresses [Janhvi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Janhvi_Kapoor "Janhvi Kapoor") and [Khushi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khushi_Kapoor "Khushi Kapoor") are his nieces. [Prithviraj Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prithviraj_Kapoor "Prithviraj Kapoor") was his father's cousin.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-20)

Kapoor was educated at [Our Lady of Perpetual Succour High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Our_Lady_of_Perpetual_Succour_High_School "Our Lady of Perpetual Succour High School"), [Chembur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chembur "Chembur"),[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-21) and at the [St. Xavier's College, Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._Xavier's_College,_Mumbai "St. Xavier's College, Mumbai").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-22)

## Acting career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anil_Kapoor&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Acting career")]

Kapoor made his debut in films in 1970, playing a younger version of [Shashi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor "Shashi Kapoor")'s character in _Tu Payal Mein Geet_.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-23) The film, however, did not release theatrically.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-24)

### 1979–1980s: Rise and establishment

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anil_Kapoor&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 1979–1980s: Rise and establishment")]

Anil Kapoor made his [Hindi film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_film "Hindi film") debut with Umesh Mehra's _[Hamare Tumhare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamare\_Tumhare "Hamare Tumhare")_ (1979), in a small role.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-25) He then starred as a lead actor in the 1980 [Telugu film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_film "Telugu film"), _[Vamsa Vruksham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vamsa\_Vruksham "Vamsa Vruksham")_ directed by veteran [Bapu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapu_(director) "Bapu (director)").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-26) In the same year, he also appeared in two more Hindi films – _[Ek Baar Kaho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ek\_Baar\_Kaho "Ek Baar Kaho")_ and _[Hum Paanch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hum\_Paanch\_(film) "Hum Paanch (film)")_. In 1981, he appeared in [M. S. Sathyu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M._S._Sathyu "M. S. Sathyu") 's _Kahan Kahan Se Guzar Gaya_.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-27) After playing a small role in _[Shakti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakti\_(1982\_film) "Shakti (1982 film)")_ (1982), he made his [Kannada film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kannada_film "Kannada film") debut with [Mani Ratnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mani_Ratnam "Mani Ratnam")'s debut directorial _[Pallavi Anu Pallavi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallavi\_Anu\_Pallavi "Pallavi Anu Pallavi")_ (1983).[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-28) He played his first Hindi film leading role in _[Woh Saat Din](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woh\_Saat\_Din "Woh Saat Din")_ (1983) which was directed by Bapu and featured [Padmini Kolhapure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padmini_Kolhapure "Padmini Kolhapure") and [Naseeruddin Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naseeruddin_Shah "Naseeruddin Shah").[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-29) He gained recognition in [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") with [Yash Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yash_Chopra "Yash Chopra")'s action drama _[Mashaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mashaal "Mashaal")_ (1984) as a _[tapori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapori\_(word) "Tapori (word)")_, for which he won his first [Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor"). His _tapori_ persona and [stubble](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Designer_stubble "Designer stubble") look was considered unconventional at the time, but would become fashionable in India many years later.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-30) Kapoor's 1985 releases included _[Yudh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yudh\_(film) "Yudh (film)")_ and _[Saaheb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saaheb "Saaheb")_. _Yudh_ featured him uttering his iconic line "Ek Dum Jhakaas". But it was _[Meri Jung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meri\_Jung "Meri Jung")_ (1985), wherein he played the role of an angry young lawyer fighting for justice that earned him his first nomination for the [Filmfare Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Actor").[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-31)

He then played a comic tapori again in _[Karma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karma\_(1986\_film) "Karma (1986 film)")_ (1986), the biggest hit of the year.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-32)

He was the protagonist in [Shekhar Kapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shekhar_Kapur "Shekhar Kapur")'s sci-fi film _[Mr. India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mr.\_India\_(1987\_film) "Mr. India (1987 film)")_ (1987), the biggest hit of the year.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] The film became one of his biggest box-office hits and shot him to stardom.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-boxofficeindia1-33) In 1988, he won his first Filmfare Award for Best Actor for his performance in the film, _[Tezaab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tezaab "Tezaab")_, the biggest blockbuster of 1988.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-34) The same year also saw the release of _[Kasam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kasam\_(1988\_film) "Kasam (1988 film)")_, an action drama directed by [Umesh Mehra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umesh_Mehra "Umesh Mehra"). The following year, he delivered _[Ram Lakhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram\_Lakhan "Ram Lakhan")_ (which became the second-highest box office earner of 1989)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-35) featuring [Madhuri Dixit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhuri_Dixit "Madhuri Dixit") in the chartbuster song _One Two Ka Four_. In _[Rakhwala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rakhwala\_(1989\_film) "Rakhwala (1989 film)")_, Kapoor played the role of a tapori, and the film was declared a success.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-boxofficeindia1-33) Kapoor's portrayal of an autistic man in _[Eeshwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eeshwar\_(1989\_film) "Eeshwar (1989 film)")_ (1989) was well-received and established his versatility as an actor, earning him his third nomination for the Filmfare Award for Best Actor.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] He went on to star again alongside [Jackie Shroff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jackie_Shroff "Jackie Shroff") and [Madhuri Dixit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhuri_Dixit "Madhuri Dixit") in the crime thriller [Parinda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parinda "Parinda") (1989), his last film of the year, one of the highest grossing films of 1989.

### 1990s: Career fluctuations

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anil_Kapoor&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 1990s: Career fluctuations")]

The year 1990 saw him play a dual role, as twin brothers in the highly successful action comedy _[Kishen Kanhaiya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishen\_Kanhaiya "Kishen Kanhaiya")_ and the same year, he further attained reasonable box-office success with _[Ghar Ho To Aisa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghar\_Ho\_To\_Aisa "Ghar Ho To Aisa")_.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-36) Kapoor came up with a critically acclaimed performance in _[Awaargi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Awaargi "Awaargi")_. Many critics called that his best performance ever but the film flopped at the box office. Also films like _[Jamai Raja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamai\_Raja\_(film) "Jamai Raja (film)")_ and _[Jeevan Ek Sanghursh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeevan\_Ek\_Sanghursh "Jeevan Ek Sanghursh")_, which were remakes of South Indian films, didn't go on to become huge hits.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

This was followed by a highly praised performance as a middle-aged man in Yash Chopra's intergenerational musical romantic drama _[Lamhe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamhe "Lamhe")_ (1991), opposite [Sridevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi "Sridevi"), which won her the [Filmfare Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actress "Filmfare Award for Best Actress"), with Kapoor earning his fourth nomination for the Filmfare Award for Best Actor. The film proved to a landmark film of Indian cinema and Yash Chopra's best work to date. It was the first film in which he appeared without a moustache. Although the film was an underwhelming success at the domestic box-office, it proved to be a major success overseas. Anil Kapoor's 1991 releases, _[Benaam Badsha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benaam\_Badsha "Benaam Badsha")_ was accorded average status at the box office.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-37)

In 1992, Kapoor received his second Filmfare Award for Best Actor for his hard-hitting performance in Indra Kumar's _[Beta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beta\_(film) "Beta (film)")_ – the biggest blockbuster of the year opposite [Madhuri Dixit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madhuri_Dixit "Madhuri Dixit").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-38) In 1993, Boney Kapoor's much-delayed mega-budget, _[Roop Ki Rani Choron Ka Raja](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roop\_Ki\_Rani\_Choron\_Ka\_Raja\_(1993\_film) "Roop Ki Rani Choron Ka Raja (1993 film)")_ was a disaster at the box-office and damaged Kapoor's reputation as the industry's biggest star at the time. The only major success in these years was _[Laadla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laadla\_(1994\_film) "Laadla (1994 film)")_ (1994) again alongside [Sridevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi "Sridevi"), a film produced by Nitin Manmohan. Kapoor gave a splendid performance as a simpleton lover in the musical romantic drama _[1942: A Love Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1942:\_A\_Love\_Story "1942: A Love Story")_ opposite [Manisha Koirala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manisha_Koirala "Manisha Koirala"). Kapoor earned his sixth nomination for the Filmfare Award for Best Actor for his performance in the film. His other 1994 release, _[Andaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andaz\_(1994\_film) "Andaz (1994 film)")_, opposite [Juhi Chawla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juhi_Chawla "Juhi Chawla") and [Karisma Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karisma_Kapoor "Karisma Kapoor"), was also a success. His 1995 release, _[Trimurti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trimurti "Trimurti")_ was a box-office disaster, though Kapoor's performance was positively received, earning him his second nomination for the Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

After a few box-office failures, he had successes with films like _[Loafer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loafer\_(1996\_film) "Loafer (1996 film)")_ (1996), opposite [Juhi Chawla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juhi_Chawla "Juhi Chawla").[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-39) In _[Judaai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Judaai\_(1997\_film) "Judaai (1997 film)")_, Kapoor's depiction of a loving husband torn between his two wives was appreciated and the film fared well at the box-office.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]_[Deewana Mastana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deewana\_Mastana "Deewana Mastana")_ (1997), _[Biwi No.1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biwi\_No.1 "Biwi No.1")_ (1999) and _[Hum Aapke Dil Mein Rehte Hain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hum\_Aapke\_Dil\_Mein\_Rehte\_Hain "Hum Aapke Dil Mein Rehte Hain")_ (1999) were also box office hits, with _Biwi No. 1_ earning him his first nomination for the [Filmfare Award for Best Comedian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_a_Comic_Role "Filmfare Award for Best Performance in a Comic Role").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-40) Kapoor's unusual characterisation of a zealous, crooked musical superstar in _[Taal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taal\_(film) "Taal (film)")_ (1999) shocked both audience and critics alike, earning him rave reviews, in addition to his second Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-41) He again won rave reviews for his performance in _[Virasat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virasat\_(1997\_film) "Virasat (1997 film)")_ (1997), a remake of the [Tamil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_cinema "Tamil cinema") film, _[Thevar Magan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thevar\_Magan "Thevar Magan")_ (1992), in which he played [Kamal Haasan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamal_Haasan "Kamal Haasan")'s role. The film proved to be a major box office success, and earned him his first [Filmfare Award for Best Actor (Critics)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Critics_Award_for_Best_Actor "Filmfare Critics Award for Best Actor"), in addition to his seventh nomination for the Filmfare Award for Best Actor. He also starred in the unsuccessful _[Jhooth Bole Kauwa Kaate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jhooth\_Bole\_Kauwa\_Kaate "Jhooth Bole Kauwa Kaate")_, which was filmmaker [Hrishikesh Mukherjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hrishikesh_Mukherjee "Hrishikesh Mukherjee")'s last directorial, along with [Juhi Chawla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juhi_Chawla "Juhi Chawla"). He shaved his moustache once again for the second half of the film.

### 2000s: Transition to supporting roles

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anil_Kapoor&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: 2000s: Transition to supporting roles")]

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/26/Tom_Cruise_visits_the_Taj_Mahal_with_Anil_Kapoor.jpg/330px-Tom_Cruise_visits_the_Taj_Mahal_with_Anil_Kapoor.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tom_Cruise_visits_the_Taj_Mahal_with_Anil_Kapoor.jpg)

Kapoor with [Tom Cruise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tom_Cruise "Tom Cruise") at [Taj Mahal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taj_Mahal "Taj Mahal"), [Agra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agra "Agra")

Anil Kapoor's first release of 2000 was _[Bulandi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bulandi\_(2000\_film) "Bulandi (2000 film)")_, in which he played a double role, showing restraint and maturity as the elder Thakur.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-42) He won his first [National Film Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actor "National Film Award for Best Actor"), in addition to his eighth nomination for the [Filmfare Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards") for Best Actor for his performance in [Rajkumar Santoshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkumar_Santoshi "Rajkumar Santoshi")'s critically acclaimed _[Pukar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pukar\_(2000\_film) "Pukar (2000 film)")_ (2000). Kapoor again achieved critical and commercial success with _[Hamara Dil Aapke Paas Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamara\_Dil\_Aapke\_Paas\_Hai "Hamara Dil Aapke Paas Hai")_ (2000).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] Kapoor performed as Rajeev in the much delayed _[Karobaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karobaar "Karobaar")_ (2000), a film directed by [Rakesh Roshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rakesh_Roshan "Rakesh Roshan"), where Kapoor's dialogue delivery was appreciated.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-43) He delivered a powerhouse performance in Shanker's _[Nayak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nayak\_(2001\_Hindi\_film) "Nayak (2001 Hindi film)")_ (2001), which is considered to be his career-best performances.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-44)

In 2002, Kapoor performed in the role of a fat man in _[Badhaai Ho Badhaai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badhaai\_Ho\_Badhaai "Badhaai Ho Badhaai")_, a takeoff from the [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_the_United_States "Cinema of the United States") hit, _[The Nutty Professor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Nutty\_Professor\_(1996\_film) "The Nutty Professor (1996 film)")_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] He performed in the [Indra Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indra_Kumar "Indra Kumar") directed film _[Rishtey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rishtey\_(2002\_film) "Rishtey (2002 film)")_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In _[Om Jai Jagadish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om\_Jai\_Jagadish "Om Jai Jagadish")_, he gave a performance described as "first-rate" by one critic.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-45) Kapoor shared the screen with Bollywood actor [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") for the first time in _[Armaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Armaan\_(2003\_film) "Armaan (2003 film)")_, and played the character of a neurosurgeon.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In his 2003 release, _[Calcutta Mail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta\_Mail "Calcutta Mail")_, according to PlanetBollywood.com, he delivered "one of his best performances. His character was defined with ample scope to perform in this screenplay-driven performance and in spite of the strong supporting cast, this really came out as Kapoor's one-man show."[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-46)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-47) According to [Bollywood Hungama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood_Hungama "Bollywood Hungama"), he "ignited the silver screen with an authoritative performance" in _[Musafir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musafir\_(2004\_film) "Musafir (2004 film)")_ alongside [Sameera Reddy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sameera_Reddy "Sameera Reddy"), [Aditya Pancholi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aditya_Pancholi "Aditya Pancholi"), [Sanjay Dutt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjay_Dutt "Sanjay Dutt") and [Koena Mitra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Koena_Mitra "Koena Mitra").[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-49) Kapoor performed as the stricken husband in the thriller _[My Wife's Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Wife's\_Murder "My Wife's Murder")_, which he also produced.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-51)[Anees Bazmee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anees_Bazmee "Anees Bazmee")'s super-hit comedy _[No Entry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/No\_Entry "No Entry")_ (2005), followed for Kapoor that year. The film went on to become the highest-grossing film of the year, earning him his second nomination for the Filmfare Award for Best Comedian.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-52) He was also in the film [_Bewafaa_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bewafaa_(2005_film) "Bewafaa (2005 film)"), playing a rich businessman who is forced to marry the sister of his wife after she passes away in childbirth.

Kapoor played a grey character in the 2005 thriller, _[Chocolate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chocolate\_(2005\_film) "Chocolate (2005 film)")_.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-53) Anil's first release of 2007 _[Salaam-e-Ishq: A Tribute to Love](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salaam-e-Ishq:\_A\_Tribute\_to\_Love "Salaam-e-Ishq: A Tribute to Love")_ was a box office hit in overseas though a flop in India.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-54) Anees Bazmee's _[Welcome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welcome\_(2007\_film) "Welcome (2007 film)")_, which released on 21 December 2007 was declared the biggest success of the year, earning him his fourth nomination for the Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-55) Kapoor's understated performance in [Subhash Ghai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subhash_Ghai "Subhash Ghai")'s _[Black & White](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black\_&\_White\_(2008\_Hindi\_film) "Black & White (2008 Hindi film)")_ was highly lauded.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-56) His first release in 2008, Abbas Mustan's thriller, _[Race](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race\_(2008\_film) "Race (2008 film)")_ became a box-office hit. Vijay Krishna Acharya's _[Tashan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tashan\_(film) "Tashan (film)")_ marked Anil's comeback to [Yash Raj Films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yash_Raj_Films "Yash Raj Films"), but failed to do well at the box-office.

His first English language film, _[Slumdog Millionaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slumdog\_Millionaire "Slumdog Millionaire")_, which was released on 12 November 2008. _[Yuvvraaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuvvraaj "Yuvvraaj")_ was released on 21 November 2008. _[Yuvvraaj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yuvvraaj "Yuvvraaj")_, with [Salman Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salman_Khan "Salman Khan") and [Katrina Kaif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katrina_Kaif "Katrina Kaif"), failed to do well at the box-office. On the other hand, _Slumdog Millionaire_ has won a number of international awards and received rave reviews from critics, costing only US$15 million to produce, but pulling in more than $352 million worldwide. In January 2009, he attended the [66th Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/66th_Golden_Globe_Awards "66th Golden Globe Awards") ceremony along with the team of _Slumdog Millionaire_, which won four [Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards "Golden Globe Awards"). Kapoor demonstrated his well-known enthusiasm after _Slumdog_ won the [Academy Award for Best Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Best_Picture "Academy Award for Best Picture") (one of eight awards). He also received a nomination for Best Ensemble at the [Black Reel Awards of 2008](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Black_Reel_Awards_of_2008 "Black Reel Awards of 2008") and has won the [Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Actors_Guild_Award_for_Outstanding_Performance_by_a_Cast_in_a_Motion_Picture "Screen Actors Guild Award for Outstanding Performance by a Cast in a Motion Picture").

### 2010–present: Subsequent success

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anil_Kapoor&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: 2010–present: Subsequent success")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/91/Anil_Kapoor_at_%E2%80%9924%E2%80%99_game_launching_event.jpg/330px-Anil_Kapoor_at_%E2%80%9924%E2%80%99_game_launching_event.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Anil_Kapoor_at_%E2%80%9924%E2%80%99_game_launching_event.jpg)

Kapoor at [_24_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24_(Indian_TV_series) "24 (Indian TV series)") video game launch

In 2010, Kapoor starred in the [eighth season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24_(season_8) "24 (season 8)") of the American television series _[24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24\_(TV\_series) "24 (TV series)")_, portraying [Omar Hassan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omar_Hassan_(24_character) "Omar Hassan (24 character)"), President of the fictional [Islamic Republic of Kamistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_Republic_of_Kamistan "Islamic Republic of Kamistan"). He made an appearance as a [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai")-based media tycoon in the Hollywood tentpole _[Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission:\_Impossible\_%E2%80%93\_Ghost\_Protocol "Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol")_ (released in December 2011)_.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil\_Kapoor#cite\_note-57)_ He was cast in _Power_, which was to be directed by [Rajkumar Santoshi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajkumar_Santoshi "Rajkumar Santoshi") but was shelved for unknown reasons _.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil\_Kapoor#cite\_note-58)_

Anil Kapoor's only release of 2012 _[Tezz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tezz "Tezz")_ earned him favourable reviews from critics; Taran Adarsh wrote that "...it's a treat watching Anil Kapoor on screen. Though the actor has been an integral part of so many movies in the past, you can never accuse him of repeating himself. Besides, he may be in his early 50s, but that hasn't deterred Anil from performing the high-octane action stunts with flourish."[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-59)

His performance in _[Shootout at Wadala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shootout\_at\_Wadala "Shootout at Wadala")_ was highly acclaimed by critics; [Sudhish Kamath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudhish_Kamath "Sudhish Kamath") of _[The Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Hindu "The Hindu")_ wrote that "Anil Kapoor is first-rate, revelling in a tailor-made role as a no-nonsense cop, reminding us of the superstar he used to be in the Eighties."[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-60) In January 2013 Kapoor became the first Indian actor to be invited for a special segment; "In conversation", at the [Toronto International Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toronto_International_Film_Festival "Toronto International Film Festival"), an honour which is reserved for actors having considerable body of work.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-62) Beginning in 2013, he starred in the lead role of Jai Singh Rathod in the [Indian remade series of _24_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24_(Indian_TV_series) "24 (Indian TV series)").

In 2015, he starred alongside an [ensemble cast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ensemble_cast "Ensemble cast") of [Shefali Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shefali_Shah "Shefali Shah"), [Priyanka Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Priyanka_Chopra "Priyanka Chopra"), [Ranveer Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranveer_Singh "Ranveer Singh"), [Anushka Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anushka_Sharma "Anushka Sharma") and [Farhan Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farhan_Akhtar "Farhan Akhtar") in [Zoya Akhtar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoya_Akhtar "Zoya Akhtar")'s family comedy-drama _[Dil Dhadakne Do](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dil\_Dhadakne\_Do "Dil Dhadakne Do")_, which proved to be a commercial success and received positive reviews, earning Kapoor his third Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor.

In September 2015, Kapoor made an appearance as himself in an ad for the _[Angry Birds Friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Angry\_Birds\_Friends "Angry Birds Friends")_ tournament Champions for Earth. Amazon cast Kapoor in its pilot _[The Book of Strange New Things](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Book\_of\_Strange\_New\_Things "The Book of Strange New Things")_,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-63) to play the role of Vikram Danesh, the authoritative head of the base on Oasis.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-64) Kapoor reprised his role of Majnu Bhai in the crime comedy _[Welcome Back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welcome\_Back\_(film) "Welcome Back (film)")_ (2015), the sequel to _[Welcome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Welcome\_(2007\_film) "Welcome (2007 film)")_ (2007).[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-65) Featuring an ensemble cast that included reprising actor [Nana Patekar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nana_Patekar "Nana Patekar") and new additions [John Abraham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Abraham "John Abraham") and [Shruti Hassan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shruti_Haasan "Shruti Haasan") among others. It opened to mixed reception but emerged as another success.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-66)

In 2017, he starred with his nephew, [Arjun Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arjun_Kapoor "Arjun Kapoor"), in [Anees Bazmee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anees_Bazmee "Anees Bazmee") directed romantic comedy _[Mubarakan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mubarakan "Mubarakan")_. Kapoor played dual roles, one of which was a turbaned [Sikh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sikhs "Sikhs").[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-67) The following year, he appeared in _[Race 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race\_3 "Race 3")_ (2018), the third instalment in [_Race franchise_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Race_(film_series) "Race (film series)"). Although Kapoor was in the first two films, his _Race 3_ character was new to the series.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-68) The film was moderately successful despite generally negative reception.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-69) In the same year, Kapoor portrayed the titular character in _[Fanney Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fanney\_Khan "Fanney Khan")_, a remake of Belgian film _[Everybody's Famous!](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Everybody's\_Famous! "Everybody's Famous!")_ (2000).[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-70) Alternatively, he voiced [Baloo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baloo "Baloo") for the Hindi dub version of _[Mowgli: Legend of the Jungle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mowgli:\_Legend\_of\_the\_Jungle "Mowgli: Legend of the Jungle")_ (2018).[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-71)

2019 was a busy year for Kapoor as he played supporting roles in the coming-of-age romantic dramedy _[Ek Ladki Ko Dekha Toh Aisa Laga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ek\_Ladki\_Ko\_Dekha\_Toh\_Aisa\_Laga "Ek Ladki Ko Dekha Toh Aisa Laga")_,[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-72) adventure comedy _[Total Dhamaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Total\_Dhamaal "Total Dhamaal")_, sports drama _[The Zoya Factor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Zoya\_Factor\_(film) "The Zoya Factor (film)")_,[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-73) and starred in the action comedy _[Pagalpanti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pagalpanti\_(2019\_film) "Pagalpanti (2019 film)")_.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-74) In _Ek Ladki Ko Dekha Toh Aisa Laga_ and _The Zoya Factor_, he worked alongside his daughter [Sonam Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonam_Kapoor "Sonam Kapoor"), with the former's screenplay being selected by the [Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_of_Motion_Picture_Arts_and_Sciences "Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences") for its library's core collection, due to its concept of [female homosexuality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Female_homosexuality "Female homosexuality").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-75) On the other hand, _Total Dhamaal_ became a hit.[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-76)

Kapoor kicked off the decade alongside [Aditya Roy Kapur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aditya_Roy_Kapur "Aditya Roy Kapur") in the prison thriller _[Malang](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malang\_(film) "Malang (film)")_ (2020).[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-77) Kapoor played a corrupt police inspector and was praised for his performance.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-78) Malang became a commercial success.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-79) He next played a fictional version of himself in black comedy _[AK vs AK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AK\_vs\_AK "AK vs AK")_, alongside [Anurag Kashyap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anurag_Kashyap "Anurag Kashyap"). The names "AK" in the title are the initials of the two leads.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-80) Directed by [Vikramaditya Motwane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vikramaditya_Motwane "Vikramaditya Motwane"), the film was released on [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") to positive reviews, with Kapoor's performance receiving particular praise as one of the best of his career.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-82) This also marked Kapoor's first time working with his son [Harsh Varrdhan Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harsh_Varrdhan_Kapoor "Harsh Varrdhan Kapoor").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-83)

In 2022, Kapoor starred with Harsh Varrdhan Kapoor in the western thriller _[Thar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thar\_(film) "Thar (film)")_, produced by Netflix. His portrayal of a 1980s police inspector, earned high praise despite mixed reviews for the film,[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-84) earned him the [Filmfare OTT Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_OTT_Awards "Filmfare OTT Awards") for Best Supporting Actor in a Web Original Film.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-85) He played a hedonistic, unfaithful husband and irresponsible father in the family dramedy _[Jugjugg Jeeyo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jugjugg\_Jeeyo "Jugjugg Jeeyo")_. Tushar Joshi of _[India Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India\_Today "India Today")_ called him the film's standout performer,[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-86) while [Taran Adarsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taran_Adarsh "Taran Adarsh") of _[Bollywood Hungama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood\_Hungama "Bollywood Hungama")_ deemed him "flawless," noting his skilful balancing of dramatic highs and lows.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-87) This role earned him his record setting fourth Best Supporting Actor award at the [68th Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/68th_Filmfare_Awards "68th Filmfare Awards").[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-88)

Kapoor co-produced and made a cameo in female sex comedy _[Thank You for Coming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank\_You\_for\_Coming "Thank You for Coming")_ (2023), which premiered at the [2023 Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/48th_Toronto_International_Film_Festival "48th Toronto International Film Festival") in the Gala Presentations section,[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-auto-89) but turned out to be a financial failure.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-90) In the 2023 action film _[Animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal\_(2023\_Indian\_film) "Animal (2023 Indian film)")_, directed by [Sandeep Reddy Vanga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sandeep_Reddy_Vanga "Sandeep Reddy Vanga"), Kapoor played a powerful industrialist and strict father to [Ranbir Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranbir_Kapoor "Ranbir Kapoor")'s character.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-91) The controversial film became [one of the highest-grossing Indian films of all time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_Indian_films "List of highest-grossing Indian films") and Kapoor's highest-grossing Indian film to date,[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-92)[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-93) earning him another Filmfare Award nomination for Best Supporting Actor.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-94)

He then starred in [Siddharth Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siddharth_Anand "Siddharth Anand")'s _[Fighter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fighter\_(2024\_film) "Fighter (2024 film)")_, alongside [Hrithik Roshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hrithik_Roshan "Hrithik Roshan") and [Deepika Padukone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepika_Padukone "Deepika Padukone").[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-95) The film fictionalises the 2019 military events between India and Pakistan, including the [Pulwama attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Pulwama_attack "2019 Pulwama attack"), the [Balakot airstrike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Balakot_airstrike "2019 Balakot airstrike"), and the subsequent border skirmishes.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-96) It was a hit, topping overseas box office charts.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-97)[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-98) He later starred in action thriller _[Savi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Savi\_(film) "Savi (film)")_ (2024), also featuring [Divya Khosla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divya_Khosla_Kumar "Divya Khosla Kumar") and [Harshvardhan Rane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harshvardhan_Rane "Harshvardhan Rane"). It was an adaptation of 2008 French film _[Anything for Her](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anything\_for\_Her "Anything for Her")_.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-99)

Kapoor appeared in the _[YRF Spy Universe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YRF\_Spy\_Universe "YRF Spy Universe")_ film _[War 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/War\_2\_(film) "War 2 (film)")_ (2025) as the Chief of [RAW](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_and_Analysis_Wing "Research and Analysis Wing") Colonel Vikrant Kaul. He reprised this role in the seventh instalment in the universe, _[Alpha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha\_(2026\_film) "Alpha (2026 film)")_ (2026)_,_ starring [Alia Bhatt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alia_Bhatt "Alia Bhatt"), [Sharvari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharvari "Sharvari"), and [Bobby Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bobby_Deol "Bobby Deol").[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-100)

## Other work

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anil_Kapoor&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Other work")]

### Producing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anil_Kapoor&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Producing")]

In 2002, Kapoor produced his first film, the comedy _[Badhaai Ho Badhaai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Badhaai\_Ho\_Badhaai "Badhaai Ho Badhaai")_, in which he also starred. It was followed by _[My Wife's Murder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/My\_Wife's\_Murder "My Wife's Murder")_ (2005), and _[Gandhi, My Father](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gandhi,\_My\_Father "Gandhi, My Father")_ (2007). _Gandhi, My Father_ focuses on the relationship between [Mahatma Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mahatma_Gandhi "Mahatma Gandhi") and his son [Harilal Gandhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harilal_Gandhi "Harilal Gandhi") and was awarded the [National Film Award – Special Jury Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_%E2%80%93_Special_Jury_Award_(feature_film) "National Film Award – Special Jury Award (feature film)"). He produced the film _[Shortkut: The Con Is On](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shortkut "Shortkut")_ starring [Akshaye Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akshaye_Khanna "Akshaye Khanna") and [Arshad Warsi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arshad_Warsi "Arshad Warsi"). In 2010, he produced _[Aisha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aisha\_(2010\_film) "Aisha (2010 film)")_ (2010), starring his daughter [Sonam Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonam_Kapoor "Sonam Kapoor") and [Abhay Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abhay_Deol "Abhay Deol"). The film performed moderately at the box-office, grossing Rs. 155 million in its theatrical run.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-101)

He has acquired the remake rights for the American TV series, _[24](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24\_(TV\_series) "24 (TV series)")_, reportedly for an amount of INR 1 billion. It took him about 1.5 years to license the rights to create an Indian rendition of the popular TV show.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-102) Kapoor will be stepping into the protagonist's (Jack Bauer) role as well. Kapoor played the role of [President Hassan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Omar_Hassan_(24_character) "Omar Hassan (24 character)") in the [8th season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/24_(season_8) "24 (season 8)") of the original series aired on [Fox Network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_Network "Fox Network"). Kapoor co-produced the female sex comedy _[Thank You for Coming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thank\_You\_for\_Coming "Thank You for Coming")_ (2023).[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-auto-89)

### Singing

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anil_Kapoor&action=edit&section=9 "Edit section: Singing")]

Anil Kapoor has on rare occasions contributed to the soundtracks of his movies as a singer. One of his first playback songs was the title track of the 1986 Bollywood comedy _[Chameli Ki Shaadi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chameli\_Ki\_Shaadi "Chameli Ki Shaadi")_. The song was comic in nature and depicted the love story of the titular Chameli and her lover [Charandas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Charandas "Charandas"), played by Kapoor. Chameli was portrayed by [Amrita Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amrita_Singh "Amrita Singh"). In the same decade, he was credited on the song "Tere Bina Main Nahin Mere Bina Tu Nahin" for the film _[Woh Saat Din](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woh\_Saat\_Din "Woh Saat Din")_. He is also credited on the song "I Love You" from _[Hamara Dil Aapke Paas Hai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamara\_Dil\_Aapke\_Paas\_Hai "Hamara Dil Aapke Paas Hai")_. In 2008, Kapoor provided a rhyme-like-dialogue to introduce his character in Yashraj's _[Tashan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tashan\_(film) "Tashan (film)")_. His theme was titled "Bhaiyaji ka Tashan". His co-stars in the movie also had their introductions incorporated in the [soundtrack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soundtrack "Soundtrack"), which was composed by [Vishal–Shekhar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishal%E2%80%93Shekhar "Vishal–Shekhar"). [Akshay Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Akshay_Kumar "Akshay Kumar")'s theme was titled "Bachchan Pandey ka Tashan". Kareena Kapoor's was "Pooja ka Tashan". _[Saif Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saif\_Ali\_Khan "Saif Ali Khan")_ was credited for "Jimmy ka Tashan". He had one full album, "Welcome" as a co-singer with [Salma Agha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salma_Agha "Salma Agha") in 1986. The album was scored by [Bappi Lahiri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bappi_Lahiri "Bappi Lahiri").

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anil_Kapoor&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Personal life")]

In 1984, Kapoor married Sunita Bhavnani, a costume designer with whom he has two daughters and a son.[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-103) Bhavnani is the cousin of [Ranveer Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ranveer_Singh "Ranveer Singh")'s mother. Their elder daughter [Sonam Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sonam_Kapoor "Sonam Kapoor") (born 1985) is a former actress and their younger daughter [Rhea Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhea_Kapoor "Rhea Kapoor") (born 1987) is a film producer while their son [Harsh Varrdhan Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harsh_Varrdhan_Kapoor "Harsh Varrdhan Kapoor") (born 1990) is an actor. Kapoor is referred to as ‘AK’ by his children.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-104)

For financially exploiting his name, appearance, and voice, as well as the slogan "jhakaas" (the [Marathi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marathi_language "Marathi language") word for wonderful), which became associated with him after he used it in one of his films, Kapoor sued a number of websites and platforms in 2023.[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-105)[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-106)

## Awards and recognition

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Anil_Kapoor&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Awards and recognition")]

Main article: [List of awards and nominations received by Anil Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Anil_Kapoor "List of awards and nominations received by Anil Kapoor")

Kapoor has been one of the most popular and successful actors of Hindi cinema.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-107) Known for his performance in films of various genres, he is also one of the few [Indian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_people "Indian people") stars to make a mark in mainstream [Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_United_States "Cinema of United States") with films like _[Slumdog Millionaire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slumdog\_Millionaire "Slumdog Millionaire")_ (2008) and _[Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mission:\_Impossible\_%E2%80%93\_Ghost\_Protocol "Mission: Impossible – Ghost Protocol")_ (2011).[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-108) Kapoor appeared in _[Box Office India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box\_Office\_India "Box Office India")_'s "Top Actors" list four times from 1988 to 1990 and 1992.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-Top_Actors-7) In 2022, he placed in _[Outlook India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlook\_India "Outlook India")_'s "75 Best Bollywood Actors" list.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-109)

**Anil Surinder Kapoor** (born 24 December 1956) is an Indian actor and producer who works primarily in [Hindi films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema"), in addition to Indian television and international films.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-DOB-1) In a career spanning over 40 years, Kapoor has appeared in more than [100 films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor_filmography "Anil Kapoor filmography").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-2) He has received [several accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_awards_and_nominations_received_by_Anil_Kapoor "List of awards and nominations received by Anil Kapoor"), including two [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards") and seven [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-Filmfare-3)

Born to film producer [Surinder Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surinder_Kapoor "Surinder Kapoor"), Anil made his Bollywood debut with a small role in the romance _[Hamare Tumhare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamare\_Tumhare "Hamare Tumhare")_ (1979) before starring in the [Telugu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_cinema "Telugu cinema") film _[Vamsa Vruksham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vamsa\_Vruksham "Vamsa Vruksham")_ (1980) and [Kannada film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kannada_cinema "Kannada cinema")_[Pallavi Anupallavi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallavi\_Anupallavi "Pallavi Anupallavi")_ (1983).[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-5) His first three successes were _[Mashaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mashaal "Mashaal")_ (1984), _[Woh 7 Din](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woh\_7\_Din "Woh 7 Din")_ (1984) and _[Meri Jung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meri\_Jung "Meri Jung")_ (1985), which made him a star.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anil_Kapoor#cite_note-Top_Actors-7) He went onto establish himself as an actor with highly (1987 film)")_ (1987), _[Tezaab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tezaab "Tezaab")_ (1988), _[Ram Lakhan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ram\_Lakhan "Ram Lakhan")_ (1989),
