## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Scenes_from_a_Marriage&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Legacy")]

Bergman's 1980 television film _[From the Life of the Marionettes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/From\_the\_Life\_of\_the\_Marionettes "From the Life of the Marionettes")_ centres on a couple named Peter and Katarina, loosely based on the supporting characters of those names in _Scenes from a Marriage_.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-FOOTNOTESteene2005151%E2%80%93152-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-FOOTNOTELuko2015209-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-FOOTNOTEMaltin2017507-39) Bergman also wrote the first stage adaptation of _Scenes from a Marriage_ for the [Residenztheater in Munich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Residenztheater_(Munich) "Residenztheater (Munich)") in 1981.[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-FOOTNOTEGado1986400-40)_[Saraband](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saraband "Saraband")_, a quasi-sequel set decades after the original miniseries, aired on Swedish television in 2003.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-FOOTNOTESundholmThorsenAnderssonHedling201274-41) In 2008, a theatrical adaption by [Joanna Murray-Smith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joanna_Murray-Smith "Joanna Murray-Smith") was performed at the [Belgrade Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belgrade_Theatre "Belgrade Theatre") in [Coventry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coventry "Coventry"), directed by [Trevor Nunn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trevor_Nunn "Trevor Nunn") and starring [Imogen Stubbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imogen_Stubbs "Imogen Stubbs") and [Iain Glen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iain_Glen "Iain Glen").

_[Knots Landing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knots\_Landing "Knots Landing")_ creator [David Jacobs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Jacobs_(writer) "David Jacobs (writer)") based the series on _Scenes from a Marriage_.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-42)[Shashi Deshpande](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Deshpande "Shashi Deshpande") informally adapted it into the screenplay for [Govind Nihalani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Govind_Nihalani "Govind Nihalani")'s _[Drishti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drishti\_(film) "Drishti (film)")_ in 1990.[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-44) In 1991, [Woody Allen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woody_Allen "Woody Allen") costarred in [Paul Mazursky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Mazursky "Paul Mazursky")'s _[Scenes from a Mall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes\_from\_a\_Mall "Scenes from a Mall")_, a [dark comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dark_comedy "Dark comedy") about a deteriorating marriage.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-46) Allen's similarly realist 1992 film _[Husbands and Wives](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Husbands\_and\_Wives "Husbands and Wives")_ is also influenced by _Scenes from a Marriage_.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-47) Some critics compared Allen's _[Annie Hall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annie\_Hall "Annie Hall")_ (1977) to _Scenes from a Marriage_.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-48)[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-49)

In an April 2011 _New York Times_ Opinionator article titled "Too Much Relationship Vérité", [Virginia Heffernan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Virginia_Heffernan "Virginia Heffernan") compares _[An American Family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An\_American\_Family "An American Family")_ to _Scenes from a Marriage_:

> It's now the future. And the 12-hour [PBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Public_Broadcasting_Service "Public Broadcasting Service") time capsule, which will make a rare reappearance next week at the [Paley Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paley_Center "Paley Center") in Manhattan and on some public-TV affiliates beginning Saturday, looks more like [performance art](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Performance_art "Performance art") than social science. Hammy stunts for the camera alternate with Bergman-esque staging. ("Scenes from a Marriage", Bergman’s fictional TV series, also appeared in 1973, in Sweden.)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-50)

In June 2013, actor [Ethan Hawke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethan_Hawke "Ethan Hawke") and director [Richard Linklater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Linklater "Richard Linklater") said _Scenes from a Marriage_ was the standard by which their [_Before Midnight_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Before_Midnight_(2013_film) "Before Midnight (2013 film)") must be judged.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-51) Russian director [Andrey Zvyagintsev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrey_Zvyagintsev "Andrey Zvyagintsev") initially conceived _[Loveless](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loveless\_(film) "Loveless (film)")_ (2017) as a remake of _Scenes from a Marriage_,[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-52) with critics also comparing Zvyagintsev's finished product to Bergman's miniseries.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-53)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-54)[Noah Baumbach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Noah_Baumbach "Noah Baumbach")'s _[Marriage Story](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marriage\_Story "Marriage Story")_ (2019) also contains references to _Scenes from a Marriage_.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-55)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scenes_from_a_Marriage#cite_note-56)

# People

Our MCH-affiliated faculty trains graduate students, conducts innovative and rigorous research in maternal and child health across the lifespan, and educates the world on maternal and child health issues.

Our faculty’s research addresses a wide array of critical MCH topics, such as human milk and neurodevelopmental outcomes, the effects of COVID-19 on maternal and perinatal health, social media’s impact on adolescent health, early childhood adversity, and more. Each year, our faculty provides technical assistance to partners at local, regional, national, and international levels, actively engages in numerous conferences and events, and publishes an average of 150 scholarly articles.

For more information about our research, please feel free to email us at [mchconcentration@hsph.harvard.edu](mailto:mchconcentration@hsph.harvard.edu).

# People

Our MCH-affiliated faculty trains graduate students, conducts innovative and rigorous research in maternal and child health across the lifespan, and educates the world on maternal and child health issues.

Our faculty’s research addresses a wide array of critical MCH topics, such as human milk and neurodevelopmental outcomes, the effects of COVID-19 on maternal and perinatal health, social media’s impact on adolescent health, early childhood adversity, and more. Each year, our faculty provides technical assistance to partners at local, regional, national, and international levels, actively engages in numerous conferences and events, and publishes an average of 150 scholarly articles.

For more information about our research, please feel free to email us at [mchconcentration@hsph.harvard.edu](mailto:mchconcentration@hsph.harvard.edu).

## Jodie Foster graduated from Yale in 1985 with a degree in English literature.

![Image 3: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Jodie Foster.Mark Metcalfe/Getty Images

Foster became famous when she was just 5 years old, with a role in the sitcom "Mayberry R.F.D.," and she won critical acclaim as a teenager acting in Martin Scorsese's "Taxi Driver."

Foster continued acting over summer vacations during her time at Yale, where she wrote her thesis on the work of Toni Morrison.

Foster returned to acting full-time after college, [winning two best actress Oscars](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000149/awards?ref_=nm_ql_2) for "The Accused" and "Silence of the Lambs." She most recently appeared in "Hotel Artemis" and "The Mauritanian."

## Jeff Cohen, who played Chunk in "The Goonies," attended Berkeley and earned his law degree from UCLA.

![Image 5: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Jeff Cohen.Michael Buckner/Getty Images for Entertainment Weekly

Cohen quit acting, but he's stayed in the industry as an entertainment lawyer. After earning his law degree, he [cofounded the entertainment law firm Cohen Gardner in 2002](https://www.chambers-associate.com/the-big-interview/jeff-cohen-chunk-from-the-goonies-lawyer).

## Haley Joel Osment, who starred in "The Sixth Sense" when he was 11, studied acting at NYU's Tisch School of the Arts.

![Image 7: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Haley Joel Osment.Claudette Barius/Warner Bros.

Osment took a hiatus from Hollywood while enrolled at the Experimental Theatre Wing at NYU's Tisch School of the Arts. He [graduated in 2011](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005286/bio?ref_=nm_ov_bio_sm).

"A film like 'The Sixth Sense' burns an image of who you are into people's minds," Osment told [The New Yorker](https://www.newyorker.com/culture/culture-desk/haley-joel-osment) in 2014. "In the midst of that it can be difficult to know who you are, or who you are becoming. College seemed like a manageable next step, a place where I could figure that stuff out."

Osment has continued acting since his graduation, appearing in shows like "Silicon Valley" and "The Boys," and movies such as Netflix's "Extremely Wicked, Shockingly Evil and Vile." He has also lent his voice to animated series such as "American Dad!," "Jurassic World: Camp Cretaceous," and "Dogs in Space."

## After starring in "Blossom," Mayim Bialik earned a doctorate in neuroscience from UCLA before returning to acting.

![Image 9: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Mayim Bialik.Gustavo Caballero/Getty Images

After finishing her TV series "Blossom" in 1995, Bialik enrolled at UCLA and got her undergraduate degree in neuroscience with minors in Hebrew and Jewish studies in 2000. [She went on to get a doctorate in neuroscience](http://www.cnn.com/2011/HEALTH/07/15/mayim.bialik.big.bang.theory/index.html), receiving her PhD in 2007.

She then proceeded to play a neuroscientist on TV as Amy Farrah Fowler in "The Big Bang Theory."

Bialik currently [shares "Jeopardy!" hosting duties with Ken Jennings](https://www.businessinsider.com/mayim-bialik-facts-jeopardy-host-2021-8) while starring in and executive producing "Call Me Kat" on Fox.

## Natalie Portman took a break from acting to study psychology at Harvard, and she returned to address graduating students in 2015.

![Image 11: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Natalie Portman at Harvard.Dominick Reuter/Reuters

Portman became famous at a young age, filming "Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace" while still attending Syosset High School in New York.

She went on to attend Harvard University, graduating in 2003 with a degree in psychology. She also took classes at Hebrew University in Jerusalem and[guest-lectured at Columbia University](http://www.columbia.edu/cu/news/06/03/nataliePortman.html)on the topic of political violence. But while she dabbled in academia for a bit after college, she mostly returned to acting, winning an Oscar for her role in "Black Swan" in 2011.

Years later, Portman admitted she was nervous about going to Harvard.

"I feared people would assume I had gotten in just for being famous and not worthy of the intellectual rigor here,"[she said in her 2015 Class Day speech at the university](https://www.businessinsider.com/natalie-portman-harvard-commencement-speech-2015-5). "When I got to my graduation, after four years of trying to get excited about something else, I admitted to myself that I couldn't wait to go back and make more films."

## Tia and Tamera Mowry played long-lost twins on the sitcom "Sister Sister," then they both majored in psychology at Pepperdine University.

![Image 13: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Tamera Mowry (left) and Tia Mowry.Araya Diaz/WireImage/Getty Images

"Tia and I were part-time at Pepperdine University," Tamera [told "Today"](https://www.today.com/series/morning-routine/tamera-mowry-reveals-what-it-was-sharing-room-sister-tia-t126505) in 2018. "We would go to class, do a rehearsal or shoot and then come back to class. We would do two classes every other day and then the show on Thursday and Friday. I am happy I did; it taught me about prioritizing, and that education is important. It taught me dedication and hard work too. If you put your mind to it, you can do it. It took me seven years to graduate."

Tamera hosted the daytime talk show, "The Real," for seven years, and acted in "A Christmas Miracle" in 2019.

Tia has also continued acting, including roles in "Baggage Claim" and "Indivisible," and a role on the TV show "Family Reunion."

## Emma Watson went to Brown while filming the "Harry Potter" movies, earning a degree in English literature.

![Image 15: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Emma Watson at her graduation from Brown University.Steven Senne/AP

Watson enrolled at Brown in 2009 and took time off to film the "Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows" movies. She also [studied abroad at the University of Oxford](http://www.nytimes.com/2012/08/17/t-magazine/emma-watson-the-graduate.html?mcubz=1), and she [graduated in 2014](https://www.businessinsider.com/emma-watson-is-basically-hermione-granger-harry-potter-2016-5).

"I really like the fact that it has a very open curriculum, that there aren't any requirements," Watson [told Rookie magazine about her decision to attend Brown in 2013](https://www.rookiemag.com/2013/05/emma-watson-interview/5/). "Really, I've kind of been in charge of my own education since I started out on Potter when I was 9 or 10, and I liked that I could design my own major if I wanted to, and I could take independent studies if I wanted to on subjects that weren't necessarily in the curriculum."

Watson now works as an advocate for gender equality as well as an actress, most recently appearing in Disney's live-action "[Beauty and the Beast,](https://www.businessinsider.com/beauty-and-the-beast-emma-watson-belle-2016-9)" "The Circle," and "Little Women."

## Christy Carlson Romano of "Even Stevens" and "Kim Possible" graduated from Barnard College with a degree in film studies in 2015.

![Image 17: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Christy Carlson Romano.Paul Archuleta/Getty Images

Romano [met her husband, Brendan Rooney](https://m.imdb.com/name/nm0005579/trivia), while studying at Barnard. They married in 2013 and have two children.

She continued doing voiceover work as Trina on "Big Hero 6: The Series," and she hosted the cooking show "Bucket List Bistro" on Fox. She also [discusses her experiences as a child star](https://www.businessinsider.com/christy-carlson-romano-youtube-tiktok-disney-instagram-2021-10) on her YouTube channel.

## "The Suite Life of Zach and Cody" stars Dylan and Cole Sprouse went to NYU.

![Image 19: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Dylan Sprouse (left) and Cole Sprouse.Kevin Winter/Getty Images

Cole studied archaeology, and Dylan majored in video-game design. At their NYU graduation in 2015, they switched places and received each other's diplomas.

"If you look up my graduating photo you'll see. We just decided, you know, there's no reason not to. No one's going to notice,"[Dylan told Teen Vogue](http://www.teenvogue.com/story/dylan-cole-sprouse-graduation-interview) in 2015.

Cole currently plays Jughead Jones on The CW's hit drama "[Riverdale](https://www.businessinsider.com/category/riverdale)." Dylan returned to acting in 2017 — he's appeared in music videos and voiced video games, and he played Trevor in 2020's "When We Collided." He also [opened the brewery All-Wise Meadery](https://www.instagram.com/allwisemeadery/)with two business partners in 2018.

## Dakota Fanning earned her degree in women's studies from NYU in 2016.

![Image 21: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Dakota Fanning.Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images

Fanning enrolled in NYU's Gallatin School of Individualized Study in 2011 and [slowly worked towards her degree](https://www.nyu.edu/content/dam/nyu/univEvents/documents/commencement2018/NYU-commencement-mag-2018-final-hi-res.pdf) while continuing to shoot films.

"They've been very flexible with my schedule and allowed me to do independent studies and take classes and sort of come in and out,"[Fanning told Indiewire in 2015](http://www.indiewire.com/2015/04/tribeca-why-dakota-fanning-doesnt-consider-herself-a-famous-person-62705/). "Everybody's been very understanding and supportive of that. It's kind of what Gallatin was founded upon, so it's really worked for me."

Fanning's studies focused on the portrayal of women in film.

"It's frustrating that you still have to talk about it,"[she told Elle](http://www.ellecanada.com/culture/celebrity/article/exclusive-dakota-fanning-isn-t-planning-on-cracking-anytime-soon) in 2016. "As part of my school, I've studied lots of different periods, and if you go back to, like, 'The Taming of the Shrew,' it's talking about the disparity between genders, and it's crazy that we still haven't cracked that."

## Miranda Cosgrove of "iCarly" switched her major from film to psychology at USC.

![Image 23: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Miranda Cosgrove in 2021.Amy Sussman/KCA2021/Getty Images for Nickelodeon

Best known for the Nickelodeon shows "iCarly" and "Drake and Josh," as well as the films "School of Rock" and "Despicable Me," [Cosgrove is now a student at the University of Southern California](http://dailytrojan.com/2015/02/10/famous-people-youll-see-at-usc/).

In a [2017 appearance on "Live with Kelly and Ryan,"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zv_xVG1_Oi0) Cosgrove spoke about juggling her acting career with her studies.

"I pretty much just focus on school when I'm at school," she said. "With 'Despicable Me,' it was cool because it's voiceover, so that's easy. I could just go in on the weekends."

She currently [stars in the "iCarly" reboot](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1388927/), and she will return to voice Margo in "Despicable Me 4."

## "Black-ish" and "Grown-ish" star Yara Shahidi will graduate from Harvard this year.

![Image 25: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Yara Shahidi.Rich Fury / Staff / Getty Images

Shahidi is majoring in sociology and African-American studies. She celebrated finishing her 136-page thesis in a [video posted to Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/Ca5pHQmgy13/) in March.

Shahidi has balanced her acting career with her studies, ducking out of the 2021 Primetime Emmys early in order to make it to class the next day.

"The lovely people at the Academy really helped me out because I was like, 'Guys, I have a hard out to make this flight,'" she [told Entertainment Tonight.](https://www.etonline.com/yara-shahidi-asked-to-present-early-at-emmys-so-she-could-make-her-class-at-harvard-exclusive "(opens new window)")

## Jodie Foster graduated from Yale in 1985 with a degree in English literature.

![Image 3: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Jodie Foster.Mark Metcalfe/Getty Images

Foster became famous when she was just 5 years old, with a role in the sitcom "Mayberry R.F.D.," and she won critical acclaim as a teenager acting in Martin Scorsese's "Taxi Driver."

Foster continued acting over summer vacations during her time at Yale, where she wrote her thesis on the work of Toni Morrison.

Foster returned to acting full-time after college, [winning two best actress Oscars](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0000149/awards?ref_=nm_ql_2) for "The Accused" and "Silence of the Lambs." She most recently appeared in "Hotel Artemis" and "The Mauritanian."

## Jeff Cohen, who played Chunk in "The Goonies," attended Berkeley and earned his law degree from UCLA.

![Image 5: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Jeff Cohen.Michael Buckner/Getty Images for Entertainment Weekly

Cohen quit acting, but he's stayed in the industry as an entertainment lawyer. After earning his law degree, he [cofounded the entertainment law firm Cohen Gardner in 2002](https://www.chambers-associate.com/the-big-interview/jeff-cohen-chunk-from-the-goonies-lawyer).

## Haley Joel Osment, who starred in "The Sixth Sense" when he was 11, studied acting at NYU's Tisch School of the Arts.

![Image 7: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Haley Joel Osment.Claudette Barius/Warner Bros.

Osment took a hiatus from Hollywood while enrolled at the Experimental Theatre Wing at NYU's Tisch School of the Arts. He [graduated in 2011](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm0005286/bio?ref_=nm_ov_bio_sm).

"A film like 'The Sixth Sense' burns an image of who you are into people's minds," Osment told [The New Yorker](https://www.newyorker.com/culture/culture-desk/haley-joel-osment) in 2014. "In the midst of that it can be difficult to know who you are, or who you are becoming. College seemed like a manageable next step, a place where I could figure that stuff out."

Osment has continued acting since his graduation, appearing in shows like "Silicon Valley" and "The Boys," and movies such as Netflix's "Extremely Wicked, Shockingly Evil and Vile." He has also lent his voice to animated series such as "American Dad!," "Jurassic World: Camp Cretaceous," and "Dogs in Space."

## After starring in "Blossom," Mayim Bialik earned a doctorate in neuroscience from UCLA before returning to acting.

![Image 9: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Mayim Bialik.Gustavo Caballero/Getty Images

After finishing her TV series "Blossom" in 1995, Bialik enrolled at UCLA and got her undergraduate degree in neuroscience with minors in Hebrew and Jewish studies in 2000. [She went on to get a doctorate in neuroscience](http://www.cnn.com/2011/HEALTH/07/15/mayim.bialik.big.bang.theory/index.html), receiving her PhD in 2007.

She then proceeded to play a neuroscientist on TV as Amy Farrah Fowler in "The Big Bang Theory."

Bialik currently [shares "Jeopardy!" hosting duties with Ken Jennings](https://www.businessinsider.com/mayim-bialik-facts-jeopardy-host-2021-8) while starring in and executive producing "Call Me Kat" on Fox.

## Natalie Portman took a break from acting to study psychology at Harvard, and she returned to address graduating students in 2015.

![Image 11: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Natalie Portman at Harvard.Dominick Reuter/Reuters

Portman became famous at a young age, filming "Star Wars: Episode I – The Phantom Menace" while still attending Syosset High School in New York.

She went on to attend Harvard University, graduating in 2003 with a degree in psychology. She also took classes at Hebrew University in Jerusalem and[guest-lectured at Columbia University](http://www.columbia.edu/cu/news/06/03/nataliePortman.html)on the topic of political violence. But while she dabbled in academia for a bit after college, she mostly returned to acting, winning an Oscar for her role in "Black Swan" in 2011.

Years later, Portman admitted she was nervous about going to Harvard.

"I feared people would assume I had gotten in just for being famous and not worthy of the intellectual rigor here,"[she said in her 2015 Class Day speech at the university](https://www.businessinsider.com/natalie-portman-harvard-commencement-speech-2015-5). "When I got to my graduation, after four years of trying to get excited about something else, I admitted to myself that I couldn't wait to go back and make more films."

## Tia and Tamera Mowry played long-lost twins on the sitcom "Sister Sister," then they both majored in psychology at Pepperdine University.

![Image 13: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Tamera Mowry (left) and Tia Mowry.Araya Diaz/WireImage/Getty Images

"Tia and I were part-time at Pepperdine University," Tamera [told "Today"](https://www.today.com/series/morning-routine/tamera-mowry-reveals-what-it-was-sharing-room-sister-tia-t126505) in 2018. "We would go to class, do a rehearsal or shoot and then come back to class. We would do two classes every other day and then the show on Thursday and Friday. I am happy I did; it taught me about prioritizing, and that education is important. It taught me dedication and hard work too. If you put your mind to it, you can do it. It took me seven years to graduate."

Tamera hosted the daytime talk show, "The Real," for seven years, and acted in "A Christmas Miracle" in 2019.

Tia has also continued acting, including roles in "Baggage Claim" and "Indivisible," and a role on the TV show "Family Reunion."

## Emma Watson went to Brown while filming the "Harry Potter" movies, earning a degree in English literature.

![Image 15: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Emma Watson at her graduation from Brown University.Steven Senne/AP

Watson enrolled at Brown in 2009 and took time off to film the "Harry Potter and the Deathly Hallows" movies. She also [studied abroad at the University of Oxford](http://www.nytimes.com/2012/08/17/t-magazine/emma-watson-the-graduate.html?mcubz=1), and she [graduated in 2014](https://www.businessinsider.com/emma-watson-is-basically-hermione-granger-harry-potter-2016-5).

"I really like the fact that it has a very open curriculum, that there aren't any requirements," Watson [told Rookie magazine about her decision to attend Brown in 2013](https://www.rookiemag.com/2013/05/emma-watson-interview/5/). "Really, I've kind of been in charge of my own education since I started out on Potter when I was 9 or 10, and I liked that I could design my own major if I wanted to, and I could take independent studies if I wanted to on subjects that weren't necessarily in the curriculum."

Watson now works as an advocate for gender equality as well as an actress, most recently appearing in Disney's live-action "[Beauty and the Beast,](https://www.businessinsider.com/beauty-and-the-beast-emma-watson-belle-2016-9)" "The Circle," and "Little Women."

## Christy Carlson Romano of "Even Stevens" and "Kim Possible" graduated from Barnard College with a degree in film studies in 2015.

![Image 17: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Christy Carlson Romano.Paul Archuleta/Getty Images

Romano [met her husband, Brendan Rooney](https://m.imdb.com/name/nm0005579/trivia), while studying at Barnard. They married in 2013 and have two children.

She continued doing voiceover work as Trina on "Big Hero 6: The Series," and she hosted the cooking show "Bucket List Bistro" on Fox. She also [discusses her experiences as a child star](https://www.businessinsider.com/christy-carlson-romano-youtube-tiktok-disney-instagram-2021-10) on her YouTube channel.

## "The Suite Life of Zach and Cody" stars Dylan and Cole Sprouse went to NYU.

![Image 19: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Dylan Sprouse (left) and Cole Sprouse.Kevin Winter/Getty Images

Cole studied archaeology, and Dylan majored in video-game design. At their NYU graduation in 2015, they switched places and received each other's diplomas.

"If you look up my graduating photo you'll see. We just decided, you know, there's no reason not to. No one's going to notice,"[Dylan told Teen Vogue](http://www.teenvogue.com/story/dylan-cole-sprouse-graduation-interview) in 2015.

Cole currently plays Jughead Jones on The CW's hit drama "[Riverdale](https://www.businessinsider.com/category/riverdale)." Dylan returned to acting in 2017 — he's appeared in music videos and voiced video games, and he played Trevor in 2020's "When We Collided." He also [opened the brewery All-Wise Meadery](https://www.instagram.com/allwisemeadery/)with two business partners in 2018.

## Dakota Fanning earned her degree in women's studies from NYU in 2016.

![Image 21: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Dakota Fanning.Dimitrios Kambouris/Getty Images

Fanning enrolled in NYU's Gallatin School of Individualized Study in 2011 and [slowly worked towards her degree](https://www.nyu.edu/content/dam/nyu/univEvents/documents/commencement2018/NYU-commencement-mag-2018-final-hi-res.pdf) while continuing to shoot films.

"They've been very flexible with my schedule and allowed me to do independent studies and take classes and sort of come in and out,"[Fanning told Indiewire in 2015](http://www.indiewire.com/2015/04/tribeca-why-dakota-fanning-doesnt-consider-herself-a-famous-person-62705/). "Everybody's been very understanding and supportive of that. It's kind of what Gallatin was founded upon, so it's really worked for me."

Fanning's studies focused on the portrayal of women in film.

"It's frustrating that you still have to talk about it,"[she told Elle](http://www.ellecanada.com/culture/celebrity/article/exclusive-dakota-fanning-isn-t-planning-on-cracking-anytime-soon) in 2016. "As part of my school, I've studied lots of different periods, and if you go back to, like, 'The Taming of the Shrew,' it's talking about the disparity between genders, and it's crazy that we still haven't cracked that."

## Miranda Cosgrove of "iCarly" switched her major from film to psychology at USC.

![Image 23: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Miranda Cosgrove in 2021.Amy Sussman/KCA2021/Getty Images for Nickelodeon

Best known for the Nickelodeon shows "iCarly" and "Drake and Josh," as well as the films "School of Rock" and "Despicable Me," [Cosgrove is now a student at the University of Southern California](http://dailytrojan.com/2015/02/10/famous-people-youll-see-at-usc/).

In a [2017 appearance on "Live with Kelly and Ryan,"](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Zv_xVG1_Oi0) Cosgrove spoke about juggling her acting career with her studies.

"I pretty much just focus on school when I'm at school," she said. "With 'Despicable Me,' it was cool because it's voiceover, so that's easy. I could just go in on the weekends."

She currently [stars in the "iCarly" reboot](https://www.imdb.com/name/nm1388927/), and she will return to voice Margo in "Despicable Me 4."

## "Black-ish" and "Grown-ish" star Yara Shahidi will graduate from Harvard this year.

![Image 25: Yara Shahidi wears a green dress at the Emmys.](blob:http://localhost/3f711207ef1410619eb8e4b36b1349ed)

Yara Shahidi.Rich Fury / Staff / Getty Images

Shahidi is majoring in sociology and African-American studies. She celebrated finishing her 136-page thesis in a [video posted to Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/p/Ca5pHQmgy13/) in March.

Shahidi has balanced her acting career with her studies, ducking out of the 2021 Primetime Emmys early in order to make it to class the next day.

"The lovely people at the Academy really helped me out because I was like, 'Guys, I have a hard out to make this flight,'" she [told Entertainment Tonight.](https://www.etonline.com/yara-shahidi-asked-to-present-early-at-emmys-so-she-could-make-her-class-at-harvard-exclusive "(opens new window)")

Biography:  
 Dr. Anne Hansen received her MD from Harvard Medical School and then went to Boston Children’s Hospital for her pediatric internship and residency. She stayed in Boston for her fellowship in Newborn Medicine at the combined program between Children’s, Beth Israel, and Brigham and Women’s Hospitals. She obtained her M.P.H. with a concentration in Clinical Effectiveness from Harvard School of Public Health. She joined the Harvard Medical School faculty in 1996 and is currently an Associate Professor of Pediatrics. Dr. Anne Hansen has been the Medical Director of the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at Boston Children’s Hospital since 2003. She has authored dozens of clinical guidelines, and is a chair or member of multiple unit based and hospital wide committees. She is a Fellow in the American Academy of Pediatrics. An acclaimed teacher, she is the recipient of the Merton Bernfield mentoring award, the Harvard Medical School Humanism Award, and the Tutor of the Year Award at Harvard Medical School. Dr. Hansen has published over 35 peer reviewed articles, 53 chapters and 8 books.

Research:  
 Dr. Hansen’s research focuses on improving the care of newborns seriously ill with medical and surgical conditions, medical device development, and global health. She has been working since 2010 in collaboration with the Rwanda Ministry of Health (MOH) and Partners In Health (PIH) to develop and implement national standards for newborn care. Recently, they have written a 2nd edition and conducted national trainings with nurses and doctors from all Rwandan provincial hospitals. She is currently working with OPENPediatrics, a free, open-access on-line medical education platform based at Boston Children’s Hospital, to make the Rwandan neonatal protocols, taught by Rwandan doctors and nurses, available as videos to pediatricians around the world. Working with the Rwanda MOH, PIH and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory’s Institute for Globally Transformative Technologies, she has developed a simple, inexpensive, re-usable nonelectric infant warmer that has been tested successfully in Rwanda; She is now working to scale it nationally across Rwanda, as well as globally.

Closer to home, Dr Hansen is collaborating with engineers and industry to develop a Central Venous Catheter with decreased propensity for infection or clot formation. In collaboration with surgeons and industry, she has developed a novel, minimally invasive approach to esophageal growth induction for patients with long gap esophageal atresia. She has examined innovative approaches to the treatment of neonatal conditions including intraventricular urokinase for the prevention of post hemorrhagic hydrocephalus, once daily gentamicin dosing for infants, substitution of cord for infant blood in perinatal sepsis evaluations, and inhaled racemic epinephrine for the treatments of TTN. She was lead investigator in a study of Donation after Cardiac Death (DCD) in the NICU. She developed and implemented the first therapeutic hypothermia program in New England. She is a co-editor of the Manual of Neonatal Care, now in its 8th edition, and co-editor of the Manual of Neonatal Surgical Intensive care, now in its 3rd edition.

Biography:  
 Dr. Anne Hansen received her MD from Harvard Medical School and then went to Boston Children’s Hospital for her pediatric internship and residency. She stayed in Boston for her fellowship in Newborn Medicine at the combined program between Children’s, Beth Israel, and Brigham and Women’s Hospitals. She obtained her M.P.H. with a concentration in Clinical Effectiveness from Harvard School of Public Health. She joined the Harvard Medical School faculty in 1996 and is currently an Associate Professor of Pediatrics. Dr. Anne Hansen has been the Medical Director of the Neonatal Intensive Care Unit at Boston Children’s Hospital since 2003. She has authored dozens of clinical guidelines, and is a chair or member of multiple unit based and hospital wide committees. She is a Fellow in the American Academy of Pediatrics. An acclaimed teacher, she is the recipient of the Merton Bernfield mentoring award, the Harvard Medical School Humanism Award, and the Tutor of the Year Award at Harvard Medical School. Dr. Hansen has published over 35 peer reviewed articles, 53 chapters and 8 books.

Research:  
 Dr. Hansen’s research focuses on improving the care of newborns seriously ill with medical and surgical conditions, medical device development, and global health. She has been working since 2010 in collaboration with the Rwanda Ministry of Health (MOH) and Partners In Health (PIH) to develop and implement national standards for newborn care. Recently, they have written a 2nd edition and conducted national trainings with nurses and doctors from all Rwandan provincial hospitals. She is currently working with OPENPediatrics, a free, open-access on-line medical education platform based at Boston Children’s Hospital, to make the Rwandan neonatal protocols, taught by Rwandan doctors and nurses, available as videos to pediatricians around the world. Working with the Rwanda MOH, PIH and Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory’s Institute for Globally Transformative Technologies, she has developed a simple, inexpensive, re-usable nonelectric infant warmer that has been tested successfully in Rwanda; She is now working to scale it nationally across Rwanda, as well as globally.

Closer to home, Dr Hansen is collaborating with engineers and industry to develop a Central Venous Catheter with decreased propensity for infection or clot formation. In collaboration with surgeons and industry, she has developed a novel, minimally invasive approach to esophageal growth induction for patients with long gap esophageal atresia. She has examined innovative approaches to the treatment of neonatal conditions including intraventricular urokinase for the prevention of post hemorrhagic hydrocephalus, once daily gentamicin dosing for infants, substitution of cord for infant blood in perinatal sepsis evaluations, and inhaled racemic epinephrine for the treatments of TTN. She was lead investigator in a study of Donation after Cardiac Death (DCD) in the NICU. She developed and implemented the first therapeutic hypothermia program in New England. She is a co-editor of the Manual of Neonatal Care, now in its 8th edition, and co-editor of the Manual of Neonatal Surgical Intensive care, now in its 3rd edition.

Jaya Bachchan (born April 9, 1948) is a renowned Indian film actress and politician, celebrated for her natural acting style in 1970s Hindi and Bengali cinema. A FTII graduate, she achieved stardom with films like Guddi (1971), Abhimaan (1973), and Sholay (1975).
