**Sharmila Tagore** (Bengali:[[ʃɔɾˈmila ˈʈʰakuɾ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Bengali "Help:IPA/Bengali")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/5/51/LL-Q9610_%28ben%29-Titodutta-%E0%A6%B6%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BE_%E0%A6%A0%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B0.wav/LL-Q9610_%28ben%29-Titodutta-%E0%A6%B6%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BE_%E0%A6%A0%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B0.wav.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LL-Q9610_(ben)-Titodutta-%E0%A6%B6%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BE_%E0%A6%A0%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B0.wav "File:LL-Q9610 (ben)-Titodutta-শর্মিলা ঠাকুর.wav"); born 8 December 1944), also known by her married name **Begum Ayesha Sultana**,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-timesofindia.indiatimes.com-1) is an Indian actress whose career has spanned over six decades across [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema") and [Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_West_Bengal "Cinema of West Bengal") films.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-:0-3) In recognition of her contributions to cinema, she was honoured with Commander of [Order of Arts and Letters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Arts_and_Letters "Order of Arts and Letters") by [Government of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_France "Government of France") in 1999, and [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan"), India's third highest civilian award, in 2013.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-6) Tagore is also a recipient of two [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards") and a [Filmfare Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award "Filmfare Award").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-7)

Born into the prominent [Tagore family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagore_family "Tagore family"), one of the leading families of [Calcutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta "Calcutta") and a key influence during the [Bengali Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Renaissance "Bengal Renaissance"), Tagore made her acting debut at age 14 with [Satyajit Ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satyajit_Ray "Satyajit Ray")'s acclaimed Bengali epic drama _[The World of Apu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_World\_of\_Apu "The World of Apu")_ (1959). She went on to collaborate with Ray on numerous other films, including _[Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devi\_(1960\_film) "Devi (1960 film)")_ (1960), _[Nayak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nayak\_(1966\_film) "Nayak (1966 film)")_ (1966), _[Aranyer Din Ratri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranyer\_Din\_Ratri "Aranyer Din Ratri")_ (1970), and _[Seemabaddha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seemabaddha "Seemabaddha")_ (1971), her other Bengali films over the time included _[Barnali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnali "Barnali")_ (1963), _[Shes Anko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shes\_Anko "Shes Anko")_ (1963), _[Nirjan Saikate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nirjan\_Saikate "Nirjan Saikate")_ (1965), _[Amanush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanush\_(1975\_film) "Amanush (1975 film)")_ (1975), _[Anand Ashram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anand\_Ashram "Anand Ashram")_ (1977), and _[Kalankini Kankabati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalankini\_Kankabati "Kalankini Kankabati")_ (1981); thus establishing herself as one of the most acclaimed actresses of [Bengali cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_West_Bengal "Cinema of West Bengal").

Tagore's career further expanded when she ventured into Hindi films with [Shakti Samanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakti_Samanta "Shakti Samanta")'s romance _[Kashmir Ki Kali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashmir\_Ki\_Kali "Kashmir Ki Kali")_ (1964). She established herself as one of the leading actresses of Hindi cinema with films like _[Waqt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waqt\_(1965\_film) "Waqt (1965 film)")_ (1965), _[Anupama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupama\_(1966\_film) "Anupama (1966 film)")_ (1966), _[Devar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devar "Devar")_ (1966), _[An Evening in Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An\_Evening\_in\_Paris "An Evening in Paris")_ (1967), _[Aamne Saamne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aamne\_Samne\_(1967\_film) "Aamne Samne (1967 film)")_ (1967), _[Mere Hamdam Mere Dost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mere\_Hamdam\_Mere\_Dost "Mere Hamdam Mere Dost")_ (1968), _[Satyakam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satyakam "Satyakam")_ (1969), _[Aradhana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aradhana\_(1969\_film) "Aradhana (1969 film)")_ (1969), _[Safar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safar\_(1970\_film) "Safar (1970 film)")_ (1970), _[Amar Prem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amar\_Prem\_(1972\_film) "Amar Prem (1972 film)")_ (1972), _[Daag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daag\_(1973\_film) "Daag (1973 film)")_ (1973), _[Aa Gale Lag Jaa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aa\_Gale\_Lag\_Jaa\_(1973\_film) "Aa Gale Lag Jaa (1973 film)")_ (1973), _[Avishkaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avishkaar "Avishkaar")_ (1974), _[Chupke Chupke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chupke\_Chupke\_(film) "Chupke Chupke (film)")_ (1975), _[Mausam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mausam\_(1975\_film) "Mausam (1975 film)")_ (1975), _[Ek Mahal Ho Sapno Ka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ek\_Mahal\_Ho\_Sapno\_Ka "Ek Mahal Ho Sapno Ka")_ (1975) and _[Namkeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namkeen "Namkeen")_ (1982). She won the [Filmfare Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actress "Filmfare Award for Best Actress") for _Aradhana_ and the [National Film Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actress "National Film Award for Best Actress") for _Mausam_. This was followed by intermittent film appearances in the subsequent decades, including in _[Sunny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny\_(1984\_film) "Sunny (1984 film)")_ (1984), _[Swati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swati\_(1986\_film) "Swati (1986 film)")_ (1986), _[New Delhi Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Delhi\_Times "New Delhi Times")_ (1986), [Mira Nair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mira_Nair "Mira Nair")'s _[Mississippi Masala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi\_Masala "Mississippi Masala")_ (1991) and [Goutam Ghose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goutam_Ghose "Goutam Ghose")'s _[Abar Aranye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abar\_Aranye "Abar Aranye")_ (2002), which won her the [National Film Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "National Film Award for Best Supporting Actress"), _[Shubho Mahurat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shubho\_Mahurat "Shubho Mahurat")_ (2003), and in the Hindi films _[Aashik Awara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aashik\_Awara "Aashik Awara")_ (1993), _[Mann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mann\_(1999\_film) "Mann (1999 film)")_ (1999), _[Viruddh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viruddh "Viruddh")_ (2005), _[Eklavya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eklavya:\_The\_Royal\_Guard "Eklavya: The Royal Guard")_ (2007) and _[Break Ke Baad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Break\_Ke\_Baad "Break Ke Baad")_ (2010). Following a hiatus of 13 years, she made her film comeback with the drama _[Gulmohar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulmohar\_(2023\_film) "Gulmohar (2023 film)")_ (2023) followed by a critically acclaimed performance in _[Puratawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puratawn "Puratawn")_ (2025).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-8)

Tagore served as the chairperson of the [Central Board of Film Certification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Board_of_Film_Certification "Central Board of Film Certification") from October 2004 to March 2011. In December 2005, she was chosen as a [UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNICEF_Goodwill_Ambassador "UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-UNICEF-9)

## Early life and background

Sharmila Tagore was born on 8 December 1944 in Cawnpore (now [Kanpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanpur "Kanpur")), [United Provinces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Provinces_(1937%E2%80%931950) "United Provinces (1937–1950)") to Gitindranath Tagore, a general manager in the [British India Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_India_Corporation "British India Corporation"), and his wife Ira Tagore (née Barua).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-10) As a member of the aristocratic [Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengalis "Bengalis")[Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_Hindus "Bengali Hindus")[Tagore family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagore_family "Tagore family"), she is related to the Nobel laureate [Rabindranath Tagore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabindranath_Tagore "Rabindranath Tagore"), actress [Devika Rani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devika_Rani "Devika Rani") and the painter [Abanindranath Tagore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abanindranath_Tagore "Abanindranath Tagore"). Her mother was of [Assamese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assamese_people "Assamese people") descent and hailed from the [Barua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barua "Barua") family.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-13) Gitindranath was the grandson of the noted painter [Gaganendranath Tagore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaganendranath_Tagore "Gaganendranath Tagore"), whose own father Gunendranath had been a first cousin of the laureate.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-tagore_tree-14) In fact, Tagore is more closely related to [Rabindranath Tagore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabindranath_Tagore "Rabindranath Tagore") through her mother: her maternal grandmother, Latika Barua (née Tagore), was the granddaughter of [Rabindranath Tagore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabindranath_Tagore "Rabindranath Tagore")'s brother, [Dwijendranath Tagore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwijendranath_Tagore "Dwijendranath Tagore"). Her parents were fourth-cousins.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-tagore_tree-14) Tagore's maternal grandfather (husband of Latika Barua née Tagore) was [Jnanadabhiram Barua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jnanadabhiram_Barua "Jnanadabhiram Barua"), an [Assamese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assamese_people "Assamese people") Freedom Fighter and Writer who was the First Principal of Earl Law College in [Guwahati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guwahati "Guwahati") (now known as Government Law College), himself the son of the noted social worker [Gunabhiram Barua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunabhiram_Barua "Gunabhiram Barua").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-16)

Tagore was the eldest of three daughters and had two younger sisters, the late Oindrila Kunda and Romila Sen. Oindrila was the first in the family to act, and appeared in [Tapan Sinha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapan_Sinha "Tapan Sinha")'s [_Kabuliwala_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabuliwala_(1957_film) "Kabuliwala (1957 film)") (1957) as a child.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-tagore_tree-14)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-17) She later became an international bridge player.

Tagore attended [St. John's Diocesan Girls' Higher Secondary School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._John's_Diocesan_Girls'_Higher_Secondary_School "St. John's Diocesan Girls' Higher Secondary School") and [Loreto Convent, Asansol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loreto_Convent,_Asansol "Loreto Convent, Asansol").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-18) She made her film debut when she was a 13-year-old schoolgirl, after which her studies lost priority. Within a short while, her attendance and performance at school suffered, she came to be regarded as a bad influence on her classmates, and was faced with a choice of either doing films or studying further.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-Indian_Expres6_May_2011-19) At that point, her father advised her to move ahead in life, commit herself to a film career and 'give it her all' in order to become successful.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-Indian_Expres6_May_2011-19)

## Career

### Beginnings and Cinematic Emergence (1958–1968)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Ms._Sharmila_Tagore%2C_actress_and_Shri_Saumitra_Chatterjee%2C_actor_at_the_presentation_of_the_film_%E2%80%98Apur_Sansar%E2%80%99%2C_during_the_40th_International_Film_Festival_%28IFFI-2009%29%2C_at_Panaji%2C_Goa_on_November_30%2C_2009_%281%29.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ms._Sharmila_Tagore,_actress_and_Shri_Saumitra_Chatterjee,_actor_at_the_presentation_of_the_film_%E2%80%98Apur_Sansar%E2%80%99,_during_the_40th_International_Film_Festival_(IFFI-2009),_at_Panaji,_Goa_on_November_30,_2009_(1).jpg)

Sharmila Tagore with [Soumitra Chatterjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soumitra_Chatterjee "Soumitra Chatterjee") at _[Apur Sansar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apur\_Sansar\_(The\_World\_of\_Apu) "Apur Sansar (The World of Apu)")_ presentation in 2009

Tagore began her career as an actress in [Satyajit Ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satyajit_Ray "Satyajit Ray")'s Bengali epic drama _[Apur Sansar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_World\_of\_Apu "The World of Apu")_ (1959), as an ill-fated bride.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-Being_Sharmila,_all_through_life-20) In 1960, Ray cast her again in _[Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devi\_(1960\_film) "Devi (1960 film)")_, a film set in 1860 on Hindu orthodoxy and rational reforms, which she considers her favourite film and performance.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-21) She went onto appear in Bengali films _[Shes Anko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shes\_Anko "Shes Anko")_ and _[Nirjan Saikate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nirjan\_Saikate "Nirjan Saikate")_, winning the [IFFI Best Actor Award (Female)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFFI_Best_Actor_Award_(Female) "IFFI Best Actor Award (Female)") for the latter, alongside [Chhaya Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chhaya_Devi "Chhaya Devi"), [Ruma Guha Thakurta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruma_Guha_Thakurta "Ruma Guha Thakurta"), Renuka Devi and Bharati Devi.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-22)

Tagore made her Hindi film debut with [Shakti Samanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakti_Samanta "Shakti Samanta")'s musical romance _[Kashmir Ki Kali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashmir\_Ki\_Kali "Kashmir Ki Kali")_ (1964) alongside [Shammi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shammi_Kapoor "Shammi Kapoor"). She and Samanta collaborated on several of his later films, including the romantic thriller _[An Evening in Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An\_Evening\_in\_Paris "An Evening in Paris")_ (1967) again opposite Kapoor. With the film, she became the first Indian actress to appear in a swimsuit,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-23)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-Being_Sharmila,_all_through_life-20)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-Rashtriya_Sahara_page_28-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-avi-27) which established Tagore as a [sex symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_symbol "Sex symbol") in Hindi films.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-29) While the scene in the film is often referred to as 'the bikini scene', Tagore's swimwear is actually a one piece. However, she did pose in a bikini for the cover of _[Filmfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare "Filmfare")_ magazine in 1966.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-30)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-Rashtriya_Sahara_page_28-25)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-33) But, when she was the chairperson of the [Central Board of Film Certification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Board_of_Film_Certification "Central Board of Film Certification") 36 years later, she expressed concerns about the increased use of bikinis in Indian films.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-34)

Tagore went on to appear in films such as _[Waqt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waqt\_(1965\_film) "Waqt (1965 film)")_ (1965) opposite [Shashi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor "Shashi Kapoor"), _[Anupama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupama\_(1966\_film) "Anupama (1966 film)")_ (1966) opposite [Dharmendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharmendra "Dharmendra"), _[Devar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devar "Devar")_ (1966) opposite [Dharmendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharmendra "Dharmendra"), _[Sawan Ki Ghata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawan\_Ki\_Ghata "Sawan Ki Ghata")_ (1966) opposite [Manoj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoj_Kumar "Manoj Kumar"), _[Aamne Saamne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aamne\_Samne\_(1967\_film) "Aamne Samne (1967 film)")_ (1967) opposite [Shashi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor "Shashi Kapoor"), _[Mere Hamdam Mere Dost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mere\_Hamdam\_Mere\_Dost "Mere Hamdam Mere Dost")_ (1968) opposite [Dharmendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharmendra "Dharmendra") and the Bengali film _[Nayak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nayak\_(1966\_film) "Nayak (1966 film)")_ (1966) opposite [Uttam Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uttam_Kumar "Uttam Kumar").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-36) Her performance in _Anupama_ proved to be her breakthrough in Hindi cinema.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-37)

### Commercial success and stardom (1969–1979)

The 1970s marked the most successful period of Tagore's career with a string of critical and commercial successes. She worked alongside [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna") on several films including [_Aradhana_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aradhana_(1969_film) "Aradhana (1969 film)") (1969), [_Safar_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safar_(1970_film) "Safar (1970 film)") (1970), _[Chhoti Bahu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chhoti\_Bahu "Chhoti Bahu")_ (1971), _[Amar Prem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amar\_Prem\_(1972\_film) "Amar Prem (1972 film)")_ (1971), [_Raja Rani_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Rani_(1973_film) "Raja Rani (1973 film)") (1973), [_Daag_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daag_(1973_film) "Daag (1973 film)") (1973) and _[Avishkaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avishkaar "Avishkaar")_ (1974), [_Maalik_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maalik_(1972_film) "Maalik (1972 film)") (1972).[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-40) She won the [Filmfare Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actress "Filmfare Award for Best Actress") for _Aradhana_, and was nominated for _Safar_, _Amar Prem_ and _Daag_.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-42) She was paired opposite [Dharmendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharmendra "Dharmendra") in _[Satyakam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satyakam "Satyakam")_ (1969),_[Yakeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yakeen\_(1969\_film) "Yakeen (1969 film)")_ (1969), _[Chupke Chupke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chupke\_Chupke\_(film) "Chupke Chupke (film)")_ (1975), and _[Ek Mahal Ho Sapno Ka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ek\_Mahal\_Ho\_Sapno\_Ka "Ek Mahal Ho Sapno Ka")_ (1975).[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-43)

Tagore teamed up again with [Shashi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor "Shashi Kapoor") for _[Suhana Safar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suhana\_Safar "Suhana Safar")_ (1970), _[Aa Gale Lag Jaa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aa\_Gale\_Lag\_Jaa\_(1973\_film) "Aa Gale Lag Jaa (1973 film)")_ (1973), and _[Paap Aur Punya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paap\_Aur\_Punya "Paap Aur Punya")_ (1974). She also paired with [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") in _[Faraar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faraar\_(1975\_film) "Faraar (1975 film)")_ (1975) and _[Besharam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Besharam\_(1978\_film) "Besharam (1978 film)")_ (1978).

In [Gulzar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar_(lyricist) "Gulzar (lyricist)")'s _[Mausam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mausam\_(1975\_film) "Mausam (1975 film)")_ (1975), Tagore starred alongside [Sanjeev Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjeev_Kumar "Sanjeev Kumar"), earning earned her first [National Film Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actress "National Film Award for Best Actress"), and her fifth nomination for the Filmfare Award for Best Actress.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-auto-44) During this time, she also worked with [Uttam Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uttam_Kumar "Uttam Kumar") in [_Amanush_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanush_(1975_film) "Amanush (1975 film)") (1975), _[Anand Ashram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anand\_Ashram "Anand Ashram")_ (1977) and _[Dooriyaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dooriyaan "Dooriyaan")_ (1979).

Tagore's other films during this period included _[Ek Se Badhkar Ek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ek\_Se\_Badhkar\_Ek\_(1976\_film) "Ek Se Badhkar Ek (1976 film)")_ (1976), _[Tyaag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyaag\_(1977\_film) "Tyaag (1977 film)")_ (1977), which she also co-produced, and the Malayalam film _[Chuvanna Chirakukal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuvanna\_Chirakukal "Chuvanna Chirakukal")_ (1978) among others.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-46)

### Further success and sporadic work (1980–2010)

In the 1980s, Tagore appeared in _[Kalankini Kankabati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalankini\_Kankabati "Kalankini Kankabati")_ (1981), _[Namkeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namkeen "Namkeen")_ (1982), _[New Delhi Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Delhi\_Times "New Delhi Times")_ (1986) and _[Swati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swati\_(1986\_film) "Swati (1986 film)")_ (1986).[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-48) She reunited with Dharmendra in the film _[Sunny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny\_(1984\_film) "Sunny (1984 film)")_ (1984), which also featured Dharmendra's son [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol") in the lead role. Her performance in the film earned her a nomination for the [Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress").

Tagore starred in the Bengali action film _[Protidan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protidan "Protidan")_ (1983) opposite [Naseeruddin Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naseeruddin_Shah "Naseeruddin Shah"), and [Mira Nair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mira_Nair "Mira Nair")'s interracial romantic drama _[Mississippi Masala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi\_Masala "Mississippi Masala")_ (1991).[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-49) She also appeared in supporting roles in _[Ghar Bazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghar\_Bazar "Ghar Bazar")_ (1998) and _[Mann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mann\_(1999\_film) "Mann (1999 film)")_ (1999). She also appeared in two television shows, _[Katha Sagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katha\_Sagar "Katha Sagar")_ (1986) for [DD National](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DD_National "DD National") and _Zindagi_ (1999) for [Star Plus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Plus "Star Plus").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-51)

Tagore was cast in her son [Saif Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saif_Ali_Khan "Saif Ali Khan") in his debut film _[Aashik Awara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aashik\_Awara "Aashik Awara")_ (1993) and the action drama _[Eklavya: The Royal Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eklavya:\_The\_Royal\_Guard "Eklavya: The Royal Guard")_ (2007). She appeared in supporting roles in the musical romantic drama _[Dhadkan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhadkan\_(2000\_film) "Dhadkan (2000 film)")_ (2000) and _[Abar Aranye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abar\_Aranye "Abar Aranye")_ (2003), the latter of which earned her the [National Film Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "National Film Award for Best Supporting Actress").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-52) She also received critical acclaim for her performance in _[Shubho Mahurat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shubho\_Mahurat "Shubho Mahurat")_ (2003).

Tagore appeared in family drama _[Virruddh... Family Comes First](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viruddh "Viruddh")_ (2005) alongside Bachchan, earning her sixth nomination for the Filmfare Award for Best Actress.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

From 2007 to 2009, Tagore appeared in films such as _[Fool & Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fool\_&\_Final "Fool & Final")_ (2007), _[Tasveer 8*10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasveer\_8*10 "Tasveer 8*10")_ (2009), _[Antaheen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antaheen "Antaheen")_ (2009) and the Marathi film _[Samaantar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samaantar "Samaantar")_ (2009).[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-The_Hindu-53) In 2009, she served on the jury at the [62nd Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Cannes_Film_Festival "2009 Cannes Film Festival").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-SharmilaCannes-54) She played a supporting role in the romantic comedy-drama _[Break Ke Baad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Break\_Ke\_Baad "Break Ke Baad")_ (2010)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-55) before embarking on an acting hiatus.

### Return to Cinema and acclaimed performances (2023 to Present)

Tagore made her comeback after a 13-year hiatus with the drama _[Gulmohar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulmohar\_(2023\_film) "Gulmohar (2023 film)")_ (2023), which released on [Disney+ Hotstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+_Hotstar "Disney+ Hotstar").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-hindustantimes.com-56) The film earned her critical acclaim, with the _[Hindustan Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindustan\_Times "Hindustan Times")_ noting that, "The elegance and poise Tagore exudes are remarkable. Her dialogue delivery, gestures, body language, emotions, everything looks just so effortless even after a long hiatus." _[India Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India\_Today "India Today")_ also opined that, "Tagore is always a joy to watch on screen. And, what a comeback!"[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-58) Her performance earned her the [Filmfare OTT Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_OTT_Awards "Filmfare OTT Awards") for Best Actress Critics – Web Original Film, in addition to a nomination for Best Actress – Web Original Film.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-59)

In 2024, Tagore returned to Marathi films with _Outhouse_ alongside [Mohan Agashe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohan_Agashe "Mohan Agashe"), where she played a loving grandmother.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-60) Devesh Sharma of _[Filmfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare "Filmfare")_ noted, "Tagore brings warmth, wisdom, and a spark of curiosity to Aadima, portraying her as a nuanced blend of strength and vulnerability."[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-61) Tagore made her comeback to Bengali films after 14 years with Suman Ghosh's _[Puratawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puratawn "Puratawn")_ (2025).

## Personal life

Tagore with her daughter [Soha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soha_Ali_Khan "Soha Ali Khan") at the premiere of _[Khoya Khoya Chand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khoya\_Khoya\_Chand "Khoya Khoya Chand")_

Tagore [converted to Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converted_to_Islam "Converted to Islam"), changed her name to Begum Ayesha Sultana,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-timesofindia.indiatimes.com-1)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-62) and married [Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mansoor_Ali_Khan_Pataudi "Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi"), the titular [Nawab of Pataudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nawab_of_Pataudi "Nawab of Pataudi") and [Bhopal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nawabs_of_Bhopal "Nawabs of Bhopal") and former captain of the [Indian cricket team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cricket_team "Indian cricket team"), on 27 December 1968.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-64) They had three children: [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") actor [Saif Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saif_Ali_Khan "Saif Ali Khan") (born 1970); [Saba Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saba_Ali_Khan "Saba Ali Khan") (born 1976),[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-65) a jewellery designer; and [Soha Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soha_Ali_Khan "Soha Ali Khan") (born 1978), a Bollywood actress and TV personality. Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi died at age 70 on 22 September 2011.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-66)

From 1991 to 2004, [Saif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saif_Ali_Khan "Saif Ali Khan") was married to actress [Amrita Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amrita_Singh "Amrita Singh"). They have two children, daughter [Sara Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Ali_Khan "Sara Ali Khan") (born 1995) and son [Ibrahim Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibrahim_Ali_Khan_(actor) "Ibrahim Ali Khan (actor)") (born 2001), both actors.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-67) His second marriage is to actress [Kareena Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kareena_Kapoor "Kareena Kapoor") in 2012 with whom he has two sons, Taimur Ali Khan (born 2016) and Jeh Ali Khan (born 2021).[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-68)[Soha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soha_Ali_Khan "Soha Ali Khan") married actor [Kunal Khemu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunal_Khemu "Kunal Khemu") in 2015, and has a daughter Inaaya Naumi Khemmu (born 2017).[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-69)

## Public image and legacy

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Sharmila_T_Lux-Award_2016.jpg/250px-Sharmila_T_Lux-Award_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sharmila_T_Lux-Award_2016.jpg)

Tagore in 2016

Tagore was the highest paid Indian actress in the 1970s, and is considered an accomplished [Indian cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cinema "Indian cinema") veteran.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-71) Surendra Kumar of _[The Sunday Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sunday\_Guardian "The Sunday Guardian")_ considers her to be an actress "ahead of her time" for balancing "the serious persona of realist Bengali films, and the Bollywood persona of films with song-and-dance sequences focused on success at the box office."[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-aheadoftime-72) She has received widespread critical acclaim for her on-screen work, both nationally and internationally. During the introduction of the [2025 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Cannes_Film_Festival "2025 Cannes Film Festival") screening of _Aranyer Din Ratri_, American filmmaker [Wes Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Anderson "Wes Anderson") recalled watching the film 25 years ago "in a very strangely translated, blurry, scratchy, pirated [DVD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DVD "DVD") from a little Bollywood shop in [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey")." He described Tagore's performance in _Aranyer Din Ratri_ as "mysterious, cerebral, mesmerising."[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-:1-73)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-KaelPerfect-74)

Unlike most of her contemporaries in the 1960s, Tagore struck a convenient balance playing both glamorous and homely women on screen. She "explored roles beyond the stereotypical" in an era where women were rarely offered an opportunity to be more than "just a pretty appendage to the hero."[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-:1-73) Her wide range of complex female characters often circumvented the [damsel in distress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damsel_in_distress "Damsel in distress") tropes, defying Indian societal norms and capturing a version of womanhood that is flawed but purposeful.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-75)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-SharmilaT-77) According to Nandini Balial of [Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RogerEbert.com "RogerEbert.com"), she "redefined what an Indian woman could do in a film," and "altered the cinematic landscape for leading ladies." Balial goes on to say that Tagore's women epitomised that "being demure didn't mean being spineless, [and that] emotional devastation wasn't a death sentence."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-:0-3) Filmfare considered her portrayal of a foul-mouthed shrew-ish [sex-worker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_worker "Sex worker") in _Mausam_ as one of the most iconic Bollywood performances.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-80_Iconic-78)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7b/Sharmila_Tagore.jpg/250px-Sharmila_Tagore.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sharmila_Tagore.jpg)

Tagore in 2018

Bucking the Indian film industry's expectations from actresses, Tagore wore a one-piece swimsuit for her 1967 film _An Evening In Paris_. She was the first Bollywood actress to have done so, paving the way for [Dimple Kapadia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimple_Kapadia "Dimple Kapadia") in _Bobby_ (1973), [Zeenat Aman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeenat_Aman "Zeenat Aman") in _[Qurbani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qurbani\_(film) "Qurbani (film)")_ (1980), and [Parveen Babi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parveen_Babi "Parveen Babi") in _[Yeh Nazdeekiyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeh\_Nazdeekiyan "Yeh Nazdeekiyan")_ (1982).[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-79) Her 1969 Filmfare magazine cover, where Tagore poses in a two-piece bikini, was publicly labelled as "obscene" and "attention-seeking." She said her _An Evening In Paris_ director [Shakti Samanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakti_Samanta "Shakti Samanta") called her after the magazine hit the stands and said,"If you want to be in the public eye, this is not the way to go." He also asked Tagore, who was in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") at the time, to return to India immediately. Tagore was "really hurt" by the cover being interpreted as her trying to "be [upwardly mobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_mobility "Social mobility")" and "catch eyeballs."[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In a televised interview with [Karan Johar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karan_Johar "Karan Johar"), she confirmed that "questions were asked in the [Indian] Parliament" following the controversy, and she strategically chose the wife-mother role in _Aradhana_ as her next on-screen appearance.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-80)

With her voluminous hairdos and [chiffon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiffon_(fabric) "Chiffon (fabric)") floral-print [_sarees_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sari "Sari"), Tagore's sense of fashion seamlessly blended traditional elegance with modern glamour. Numerous Indian actresses have gone to emulate her retro-vintage style in recent times, including [Anushka Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anushka_Sharma "Anushka Sharma") for [Bombay Velvet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay_Velvet "Bombay Velvet"), [Preity Zinta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preity_Zinta "Preity Zinta") for _[Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rab\_Ne\_Bana\_Di\_Jodi "Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi")_, and [Deepika Padukone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepika_Padukone "Deepika Padukone") in [Om Shanti Om](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om "Om Shanti Om").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-83) Film historian Sanjay Mukhopadhyay said that her "most significant contribution to Indian cinema is a sense of dignity and grace—after [Waheeda Rehman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waheeda_Rehman "Waheeda Rehman"), she was the only actress of her time who exuded this." Mukhopadhyay adds that with a "strong Tagore lineage coupled with the [Pataudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pataudi_family "Pataudi family")_gharana_ (family dynasty)" she was a "bourgeois star with a biography" who "occupied a cultural space beyond the reach of commoner—she could be looked at, but not possessed."[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-Sharmila'slife-84)

Tagore was inducted into the [Bollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walk_of_the_Stars "Walk of the Stars") at [Bandra Bandstand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandstand_Promenade "Bandstand Promenade"), Mumbai.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-85)

**Sharmila Tagore** (Bengali:[[ʃɔɾˈmila ˈʈʰakuɾ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Bengali "Help:IPA/Bengali")[](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/5/51/LL-Q9610_%28ben%29-Titodutta-%E0%A6%B6%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BE_%E0%A6%A0%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B0.wav/LL-Q9610_%28ben%29-Titodutta-%E0%A6%B6%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BE_%E0%A6%A0%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B0.wav.mp3 "Play audio")[ⓘ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:LL-Q9610_(ben)-Titodutta-%E0%A6%B6%E0%A6%B0%E0%A7%8D%E0%A6%AE%E0%A6%BF%E0%A6%B2%E0%A6%BE_%E0%A6%A0%E0%A6%BE%E0%A6%95%E0%A7%81%E0%A6%B0.wav "File:LL-Q9610 (ben)-Titodutta-শর্মিলা ঠাকুর.wav"); born 8 December 1944), also known by her married name **Begum Ayesha Sultana**,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-timesofindia.indiatimes.com-1) is an Indian actress whose career has spanned over six decades across [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema") and [Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_West_Bengal "Cinema of West Bengal") films.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-:0-3) In recognition of her contributions to cinema, she was honoured with Commander of [Order of Arts and Letters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_of_Arts_and_Letters "Order of Arts and Letters") by [Government of France](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_France "Government of France") in 1999, and [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan"), India's third highest civilian award, in 2013.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-6) Tagore is also a recipient of two [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards") and a [Filmfare Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award "Filmfare Award").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-7)

Born into the prominent [Tagore family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagore_family "Tagore family"), one of the leading families of [Calcutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta "Calcutta") and a key influence during the [Bengali Renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Renaissance "Bengal Renaissance"), Tagore made her acting debut at age 14 with [Satyajit Ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satyajit_Ray "Satyajit Ray")'s acclaimed Bengali epic drama _[The World of Apu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_World\_of\_Apu "The World of Apu")_ (1959). She went on to collaborate with Ray on numerous other films, including _[Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devi\_(1960\_film) "Devi (1960 film)")_ (1960), _[Nayak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nayak\_(1966\_film) "Nayak (1966 film)")_ (1966), _[Aranyer Din Ratri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aranyer\_Din\_Ratri "Aranyer Din Ratri")_ (1970), and _[Seemabaddha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seemabaddha "Seemabaddha")_ (1971), her other Bengali films over the time included _[Barnali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnali "Barnali")_ (1963), _[Shes Anko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shes\_Anko "Shes Anko")_ (1963), _[Nirjan Saikate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nirjan\_Saikate "Nirjan Saikate")_ (1965), _[Amanush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanush\_(1975\_film) "Amanush (1975 film)")_ (1975), _[Anand Ashram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anand\_Ashram "Anand Ashram")_ (1977), and _[Kalankini Kankabati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalankini\_Kankabati "Kalankini Kankabati")_ (1981); thus establishing herself as one of the most acclaimed actresses of [Bengali cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cinema_of_West_Bengal "Cinema of West Bengal").

Tagore's career further expanded when she ventured into Hindi films with [Shakti Samanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakti_Samanta "Shakti Samanta")'s romance _[Kashmir Ki Kali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashmir\_Ki\_Kali "Kashmir Ki Kali")_ (1964). She established herself as one of the leading actresses of Hindi cinema with films like _[Waqt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waqt\_(1965\_film) "Waqt (1965 film)")_ (1965), _[Anupama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupama\_(1966\_film) "Anupama (1966 film)")_ (1966), _[Devar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devar "Devar")_ (1966), _[An Evening in Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An\_Evening\_in\_Paris "An Evening in Paris")_ (1967), _[Aamne Saamne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aamne\_Samne\_(1967\_film) "Aamne Samne (1967 film)")_ (1967), _[Mere Hamdam Mere Dost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mere\_Hamdam\_Mere\_Dost "Mere Hamdam Mere Dost")_ (1968), _[Satyakam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satyakam "Satyakam")_ (1969), _[Aradhana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aradhana\_(1969\_film) "Aradhana (1969 film)")_ (1969), _[Safar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safar\_(1970\_film) "Safar (1970 film)")_ (1970), _[Amar Prem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amar\_Prem\_(1972\_film) "Amar Prem (1972 film)")_ (1972), _[Daag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daag\_(1973\_film) "Daag (1973 film)")_ (1973), _[Aa Gale Lag Jaa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aa\_Gale\_Lag\_Jaa\_(1973\_film) "Aa Gale Lag Jaa (1973 film)")_ (1973), _[Avishkaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avishkaar "Avishkaar")_ (1974), _[Chupke Chupke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chupke\_Chupke\_(film) "Chupke Chupke (film)")_ (1975), _[Mausam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mausam\_(1975\_film) "Mausam (1975 film)")_ (1975), _[Ek Mahal Ho Sapno Ka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ek\_Mahal\_Ho\_Sapno\_Ka "Ek Mahal Ho Sapno Ka")_ (1975) and _[Namkeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namkeen "Namkeen")_ (1982). She won the [Filmfare Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actress "Filmfare Award for Best Actress") for _Aradhana_ and the [National Film Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actress "National Film Award for Best Actress") for _Mausam_. This was followed by intermittent film appearances in the subsequent decades, including in _[Sunny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny\_(1984\_film) "Sunny (1984 film)")_ (1984), _[Swati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swati\_(1986\_film) "Swati (1986 film)")_ (1986), _[New Delhi Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Delhi\_Times "New Delhi Times")_ (1986), [Mira Nair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mira_Nair "Mira Nair")'s _[Mississippi Masala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi\_Masala "Mississippi Masala")_ (1991) and [Goutam Ghose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goutam_Ghose "Goutam Ghose")'s _[Abar Aranye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abar\_Aranye "Abar Aranye")_ (2002), which won her the [National Film Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "National Film Award for Best Supporting Actress"), _[Shubho Mahurat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shubho\_Mahurat "Shubho Mahurat")_ (2003), and in the Hindi films _[Aashik Awara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aashik\_Awara "Aashik Awara")_ (1993), _[Mann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mann\_(1999\_film) "Mann (1999 film)")_ (1999), _[Viruddh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viruddh "Viruddh")_ (2005), _[Eklavya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eklavya:\_The\_Royal\_Guard "Eklavya: The Royal Guard")_ (2007) and _[Break Ke Baad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Break\_Ke\_Baad "Break Ke Baad")_ (2010). Following a hiatus of 13 years, she made her film comeback with the drama _[Gulmohar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulmohar\_(2023\_film) "Gulmohar (2023 film)")_ (2023) followed by a critically acclaimed performance in _[Puratawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puratawn "Puratawn")_ (2025).[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-8)

Tagore served as the chairperson of the [Central Board of Film Certification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Board_of_Film_Certification "Central Board of Film Certification") from October 2004 to March 2011. In December 2005, she was chosen as a [UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UNICEF_Goodwill_Ambassador "UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-UNICEF-9)

## Early life and background

Sharmila Tagore was born on 8 December 1944 in Cawnpore (now [Kanpur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanpur "Kanpur")), [United Provinces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Provinces_(1937%E2%80%931950) "United Provinces (1937–1950)") to Gitindranath Tagore, a general manager in the [British India Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_India_Corporation "British India Corporation"), and his wife Ira Tagore (née Barua).[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-10) As a member of the aristocratic [Bengali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengalis "Bengalis")[Hindu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengali_Hindus "Bengali Hindus")[Tagore family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagore_family "Tagore family"), she is related to the Nobel laureate [Rabindranath Tagore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabindranath_Tagore "Rabindranath Tagore"), actress [Devika Rani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devika_Rani "Devika Rani") and the painter [Abanindranath Tagore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abanindranath_Tagore "Abanindranath Tagore"). Her mother was of [Assamese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assamese_people "Assamese people") descent and hailed from the [Barua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barua "Barua") family.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-11)[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-13) Gitindranath was the grandson of the noted painter [Gaganendranath Tagore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaganendranath_Tagore "Gaganendranath Tagore"), whose own father Gunendranath had been a first cousin of the laureate.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-tagore_tree-14) In fact, Tagore is more closely related to [Rabindranath Tagore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabindranath_Tagore "Rabindranath Tagore") through her mother: her maternal grandmother, Latika Barua (née Tagore), was the granddaughter of [Rabindranath Tagore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rabindranath_Tagore "Rabindranath Tagore")'s brother, [Dwijendranath Tagore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dwijendranath_Tagore "Dwijendranath Tagore"). Her parents were fourth-cousins.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-tagore_tree-14) Tagore's maternal grandfather (husband of Latika Barua née Tagore) was [Jnanadabhiram Barua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jnanadabhiram_Barua "Jnanadabhiram Barua"), an [Assamese](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assamese_people "Assamese people") Freedom Fighter and Writer who was the First Principal of Earl Law College in [Guwahati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guwahati "Guwahati") (now known as Government Law College), himself the son of the noted social worker [Gunabhiram Barua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunabhiram_Barua "Gunabhiram Barua").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-15)[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-16)

Tagore was the eldest of three daughters and had two younger sisters, the late Oindrila Kunda and Romila Sen. Oindrila was the first in the family to act, and appeared in [Tapan Sinha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapan_Sinha "Tapan Sinha")'s [_Kabuliwala_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabuliwala_(1957_film) "Kabuliwala (1957 film)") (1957) as a child.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-tagore_tree-14)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-17) She later became an international bridge player.

Tagore attended [St. John's Diocesan Girls' Higher Secondary School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/St._John's_Diocesan_Girls'_Higher_Secondary_School "St. John's Diocesan Girls' Higher Secondary School") and [Loreto Convent, Asansol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loreto_Convent,_Asansol "Loreto Convent, Asansol").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-18) She made her film debut when she was a 13-year-old schoolgirl, after which her studies lost priority. Within a short while, her attendance and performance at school suffered, she came to be regarded as a bad influence on her classmates, and was faced with a choice of either doing films or studying further.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-Indian_Expres6_May_2011-19) At that point, her father advised her to move ahead in life, commit herself to a film career and 'give it her all' in order to become successful.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-Indian_Expres6_May_2011-19)

## Career

### Beginnings and Cinematic Emergence (1958–1968)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f2/Ms._Sharmila_Tagore%2C_actress_and_Shri_Saumitra_Chatterjee%2C_actor_at_the_presentation_of_the_film_%E2%80%98Apur_Sansar%E2%80%99%2C_during_the_40th_International_Film_Festival_%28IFFI-2009%29%2C_at_Panaji%2C_Goa_on_November_30%2C_2009_%281%29.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ms._Sharmila_Tagore,_actress_and_Shri_Saumitra_Chatterjee,_actor_at_the_presentation_of_the_film_%E2%80%98Apur_Sansar%E2%80%99,_during_the_40th_International_Film_Festival_(IFFI-2009),_at_Panaji,_Goa_on_November_30,_2009_(1).jpg)

Sharmila Tagore with [Soumitra Chatterjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soumitra_Chatterjee "Soumitra Chatterjee") at _[Apur Sansar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apur\_Sansar\_(The\_World\_of\_Apu) "Apur Sansar (The World of Apu)")_ presentation in 2009

Tagore began her career as an actress in [Satyajit Ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satyajit_Ray "Satyajit Ray")'s Bengali epic drama _[Apur Sansar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_World\_of\_Apu "The World of Apu")_ (1959), as an ill-fated bride.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-Being_Sharmila,_all_through_life-20) In 1960, Ray cast her again in _[Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devi\_(1960\_film) "Devi (1960 film)")_, a film set in 1860 on Hindu orthodoxy and rational reforms, which she considers her favourite film and performance.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-21) She went onto appear in Bengali films _[Shes Anko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shes\_Anko "Shes Anko")_ and _[Nirjan Saikate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nirjan\_Saikate "Nirjan Saikate")_, winning the [IFFI Best Actor Award (Female)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IFFI_Best_Actor_Award_(Female) "IFFI Best Actor Award (Female)") for the latter, alongside [Chhaya Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chhaya_Devi "Chhaya Devi"), [Ruma Guha Thakurta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruma_Guha_Thakurta "Ruma Guha Thakurta"), Renuka Devi and Bharati Devi.[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-22)

Tagore made her Hindi film debut with [Shakti Samanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakti_Samanta "Shakti Samanta")'s musical romance _[Kashmir Ki Kali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kashmir\_Ki\_Kali "Kashmir Ki Kali")_ (1964) alongside [Shammi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shammi_Kapoor "Shammi Kapoor"). She and Samanta collaborated on several of his later films, including the romantic thriller _[An Evening in Paris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/An\_Evening\_in\_Paris "An Evening in Paris")_ (1967) again opposite Kapoor. With the film, she became the first Indian actress to appear in a swimsuit,[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-23)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-Being_Sharmila,_all_through_life-20)[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-Rashtriya_Sahara_page_28-25)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-avi-27) which established Tagore as a [sex symbol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_symbol "Sex symbol") in Hindi films.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-29) While the scene in the film is often referred to as 'the bikini scene', Tagore's swimwear is actually a one piece. However, she did pose in a bikini for the cover of _[Filmfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare "Filmfare")_ magazine in 1966.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-30)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-Rashtriya_Sahara_page_28-25)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-33) But, when she was the chairperson of the [Central Board of Film Certification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Board_of_Film_Certification "Central Board of Film Certification") 36 years later, she expressed concerns about the increased use of bikinis in Indian films.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-34)

Tagore went on to appear in films such as _[Waqt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waqt\_(1965\_film) "Waqt (1965 film)")_ (1965) opposite [Shashi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor "Shashi Kapoor"), _[Anupama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anupama\_(1966\_film) "Anupama (1966 film)")_ (1966) opposite [Dharmendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharmendra "Dharmendra"), _[Devar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Devar "Devar")_ (1966) opposite [Dharmendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharmendra "Dharmendra"), _[Sawan Ki Ghata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawan\_Ki\_Ghata "Sawan Ki Ghata")_ (1966) opposite [Manoj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoj_Kumar "Manoj Kumar"), _[Aamne Saamne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aamne\_Samne\_(1967\_film) "Aamne Samne (1967 film)")_ (1967) opposite [Shashi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor "Shashi Kapoor"), _[Mere Hamdam Mere Dost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mere\_Hamdam\_Mere\_Dost "Mere Hamdam Mere Dost")_ (1968) opposite [Dharmendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharmendra "Dharmendra") and the Bengali film _[Nayak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nayak\_(1966\_film) "Nayak (1966 film)")_ (1966) opposite [Uttam Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uttam_Kumar "Uttam Kumar").[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-35)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-36) Her performance in _Anupama_ proved to be her breakthrough in Hindi cinema.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-37)

### Commercial success and stardom (1969–1979)

The 1970s marked the most successful period of Tagore's career with a string of critical and commercial successes. She worked alongside [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna") on several films including [_Aradhana_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aradhana_(1969_film) "Aradhana (1969 film)") (1969), [_Safar_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Safar_(1970_film) "Safar (1970 film)") (1970), _[Chhoti Bahu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chhoti\_Bahu "Chhoti Bahu")_ (1971), _[Amar Prem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amar\_Prem\_(1972\_film) "Amar Prem (1972 film)")_ (1971), [_Raja Rani_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raja_Rani_(1973_film) "Raja Rani (1973 film)") (1973), [_Daag_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daag_(1973_film) "Daag (1973 film)") (1973) and _[Avishkaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Avishkaar "Avishkaar")_ (1974), [_Maalik_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maalik_(1972_film) "Maalik (1972 film)") (1972).[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-40) She won the [Filmfare Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actress "Filmfare Award for Best Actress") for _Aradhana_, and was nominated for _Safar_, _Amar Prem_ and _Daag_.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-41)[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-42) She was paired opposite [Dharmendra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharmendra "Dharmendra") in _[Satyakam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satyakam "Satyakam")_ (1969),_[Yakeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yakeen\_(1969\_film) "Yakeen (1969 film)")_ (1969), _[Chupke Chupke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chupke\_Chupke\_(film) "Chupke Chupke (film)")_ (1975), and _[Ek Mahal Ho Sapno Ka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ek\_Mahal\_Ho\_Sapno\_Ka "Ek Mahal Ho Sapno Ka")_ (1975).[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-43)

Tagore teamed up again with [Shashi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor "Shashi Kapoor") for _[Suhana Safar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suhana\_Safar "Suhana Safar")_ (1970), _[Aa Gale Lag Jaa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aa\_Gale\_Lag\_Jaa\_(1973\_film) "Aa Gale Lag Jaa (1973 film)")_ (1973), and _[Paap Aur Punya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paap\_Aur\_Punya "Paap Aur Punya")_ (1974). She also paired with [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") in _[Faraar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faraar\_(1975\_film) "Faraar (1975 film)")_ (1975) and _[Besharam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Besharam\_(1978\_film) "Besharam (1978 film)")_ (1978).

In [Gulzar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar_(lyricist) "Gulzar (lyricist)")'s _[Mausam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mausam\_(1975\_film) "Mausam (1975 film)")_ (1975), Tagore starred alongside [Sanjeev Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjeev_Kumar "Sanjeev Kumar"), earning earned her first [National Film Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actress "National Film Award for Best Actress"), and her fifth nomination for the Filmfare Award for Best Actress.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-auto-44) During this time, she also worked with [Uttam Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uttam_Kumar "Uttam Kumar") in [_Amanush_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amanush_(1975_film) "Amanush (1975 film)") (1975), _[Anand Ashram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anand\_Ashram "Anand Ashram")_ (1977) and _[Dooriyaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dooriyaan "Dooriyaan")_ (1979).

Tagore's other films during this period included _[Ek Se Badhkar Ek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ek\_Se\_Badhkar\_Ek\_(1976\_film) "Ek Se Badhkar Ek (1976 film)")_ (1976), _[Tyaag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tyaag\_(1977\_film) "Tyaag (1977 film)")_ (1977), which she also co-produced, and the Malayalam film _[Chuvanna Chirakukal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chuvanna\_Chirakukal "Chuvanna Chirakukal")_ (1978) among others.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-46)

### Further success and sporadic work (1980–2010)

In the 1980s, Tagore appeared in _[Kalankini Kankabati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalankini\_Kankabati "Kalankini Kankabati")_ (1981), _[Namkeen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namkeen "Namkeen")_ (1982), _[New Delhi Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Delhi\_Times "New Delhi Times")_ (1986) and _[Swati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swati\_(1986\_film) "Swati (1986 film)")_ (1986).[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-47)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-48) She reunited with Dharmendra in the film _[Sunny](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny\_(1984\_film) "Sunny (1984 film)")_ (1984), which also featured Dharmendra's son [Sunny Deol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sunny_Deol "Sunny Deol") in the lead role. Her performance in the film earned her a nomination for the [Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress").

Tagore starred in the Bengali action film _[Protidan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protidan "Protidan")_ (1983) opposite [Naseeruddin Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naseeruddin_Shah "Naseeruddin Shah"), and [Mira Nair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mira_Nair "Mira Nair")'s interracial romantic drama _[Mississippi Masala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mississippi\_Masala "Mississippi Masala")_ (1991).[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-49) She also appeared in supporting roles in _[Ghar Bazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghar\_Bazar "Ghar Bazar")_ (1998) and _[Mann](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mann\_(1999\_film) "Mann (1999 film)")_ (1999). She also appeared in two television shows, _[Katha Sagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Katha\_Sagar "Katha Sagar")_ (1986) for [DD National](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DD_National "DD National") and _Zindagi_ (1999) for [Star Plus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Plus "Star Plus").[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-50)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-51)

Tagore was cast in her son [Saif Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saif_Ali_Khan "Saif Ali Khan") in his debut film _[Aashik Awara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aashik\_Awara "Aashik Awara")_ (1993) and the action drama _[Eklavya: The Royal Guard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eklavya:\_The\_Royal\_Guard "Eklavya: The Royal Guard")_ (2007). She appeared in supporting roles in the musical romantic drama _[Dhadkan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dhadkan\_(2000\_film) "Dhadkan (2000 film)")_ (2000) and _[Abar Aranye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abar\_Aranye "Abar Aranye")_ (2003), the latter of which earned her the [National Film Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "National Film Award for Best Supporting Actress").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-52) She also received critical acclaim for her performance in _[Shubho Mahurat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shubho\_Mahurat "Shubho Mahurat")_ (2003).

Tagore appeared in family drama _[Virruddh... Family Comes First](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viruddh "Viruddh")_ (2005) alongside Bachchan, earning her sixth nomination for the Filmfare Award for Best Actress.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]
