From 2007 to 2009, Tagore appeared in films such as _[Fool & Final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fool\_&\_Final "Fool & Final")_ (2007), _[Tasveer 8*10](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tasveer\_8*10 "Tasveer 8*10")_ (2009), _[Antaheen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antaheen "Antaheen")_ (2009) and the Marathi film _[Samaantar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samaantar "Samaantar")_ (2009).[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-The_Hindu-53) In 2009, she served on the jury at the [62nd Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2009_Cannes_Film_Festival "2009 Cannes Film Festival").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-SharmilaCannes-54) She played a supporting role in the romantic comedy-drama _[Break Ke Baad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Break\_Ke\_Baad "Break Ke Baad")_ (2010)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-55) before embarking on an acting hiatus.

### Return to Cinema and acclaimed performances (2023 to Present)

Tagore made her comeback after a 13-year hiatus with the drama _[Gulmohar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulmohar\_(2023\_film) "Gulmohar (2023 film)")_ (2023), which released on [Disney+ Hotstar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disney+_Hotstar "Disney+ Hotstar").[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-hindustantimes.com-56) The film earned her critical acclaim, with the _[Hindustan Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindustan\_Times "Hindustan Times")_ noting that, "The elegance and poise Tagore exudes are remarkable. Her dialogue delivery, gestures, body language, emotions, everything looks just so effortless even after a long hiatus." _[India Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India\_Today "India Today")_ also opined that, "Tagore is always a joy to watch on screen. And, what a comeback!"[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-57)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-58) Her performance earned her the [Filmfare OTT Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_OTT_Awards "Filmfare OTT Awards") for Best Actress Critics – Web Original Film, in addition to a nomination for Best Actress – Web Original Film.[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-59)

In 2024, Tagore returned to Marathi films with _Outhouse_ alongside [Mohan Agashe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohan_Agashe "Mohan Agashe"), where she played a loving grandmother.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-60) Devesh Sharma of _[Filmfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare "Filmfare")_ noted, "Tagore brings warmth, wisdom, and a spark of curiosity to Aadima, portraying her as a nuanced blend of strength and vulnerability."[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-61) Tagore made her comeback to Bengali films after 14 years with Suman Ghosh's _[Puratawn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puratawn "Puratawn")_ (2025).

## Personal life

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/96/Soha_Ali_Khan_Sharmila_Tagore_still1.jpg/250px-Soha_Ali_Khan_Sharmila_Tagore_still1.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Soha_Ali_Khan_Sharmila_Tagore_still1.jpg)

Tagore with her daughter [Soha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soha_Ali_Khan "Soha Ali Khan") at the premiere of _[Khoya Khoya Chand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khoya\_Khoya\_Chand "Khoya Khoya Chand")_

Tagore [converted to Islam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Converted_to_Islam "Converted to Islam"), changed her name to Begum Ayesha Sultana,[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-timesofindia.indiatimes.com-1)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-62) and married [Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mansoor_Ali_Khan_Pataudi "Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi"), the titular [Nawab of Pataudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nawab_of_Pataudi "Nawab of Pataudi") and [Bhopal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nawabs_of_Bhopal "Nawabs of Bhopal") and former captain of the [Indian cricket team](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cricket_team "Indian cricket team"), on 27 December 1968.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-63)[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-64) They had three children: [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bollywood "Bollywood") actor [Saif Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saif_Ali_Khan "Saif Ali Khan") (born 1970); [Saba Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saba_Ali_Khan "Saba Ali Khan") (born 1976),[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-65) a jewellery designer; and [Soha Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soha_Ali_Khan "Soha Ali Khan") (born 1978), a Bollywood actress and TV personality. Mansoor Ali Khan Pataudi died at age 70 on 22 September 2011.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-66)

From 1991 to 2004, [Saif](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saif_Ali_Khan "Saif Ali Khan") was married to actress [Amrita Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amrita_Singh "Amrita Singh"). They have two children, daughter [Sara Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sara_Ali_Khan "Sara Ali Khan") (born 1995) and son [Ibrahim Ali Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ibrahim_Ali_Khan_(actor) "Ibrahim Ali Khan (actor)") (born 2001), both actors.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-67) His second marriage is to actress [Kareena Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kareena_Kapoor "Kareena Kapoor") in 2012 with whom he has two sons, Taimur Ali Khan (born 2016) and Jeh Ali Khan (born 2021).[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-68)[Soha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soha_Ali_Khan "Soha Ali Khan") married actor [Kunal Khemu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunal_Khemu "Kunal Khemu") in 2015, and has a daughter Inaaya Naumi Khemmu (born 2017).[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-69)

## Public image and legacy

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/15/Sharmila_T_Lux-Award_2016.jpg/250px-Sharmila_T_Lux-Award_2016.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sharmila_T_Lux-Award_2016.jpg)

Tagore in 2016

Tagore was the highest paid Indian actress in the 1970s, and is considered an accomplished [Indian cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cinema "Indian cinema") veteran.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-71) Surendra Kumar of _[The Sunday Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Sunday\_Guardian "The Sunday Guardian")_ considers her to be an actress "ahead of her time" for balancing "the serious persona of realist Bengali films, and the Bollywood persona of films with song-and-dance sequences focused on success at the box office."[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-aheadoftime-72) She has received widespread critical acclaim for her on-screen work, both nationally and internationally. During the introduction of the [2025 Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Cannes_Film_Festival "2025 Cannes Film Festival") screening of _Aranyer Din Ratri_, American filmmaker [Wes Anderson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wes_Anderson "Wes Anderson") recalled watching the film 25 years ago "in a very strangely translated, blurry, scratchy, pirated [DVD](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DVD "DVD") from a little Bollywood shop in [New Jersey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Jersey "New Jersey")." He described Tagore's performance in _Aranyer Din Ratri_ as "mysterious, cerebral, mesmerising."[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-:1-73)[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-KaelPerfect-74)

Unlike most of her contemporaries in the 1960s, Tagore struck a convenient balance playing both glamorous and homely women on screen. She "explored roles beyond the stereotypical" in an era where women were rarely offered an opportunity to be more than "just a pretty appendage to the hero."[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-:1-73) Her wide range of complex female characters often circumvented the [damsel in distress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Damsel_in_distress "Damsel in distress") tropes, defying Indian societal norms and capturing a version of womanhood that is flawed but purposeful.[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-75)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-SharmilaT-77) According to Nandini Balial of [Roger Ebert](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/RogerEbert.com "RogerEbert.com"), she "redefined what an Indian woman could do in a film," and "altered the cinematic landscape for leading ladies." Balial goes on to say that Tagore's women epitomised that "being demure didn't mean being spineless, [and that] emotional devastation wasn't a death sentence."[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-:0-3) Filmfare considered her portrayal of a foul-mouthed shrew-ish [sex-worker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_worker "Sex worker") in _Mausam_ as one of the most iconic Bollywood performances.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-80_Iconic-78)

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7b/Sharmila_Tagore.jpg/250px-Sharmila_Tagore.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Sharmila_Tagore.jpg)

Tagore in 2018

Bucking the Indian film industry's expectations from actresses, Tagore wore a one-piece swimsuit for her 1967 film _An Evening In Paris_. She was the first Bollywood actress to have done so, paving the way for [Dimple Kapadia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dimple_Kapadia "Dimple Kapadia") in _Bobby_ (1973), [Zeenat Aman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeenat_Aman "Zeenat Aman") in _[Qurbani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qurbani\_(film) "Qurbani (film)")_ (1980), and [Parveen Babi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parveen_Babi "Parveen Babi") in _[Yeh Nazdeekiyan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeh\_Nazdeekiyan "Yeh Nazdeekiyan")_ (1982).[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-79) Her 1969 Filmfare magazine cover, where Tagore poses in a two-piece bikini, was publicly labelled as "obscene" and "attention-seeking." She said her _An Evening In Paris_ director [Shakti Samanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakti_Samanta "Shakti Samanta") called her after the magazine hit the stands and said,"If you want to be in the public eye, this is not the way to go." He also asked Tagore, who was in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") at the time, to return to India immediately. Tagore was "really hurt" by the cover being interpreted as her trying to "be [upwardly mobile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_mobility "Social mobility")" and "catch eyeballs."[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_] In a televised interview with [Karan Johar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karan_Johar "Karan Johar"), she confirmed that "questions were asked in the [Indian] Parliament" following the controversy, and she strategically chose the wife-mother role in _Aradhana_ as her next on-screen appearance.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-80)

With her voluminous hairdos and [chiffon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiffon_(fabric) "Chiffon (fabric)") floral-print [_sarees_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sari "Sari"), Tagore's sense of fashion seamlessly blended traditional elegance with modern glamour. Numerous Indian actresses have gone to emulate her retro-vintage style in recent times, including [Anushka Sharma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anushka_Sharma "Anushka Sharma") for [Bombay Velvet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bombay_Velvet "Bombay Velvet"), [Preity Zinta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preity_Zinta "Preity Zinta") for _[Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rab\_Ne\_Bana\_Di\_Jodi "Rab Ne Bana Di Jodi")_, and [Deepika Padukone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepika_Padukone "Deepika Padukone") in [Om Shanti Om](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Om_Shanti_Om "Om Shanti Om").[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-81)[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-83) Film historian Sanjay Mukhopadhyay said that her "most significant contribution to Indian cinema is a sense of dignity and grace—after [Waheeda Rehman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waheeda_Rehman "Waheeda Rehman"), she was the only actress of her time who exuded this." Mukhopadhyay adds that with a "strong Tagore lineage coupled with the [Pataudi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pataudi_family "Pataudi family")_gharana_ (family dynasty)" she was a "bourgeois star with a biography" who "occupied a cultural space beyond the reach of commoner—she could be looked at, but not possessed."[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-Sharmila'slife-84)

Tagore was inducted into the [Bollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walk_of_the_Stars "Walk of the Stars") at [Bandra Bandstand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandstand_Promenade "Bandstand Promenade"), Mumbai.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmila_Tagore#cite_note-85)

**Kamini Kaushal** (born **Uma Kashyap**; 24 February 1927 – 13 November 2025) was an Indian actress who worked in [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi") films and television in a career spanning seven decades. She is regarded as one of the finest actresses of [Hindi cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-1) She is noted for her roles in films such as _[Neecha Nagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neecha\_Nagar "Neecha Nagar")_ (1946), which won the 1946 [Palme d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palme_d'Or "Palme d'Or") at the [Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival "Cannes Film Festival") and _[Biraj Bahu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biraj\_Bahu "Biraj Bahu")_ (1954), which won her the [Filmfare Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actress "Filmfare Award for Best Actress") in 1956.

Kaushal played the lead heroine in films from 1946 to 1963, wherein her roles in _[Do Bhai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do\_Bhai\_(1947\_film) "Do Bhai (1947 film)")_ (1947), _[Shaheed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaheed\_(1948\_film) "Shaheed (1948 film)")_ (1948), _[Nadiya Ke Paar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadiya\_Ke\_Paar\_(1948\_film) "Nadiya Ke Paar (1948 film)")_ (1948), _[Ziddi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ziddi\_(1948\_film) "Ziddi (1948 film)")_ (1948), _[Shabnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabnam\_(1949\_film) "Shabnam (1949 film)")_ (1949), _[Paras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paras\_(1949\_film) "Paras (1949 film)")_ (1949), _[Namoona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namoona "Namoona")_ (1949), _[Arzoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arzoo\_(1950\_film) "Arzoo (1950 film)")_ (1950), _Jhanjar_ (1953), _Aabroo_ (1956), _[Bade Sarkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bade\_Sarkar "Bade Sarkar")_ (1957), _[Jailor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jailor\_(1958\_film) "Jailor (1958 film)")_ (1958), _Night Club_ (1958) and _[Godaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godaan "Godaan")_ (1963) are considered her career's best performances. She played character roles from 1963 onwards, and was critically acclaimed for her performance in [_Shaheed_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaheed_(1965_film) "Shaheed (1965 film)") (1965). She appeared in three of Rajesh Khanna's films, namely _[Do Raaste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do\_Raaste "Do Raaste")_ (1969), [_Prem Nagar_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem_Nagar_(1974_film) "Prem Nagar (1974 film)") (1974), _[Maha Chor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maha\_Chor "Maha Chor")_ (1976), in [_Anhonee_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anhonee_(1973_film) "Anhonee (1973 film)") (1973) with [Sanjeev Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjeev_Kumar "Sanjeev Kumar") and in eight films with [Manoj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoj_Kumar "Manoj Kumar") namely _Shaheed_, _[Upkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upkar "Upkar")_ (1967), _[Purab Aur Paschim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purab\_Aur\_Paschim "Purab Aur Paschim")_ (1970), _[Shor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shor\_(film) "Shor (film)")_ (1972), _[Roti Kapda Aur Makaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roti\_Kapda\_Aur\_Makaan "Roti Kapda Aur Makaan")_ (1974), _[Sanyasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanyasi\_(1975\_film) "Sanyasi (1975 film)")_ (1975), _[Dus Numbri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dus\_Numbri "Dus Numbri")_ (1976) and _[Santosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santosh\_(1989\_film) "Santosh (1989 film)")_ (1989).

From the 1990s, Kaushal only sporadically appeared in films. She latterly appeared in _[Chennai Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai\_Express "Chennai Express")_ (2013) and the romantic drama _[Kabir Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabir\_Singh "Kabir Singh")_ (2019), both of which rank among the [highest grossing Indian films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_Indian_films "List of highest-grossing Indian films"), winning the [Screen Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Screen Award for Best Supporting Actress") and a nomination for the [Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress") for the latter. She made her final film appearance with a cameo in _[Laal Singh Chaddha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laal\_Singh\_Chaddha "Laal Singh Chaddha")_ in 2022.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kamini_Kaushal&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Kamini Kaushal was born in [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore") on 24 February 1927.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-telegraph2014-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-3) She was the youngest of two brothers and three sisters.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Filmfare2014-4) She was the daughter of [Shiv Ram Kashyap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shiv_Ram_Kashyap "Shiv Ram Kashyap"), professor of botany, [University of Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_Punjab "University of the Punjab") at [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore"), [British India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") (present-day [Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan "Pakistan")), and used to have a house in Chaubarji area of Lahore. Kashyap is widely regarded as the father of Indian botany.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-5) Her father was a distinguished botanist who discovered six species of plants. She was only seven when her father died on 26 November 1934.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-telegraph2014-2) She did her B.A. (honours) in English literature from [Government College in Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_College_University,_Lahore "Government College University, Lahore"). She got an offer to act in films through [Chetan Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chetan_Anand_(director) "Chetan Anand (director)") in 1946 with _Neecha Nagar_.

Talking about her teenage years, she said in an interview, "I had no time to fool. I didn't have any crush. I was busy swimming, riding, skating and doing radio plays on Akashwani, for which I was paid Rs 10."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Filmfare2014-4) When her elder sister died in a car accident,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Filmfare2014-4) leaving behind two daughters, Kaushal had to marry her brother-in-law, B.S. Sood in 1948. She set up home in Bombay where her husband was a chief engineer in Bombay Port Trust.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-telegraph2014-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Filmfare2014-4) Her elder sister's daughters are Kumkum Somani and Kavita Sahni. Kumkum Somani has written a book for children on Gandhi's philosophy and Kavita Sahni is an artist.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-telegraph2014-2) Kamini had three sons after 1955, Rahul, Vidur and Shravan.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Filmfare2014-4)

In the 1950s, the couple lived in a spacious manor-type house "Gateside" in [Mazagaon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazagaon "Mazagaon"), which was allotted to her husband by BPT.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-6)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kamini_Kaushal&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Kamini had been a stage actress in [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi") during her college days from 1942 to 1945. She worked as a radio child artist with the name "Uma" in [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore") before the Partition, from 1937 to 1940.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Rediff2007-7) She said in an interview about whether she wanted to be an actress in her childhood: "I come from a very intellectual family. My dad, S. R. Kashyap, was a professor at [Government College, Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_College_University,_Lahore "Government College University, Lahore") and the President of the Science Congress. He'd written about 50 books on botany. Growing up, our family concentrated more on knowledge, but he never deterred us from doing anything we wanted as long as it was positive."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-8) Though she had no dreams of joining the film industry while being in college, she was a fan of actor Ashok Kumar. Once she said in an interview: "We were to perform for the war relief fund in college. Ashok Kumar and Leela Chitins were the chief guests. After the show we went to meet him. I thought of having some fun. As he stood talking to the students, I pulled his hair from behind."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Filmfare2014-4)[Chetan Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chetan_Anand_(director) "Chetan Anand (director)") gave her the role of the leading heroine in his film _[Neecha Nagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neecha\_Nagar "Neecha Nagar")_. This movie was done by her before marriage and released in 1946.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Rediff2007-7) She quoted in an interview, when asked about why her name was changed from Uma to Kamini: "Chetan's wife Uma Anand was also part of the film. My name also being Uma, he wanted a different name for me. I asked him to give me a name beginning with 'K' to match with the names of my daughters Kumkum and Kavita."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Filmfare2014-4) She won an award at the Montreal Film Festival for her performance in her debut film.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Kamini_Kaushal,_legend-9) She quoted in an interview about how she got her debut film: "Ravi Shankar was new, he had not done music for anybody. It was Zohra Segal's debut. Uma Anand (Chetan's wife) was with us in college — we were together. Chetan had been teaching at The Doon School and got to me through my brother.".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-telegraph2014-2)

After _Neecha Nagar_, she returned to Lahore, but offers started coming in, hence she used to come for shooting from Lahore. After her sudden marriage in 1947, she settled in Bombay with her husband. She became the first leading heroine to continue working as lead film heroine after her marriage as well. Kamini was one of the first well educated heroines (BA in English) in Hindi cinema.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Kamini_Kaushal,_legend-9) She learnt [Bharatnatyam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatnatyam "Bharatnatyam") at Mumbai's Sri Rajarajeswari Bharata Natya Kala Mandir, where Guru T. K. Mahalingam Pillai, doyen among nattuvanars taught.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-10) Since 1948, Kamini Kaushal worked with all the top leading men of her time, such as [Ashok Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashok_Kumar "Ashok Kumar"), [Raj Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Kapoor "Raj Kapoor"), [Dev Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dev_Anand "Dev Anand"), [Raaj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raaj_Kumar "Raaj Kumar") and [Dilip Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dilip_Kumar "Dilip Kumar").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In every film starring her as lead heroine, except when opposite Ashok Kumar, in the period 1947 to 1955, her name used to appear first in the credits before the leading hero's name appeared. Her pairing opposite Dilip Kumar was popular with audiences with box office hits such as _[Shaheed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaheed\_(1948\_film) "Shaheed (1948 film)")_ (1948), _Pugree_, _Nadiya Ke Paar_ (1949), _Shabnam_ (1949) and _Arzoo_ (1950)).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-red-11) The popularity as an actress increased with Filmistan's _Do Bhai_ (1947), aided by Geeta Roy's impassioned singing of songs such as "Mera sundar sapna", which, incidentally, was shot in a single take.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Kamini_Kaushal,_legend-9) Kamini was paired opposite Dev Anand in his very first success, Bombay Talkies' production _Ziddi_ (1948), a light romance. The pair followed this up with _[Namoona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namoona "Namoona")_. Kamini played the third angle to the Dev-Suraiya pair in _Shayar_. In Raj Kapoor's directorial debut _Aag_ (1948), she did a cameo as one of his three heroines (Nargis and Nigar were the other two), whose relationship with the hero doesn't fructify. She also starred with Raj Kapoor in _Jail Yatra_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Kamini_Kaushal,_legend-9)

Kamini Kaushal was the first lead heroine for whom [Lata Mangeshkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lata_Mangeshkar "Lata Mangeshkar") ever sang for and it was for the film _Ziddi_ in 1948. Kamini quoted in an interview: "Lata sang for me in _Ziddi_ for the first time. That was the first time she sang for the leading lady in a film. Before that, she sang for actresses in supporting roles. Shamshad Begum and Surinder Kaur — whose voices had more bass — used to sing my songs. On the music credits on the record, Lata's name was not mentioned. Instead, it was mentioned that Asha sang the songs — Asha was my screen name (in the film _Ziddi_). That's why people thought I had sung it.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-12) The playback singers - Kishore Kumar and Lata Mangeshkar recorded their first duet - "Ye Kaun Aya Re" together in the 1948 film _Ziddi_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-13)

Her other successful films as lead heroine in films from 1946 to 1963 include _[Paras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paras\_(1949\_film) "Paras (1949 film)")_ (1949), _Namoona_, _Jhanjar_, _Aabru_, _Night Club_, _[Jailor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jailor\_(1958\_film) "Jailor (1958 film)")_, _[Bade Sarkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bade\_Sarkar "Bade Sarkar")_, _Bada Bhai_, _Poonam_ and _[Godaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godaan "Godaan")_. Kamini became a producer and signed on then-matinee idol Ashok Kumar in _Poonam_ and _Night Club_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Rediff2007-7) She did lighthearted roles in _Chalis Baba Ek Chor_ (1954) and also did serious tragedy genre roles in _Aas_, _Ansoo_ and _Jailor_. In the Sohrab Modi-directed _Jailor_ (1958), Kamini gave a goosebump-raising performance as Modi's wife, who is pushed towards adultery by his ruthless tyranny.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Kamini_Kaushal,_legend-9) Trilok Jetley, who adopted Premchand's famous story _Godaan_ on screen, put his film on hold, while Kamini was pregnant with her second child, because he wanted to capitalise on the softness in her voice. Pandit Ravi Shankar composed the score for her first (_Neecha Nagar_ in 1946) and last (_Godaan_ in 1963) films as a heroine.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Kamini_Kaushal,_legend-9)

In 1965, she moved to playing character roles with a film called _[Shaheed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaheed\_(1965\_film) "Shaheed (1965 film)")_. She made the transition from playing leading heroine roles to character roles very easily. Her performances were appreciated in [_Waris_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waris_(1969_film) "Waris (1969 film)"), _[Vishwas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishwas "Vishwas")_, [_Yakeen_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yakeen_(1969_film) "Yakeen (1969 film)"), _[Aadmi Aur Insaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aadmi\_Aur\_Insaan "Aadmi Aur Insaan")_, _[Uphaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uphaar "Uphaar")_, _[Qaid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qaid\_(film) "Qaid (film)")_, _[Bhanwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhanwar\_(film) "Bhanwar (film)")_, _[Tangewala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tangewala "Tangewala")_ and _[Heeralaal Pannalaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heeralaal\_Pannalaal\_(1978\_film) "Heeralaal Pannalaal (1978 film)")_. As a character artist she was a fixture in seven [Manoj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoj_Kumar "Manoj Kumar") films - _[Shaheed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaheed\_(1965\_film) "Shaheed (1965 film)")_, _[Upkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upkar "Upkar")_, _[Purab Aur Paschim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purab\_Aur\_Paschim "Purab Aur Paschim")_, _[Sanyasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanyasi\_(1975\_film) "Sanyasi (1975 film)")_, _[Shor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shor\_(film) "Shor (film)")_, _[Roti Kapda Aur Makaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roti\_Kapda\_Aur\_Makaan "Roti Kapda Aur Makaan")_, _[Dus Numbari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dus\_Numbari "Dus Numbari")_ and _[Santosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santosh\_(1989\_film) "Santosh (1989 film)")_ (1989). Kaushal had a long stint in films with releases till 2014.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-14) She stunned audiences by playing a mercenary vamp with aplomb in the film [_Anhonee_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anhonee_(1973_film) "Anhonee (1973 film)") (1973).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Kamini_Kaushal,_legend-9) Kamini Kaushal played mother to [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna") in [_Prem Nagar_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem_Nagar_(1974_film) "Prem Nagar (1974 film)") in 1974, and in _[Maha Chor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maha\_Chor "Maha Chor")_ in 1976, and as sister in law to Khanna in _[Do Raaste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do\_Raaste "Do Raaste")_.

Dilip Kumar, in his biography, has admitted his attraction to her while they acted in films together, but Kamini rejected his proposal as she was already married to her elder sister's widower and was taking care of her elder sister's kids.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-15) Dilip said that she was his first love.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-17) Kamini quoted in an interview on this: "We were both shattered. We were very happy with each other. We shared a great rapport. But what to do? That's life. I can't dump people and say 'Enough now, I'm going!' I had taken on the girls. I wouldn't be able to show my face to my sister. My husband, a fine human being, understood why it happened. Everyone falls in love."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Filmfare2014-4)

She made a popular puppet show broadcast on the national channel at the time, "Doordarshan", which ran for a year (1989 to 1991), and was the first such children's series in Hindi.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-18) She stepped into writing children's stories. Her stories used to be published in the children's magazine _Paraag_, featuring the antics of 'Bunty', and 'Chotbhai' and 'Motabhai' – who were all loosely based on her own son and his cousin contemporaries. She dabbled in television doing serials such as _Chand Sitare_ on [Doordarshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doordarshan "Doordarshan"). In 1986, Kaushal made an animation film, _Meri Pari_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

She appeared in _[The Jewel in the Crown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jewel\_in\_the\_Crown\_(TV\_series) "The Jewel in the Crown (TV series)")_ (1984), a popular British television serial, as Aunt Shalini.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-telegraph2014-2)

Kaushal worked in the highly popular serial _Shanno Ki Shaadi_, on [StarPlus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/StarPlus "StarPlus").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-19) She played Bebe, the grandmother of Shanno, the main protagonist played by [Divya Dutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divya_Dutta "Divya Dutta"). She also acted in Sri Adhikari Brothers' TV Serial _Waqt Ki Raftaar_ (DD National).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

She said in an interview: "I, along with only few Indian heroines like [Saroja Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saroja_Devi "Saroja Devi"), [Bhanumathi Ramakrishna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhanumathi_Ramakrishna "Bhanumathi Ramakrishna"), [Sowcar Janaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sowcar_Janaki "Sowcar Janaki"), [Mala Sinha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mala_Sinha "Mala Sinha"), [Moushumi Chatterjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moushumi_Chatterjee "Moushumi Chatterjee"), [Padmini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padmini_(actress) "Padmini (actress)") and Sharmila Tagore were the few who got married early and had success in the film industry even after our marriages as well as led a happy married life."[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Since the 1990s, she only occasionally appeared in films such as _[Gumrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gumrah\_(1993\_film) "Gumrah (1993 film)")_ (1993), _[Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Har\_Dil\_Jo\_Pyar\_Karega "Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega")_ (2000), _[Chori Chori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chori\_Chori\_(2003\_film) "Chori Chori (2003 film)")_ (2003), _[Chennai Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai\_Express "Chennai Express")_ (2013) and _[Kabir Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabir\_Singh "Kabir Singh")_ (2019). Her final film appearance was a cameo in _[Laal Singh Chaddha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laal\_Singh\_Chaddha "Laal Singh Chaddha")_ in 2022.

## Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kamini_Kaushal&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Death")]

Kaushal died in [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai") on 13 November 2025, at the age of 98.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-21)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kamini_Kaushal&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Legacy")]

One of the highest paid actresses of the late 1940s, Kaushal appeared in _[Box Office India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box\_Office\_India "Box Office India")_'s "Top Actresses" list twice, 1947 and 1948.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-25) In 2022, she was placed in _[Outlook India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlook\_India "Outlook India")_'s "75 Best Bollywood Actresses" list.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-26)

**Kamini Kaushal** (born **Uma Kashyap**; 24 February 1927 – 13 November 2025) was an Indian actress who worked in [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi") films and television in a career spanning seven decades. She is regarded as one of the finest actresses of [Hindi cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-1) She is noted for her roles in films such as _[Neecha Nagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neecha\_Nagar "Neecha Nagar")_ (1946), which won the 1946 [Palme d'Or](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palme_d'Or "Palme d'Or") at the [Cannes Film Festival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannes_Film_Festival "Cannes Film Festival") and _[Biraj Bahu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biraj\_Bahu "Biraj Bahu")_ (1954), which won her the [Filmfare Award for Best Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Actress "Filmfare Award for Best Actress") in 1956.

Kaushal played the lead heroine in films from 1946 to 1963, wherein her roles in _[Do Bhai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do\_Bhai\_(1947\_film) "Do Bhai (1947 film)")_ (1947), _[Shaheed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaheed\_(1948\_film) "Shaheed (1948 film)")_ (1948), _[Nadiya Ke Paar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nadiya\_Ke\_Paar\_(1948\_film) "Nadiya Ke Paar (1948 film)")_ (1948), _[Ziddi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ziddi\_(1948\_film) "Ziddi (1948 film)")_ (1948), _[Shabnam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabnam\_(1949\_film) "Shabnam (1949 film)")_ (1949), _[Paras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paras\_(1949\_film) "Paras (1949 film)")_ (1949), _[Namoona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namoona "Namoona")_ (1949), _[Arzoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arzoo\_(1950\_film) "Arzoo (1950 film)")_ (1950), _Jhanjar_ (1953), _Aabroo_ (1956), _[Bade Sarkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bade\_Sarkar "Bade Sarkar")_ (1957), _[Jailor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jailor\_(1958\_film) "Jailor (1958 film)")_ (1958), _Night Club_ (1958) and _[Godaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godaan "Godaan")_ (1963) are considered her career's best performances. She played character roles from 1963 onwards, and was critically acclaimed for her performance in [_Shaheed_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaheed_(1965_film) "Shaheed (1965 film)") (1965). She appeared in three of Rajesh Khanna's films, namely _[Do Raaste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do\_Raaste "Do Raaste")_ (1969), [_Prem Nagar_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem_Nagar_(1974_film) "Prem Nagar (1974 film)") (1974), _[Maha Chor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maha\_Chor "Maha Chor")_ (1976), in [_Anhonee_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anhonee_(1973_film) "Anhonee (1973 film)") (1973) with [Sanjeev Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjeev_Kumar "Sanjeev Kumar") and in eight films with [Manoj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoj_Kumar "Manoj Kumar") namely _Shaheed_, _[Upkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upkar "Upkar")_ (1967), _[Purab Aur Paschim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purab\_Aur\_Paschim "Purab Aur Paschim")_ (1970), _[Shor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shor\_(film) "Shor (film)")_ (1972), _[Roti Kapda Aur Makaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roti\_Kapda\_Aur\_Makaan "Roti Kapda Aur Makaan")_ (1974), _[Sanyasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanyasi\_(1975\_film) "Sanyasi (1975 film)")_ (1975), _[Dus Numbri](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dus\_Numbri "Dus Numbri")_ (1976) and _[Santosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santosh\_(1989\_film) "Santosh (1989 film)")_ (1989).

From the 1990s, Kaushal only sporadically appeared in films. She latterly appeared in _[Chennai Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai\_Express "Chennai Express")_ (2013) and the romantic drama _[Kabir Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabir\_Singh "Kabir Singh")_ (2019), both of which rank among the [highest grossing Indian films](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_highest-grossing_Indian_films "List of highest-grossing Indian films"), winning the [Screen Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screen_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Screen Award for Best Supporting Actress") and a nomination for the [Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actress "Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actress") for the latter. She made her final film appearance with a cameo in _[Laal Singh Chaddha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laal\_Singh\_Chaddha "Laal Singh Chaddha")_ in 2022.

## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kamini_Kaushal&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

Kamini Kaushal was born in [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore") on 24 February 1927.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-telegraph2014-2)[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-3) She was the youngest of two brothers and three sisters.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Filmfare2014-4) She was the daughter of [Shiv Ram Kashyap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shiv_Ram_Kashyap "Shiv Ram Kashyap"), professor of botany, [University of Punjab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_the_Punjab "University of the Punjab") at [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore"), [British India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") (present-day [Pakistan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pakistan "Pakistan")), and used to have a house in Chaubarji area of Lahore. Kashyap is widely regarded as the father of Indian botany.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-5) Her father was a distinguished botanist who discovered six species of plants. She was only seven when her father died on 26 November 1934.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-telegraph2014-2) She did her B.A. (honours) in English literature from [Government College in Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_College_University,_Lahore "Government College University, Lahore"). She got an offer to act in films through [Chetan Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chetan_Anand_(director) "Chetan Anand (director)") in 1946 with _Neecha Nagar_.

Talking about her teenage years, she said in an interview, "I had no time to fool. I didn't have any crush. I was busy swimming, riding, skating and doing radio plays on Akashwani, for which I was paid Rs 10."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Filmfare2014-4) When her elder sister died in a car accident,[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Filmfare2014-4) leaving behind two daughters, Kaushal had to marry her brother-in-law, B.S. Sood in 1948. She set up home in Bombay where her husband was a chief engineer in Bombay Port Trust.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-telegraph2014-2)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Filmfare2014-4) Her elder sister's daughters are Kumkum Somani and Kavita Sahni. Kumkum Somani has written a book for children on Gandhi's philosophy and Kavita Sahni is an artist.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-telegraph2014-2) Kamini had three sons after 1955, Rahul, Vidur and Shravan.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Filmfare2014-4)

In the 1950s, the couple lived in a spacious manor-type house "Gateside" in [Mazagaon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mazagaon "Mazagaon"), which was allotted to her husband by BPT.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-6)

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kamini_Kaushal&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

Kamini had been a stage actress in [Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Delhi "Delhi") during her college days from 1942 to 1945. She worked as a radio child artist with the name "Uma" in [Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lahore "Lahore") before the Partition, from 1937 to 1940.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Rediff2007-7) She said in an interview about whether she wanted to be an actress in her childhood: "I come from a very intellectual family. My dad, S. R. Kashyap, was a professor at [Government College, Lahore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_College_University,_Lahore "Government College University, Lahore") and the President of the Science Congress. He'd written about 50 books on botany. Growing up, our family concentrated more on knowledge, but he never deterred us from doing anything we wanted as long as it was positive."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-8) Though she had no dreams of joining the film industry while being in college, she was a fan of actor Ashok Kumar. Once she said in an interview: "We were to perform for the war relief fund in college. Ashok Kumar and Leela Chitins were the chief guests. After the show we went to meet him. I thought of having some fun. As he stood talking to the students, I pulled his hair from behind."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Filmfare2014-4)[Chetan Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chetan_Anand_(director) "Chetan Anand (director)") gave her the role of the leading heroine in his film _[Neecha Nagar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neecha\_Nagar "Neecha Nagar")_. This movie was done by her before marriage and released in 1946.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Rediff2007-7) She quoted in an interview, when asked about why her name was changed from Uma to Kamini: "Chetan's wife Uma Anand was also part of the film. My name also being Uma, he wanted a different name for me. I asked him to give me a name beginning with 'K' to match with the names of my daughters Kumkum and Kavita."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Filmfare2014-4) She won an award at the Montreal Film Festival for her performance in her debut film.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Kamini_Kaushal,_legend-9) She quoted in an interview about how she got her debut film: "Ravi Shankar was new, he had not done music for anybody. It was Zohra Segal's debut. Uma Anand (Chetan's wife) was with us in college — we were together. Chetan had been teaching at The Doon School and got to me through my brother.".[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-telegraph2014-2)

After _Neecha Nagar_, she returned to Lahore, but offers started coming in, hence she used to come for shooting from Lahore. After her sudden marriage in 1947, she settled in Bombay with her husband. She became the first leading heroine to continue working as lead film heroine after her marriage as well. Kamini was one of the first well educated heroines (BA in English) in Hindi cinema.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Kamini_Kaushal,_legend-9) She learnt [Bharatnatyam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharatnatyam "Bharatnatyam") at Mumbai's Sri Rajarajeswari Bharata Natya Kala Mandir, where Guru T. K. Mahalingam Pillai, doyen among nattuvanars taught.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-10) Since 1948, Kamini Kaushal worked with all the top leading men of her time, such as [Ashok Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashok_Kumar "Ashok Kumar"), [Raj Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Kapoor "Raj Kapoor"), [Dev Anand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dev_Anand "Dev Anand"), [Raaj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raaj_Kumar "Raaj Kumar") and [Dilip Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dilip_Kumar "Dilip Kumar").[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

In every film starring her as lead heroine, except when opposite Ashok Kumar, in the period 1947 to 1955, her name used to appear first in the credits before the leading hero's name appeared. Her pairing opposite Dilip Kumar was popular with audiences with box office hits such as _[Shaheed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaheed\_(1948\_film) "Shaheed (1948 film)")_ (1948), _Pugree_, _Nadiya Ke Paar_ (1949), _Shabnam_ (1949) and _Arzoo_ (1950)).[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-red-11) The popularity as an actress increased with Filmistan's _Do Bhai_ (1947), aided by Geeta Roy's impassioned singing of songs such as "Mera sundar sapna", which, incidentally, was shot in a single take.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Kamini_Kaushal,_legend-9) Kamini was paired opposite Dev Anand in his very first success, Bombay Talkies' production _Ziddi_ (1948), a light romance. The pair followed this up with _[Namoona](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namoona "Namoona")_. Kamini played the third angle to the Dev-Suraiya pair in _Shayar_. In Raj Kapoor's directorial debut _Aag_ (1948), she did a cameo as one of his three heroines (Nargis and Nigar were the other two), whose relationship with the hero doesn't fructify. She also starred with Raj Kapoor in _Jail Yatra_.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Kamini_Kaushal,_legend-9)

Kamini Kaushal was the first lead heroine for whom [Lata Mangeshkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lata_Mangeshkar "Lata Mangeshkar") ever sang for and it was for the film _Ziddi_ in 1948. Kamini quoted in an interview: "Lata sang for me in _Ziddi_ for the first time. That was the first time she sang for the leading lady in a film. Before that, she sang for actresses in supporting roles. Shamshad Begum and Surinder Kaur — whose voices had more bass — used to sing my songs. On the music credits on the record, Lata's name was not mentioned. Instead, it was mentioned that Asha sang the songs — Asha was my screen name (in the film _Ziddi_). That's why people thought I had sung it.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-12) The playback singers - Kishore Kumar and Lata Mangeshkar recorded their first duet - "Ye Kaun Aya Re" together in the 1948 film _Ziddi_.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-13)

Her other successful films as lead heroine in films from 1946 to 1963 include _[Paras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paras\_(1949\_film) "Paras (1949 film)")_ (1949), _Namoona_, _Jhanjar_, _Aabru_, _Night Club_, _[Jailor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jailor\_(1958\_film) "Jailor (1958 film)")_, _[Bade Sarkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bade\_Sarkar "Bade Sarkar")_, _Bada Bhai_, _Poonam_ and _[Godaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Godaan "Godaan")_. Kamini became a producer and signed on then-matinee idol Ashok Kumar in _Poonam_ and _Night Club_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Rediff2007-7) She did lighthearted roles in _Chalis Baba Ek Chor_ (1954) and also did serious tragedy genre roles in _Aas_, _Ansoo_ and _Jailor_. In the Sohrab Modi-directed _Jailor_ (1958), Kamini gave a goosebump-raising performance as Modi's wife, who is pushed towards adultery by his ruthless tyranny.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Kamini_Kaushal,_legend-9) Trilok Jetley, who adopted Premchand's famous story _Godaan_ on screen, put his film on hold, while Kamini was pregnant with her second child, because he wanted to capitalise on the softness in her voice. Pandit Ravi Shankar composed the score for her first (_Neecha Nagar_ in 1946) and last (_Godaan_ in 1963) films as a heroine.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Kamini_Kaushal,_legend-9)

In 1965, she moved to playing character roles with a film called _[Shaheed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaheed\_(1965\_film) "Shaheed (1965 film)")_. She made the transition from playing leading heroine roles to character roles very easily. Her performances were appreciated in [_Waris_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waris_(1969_film) "Waris (1969 film)"), _[Vishwas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vishwas "Vishwas")_, [_Yakeen_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yakeen_(1969_film) "Yakeen (1969 film)"), _[Aadmi Aur Insaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aadmi\_Aur\_Insaan "Aadmi Aur Insaan")_, _[Uphaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uphaar "Uphaar")_, _[Qaid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qaid\_(film) "Qaid (film)")_, _[Bhanwar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhanwar\_(film) "Bhanwar (film)")_, _[Tangewala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tangewala "Tangewala")_ and _[Heeralaal Pannalaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heeralaal\_Pannalaal\_(1978\_film) "Heeralaal Pannalaal (1978 film)")_. As a character artist she was a fixture in seven [Manoj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoj_Kumar "Manoj Kumar") films - _[Shaheed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaheed\_(1965\_film) "Shaheed (1965 film)")_, _[Upkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upkar "Upkar")_, _[Purab Aur Paschim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Purab\_Aur\_Paschim "Purab Aur Paschim")_, _[Sanyasi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanyasi\_(1975\_film) "Sanyasi (1975 film)")_, _[Shor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shor\_(film) "Shor (film)")_, _[Roti Kapda Aur Makaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roti\_Kapda\_Aur\_Makaan "Roti Kapda Aur Makaan")_, _[Dus Numbari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dus\_Numbari "Dus Numbari")_ and _[Santosh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santosh\_(1989\_film) "Santosh (1989 film)")_ (1989). Kaushal had a long stint in films with releases till 2014.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-14) She stunned audiences by playing a mercenary vamp with aplomb in the film [_Anhonee_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anhonee_(1973_film) "Anhonee (1973 film)") (1973).[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Kamini_Kaushal,_legend-9) Kamini Kaushal played mother to [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna") in [_Prem Nagar_](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem_Nagar_(1974_film) "Prem Nagar (1974 film)") in 1974, and in _[Maha Chor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maha\_Chor "Maha Chor")_ in 1976, and as sister in law to Khanna in _[Do Raaste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do\_Raaste "Do Raaste")_.

Dilip Kumar, in his biography, has admitted his attraction to her while they acted in films together, but Kamini rejected his proposal as she was already married to her elder sister's widower and was taking care of her elder sister's kids.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-15) Dilip said that she was his first love.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-16)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-17) Kamini quoted in an interview on this: "We were both shattered. We were very happy with each other. We shared a great rapport. But what to do? That's life. I can't dump people and say 'Enough now, I'm going!' I had taken on the girls. I wouldn't be able to show my face to my sister. My husband, a fine human being, understood why it happened. Everyone falls in love."[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-Filmfare2014-4)

She made a popular puppet show broadcast on the national channel at the time, "Doordarshan", which ran for a year (1989 to 1991), and was the first such children's series in Hindi.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-18) She stepped into writing children's stories. Her stories used to be published in the children's magazine _Paraag_, featuring the antics of 'Bunty', and 'Chotbhai' and 'Motabhai' – who were all loosely based on her own son and his cousin contemporaries. She dabbled in television doing serials such as _Chand Sitare_ on [Doordarshan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Doordarshan "Doordarshan"). In 1986, Kaushal made an animation film, _Meri Pari_.[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

She appeared in _[The Jewel in the Crown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Jewel\_in\_the\_Crown\_(TV\_series) "The Jewel in the Crown (TV series)")_ (1984), a popular British television serial, as Aunt Shalini.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-telegraph2014-2)

Kaushal worked in the highly popular serial _Shanno Ki Shaadi_, on [StarPlus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/StarPlus "StarPlus").[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-19) She played Bebe, the grandmother of Shanno, the main protagonist played by [Divya Dutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Divya_Dutta "Divya Dutta"). She also acted in Sri Adhikari Brothers' TV Serial _Waqt Ki Raftaar_ (DD National).[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

She said in an interview: "I, along with only few Indian heroines like [Saroja Devi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saroja_Devi "Saroja Devi"), [Bhanumathi Ramakrishna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bhanumathi_Ramakrishna "Bhanumathi Ramakrishna"), [Sowcar Janaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sowcar_Janaki "Sowcar Janaki"), [Mala Sinha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mala_Sinha "Mala Sinha"), [Moushumi Chatterjee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moushumi_Chatterjee "Moushumi Chatterjee"), [Padmini](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padmini_(actress) "Padmini (actress)") and Sharmila Tagore were the few who got married early and had success in the film industry even after our marriages as well as led a happy married life."[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_]

Since the 1990s, she only occasionally appeared in films such as _[Gumrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gumrah\_(1993\_film) "Gumrah (1993 film)")_ (1993), _[Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Har\_Dil\_Jo\_Pyar\_Karega "Har Dil Jo Pyar Karega")_ (2000), _[Chori Chori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chori\_Chori\_(2003\_film) "Chori Chori (2003 film)")_ (2003), _[Chennai Express](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chennai\_Express "Chennai Express")_ (2013) and _[Kabir Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabir\_Singh "Kabir Singh")_ (2019). Her final film appearance was a cameo in _[Laal Singh Chaddha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laal\_Singh\_Chaddha "Laal Singh Chaddha")_ in 2022.

## Death

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kamini_Kaushal&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Death")]

Kaushal died in [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai") on 13 November 2025, at the age of 98.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-21)

## Legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Kamini_Kaushal&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Legacy")]

One of the highest paid actresses of the late 1940s, Kaushal appeared in _[Box Office India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box\_Office\_India "Box Office India")_'s "Top Actresses" list twice, 1947 and 1948.[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-25) In 2022, she was placed in _[Outlook India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlook\_India "Outlook India")_'s "75 Best Bollywood Actresses" list.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kamini_Kaushal#cite_note-26)

Ask ten people to name the best economics college in India, and you'll get ten different answers. It really just comes down to the kind of career you want and the type of campus environment you prefer.

On the government side, Delhi University is still the go-to for a BA (Hons.) Economics. Places like SRCC, St. Stephen’s, Hindu, Hansraj, and LSR have built huge reputations because of intense academics and a super competitive cohort.

If you are looking at private universities, the options look quite different. One of the names that comes up often is O.P. Jindal Global University. They blend economics with fields like public policy, international relations, business, or data science, rather than studying it as a single subject. It’s also a good option because economics today extends well beyond supply and demand graphs.

One mistake I often see is students choosing a college based only on popularity. I would suggest that you look at the curriculum, faculty, internship opportunities, research exposure, exchange programs, and the kind of careers graduates pursue after finishing the degree.

The good news is that a BA (Hons.) Economics can open doors to consulting, finance, public policy, analytics, research, higher education, and even entrepreneurship. The right college gives you the foundation, but your curiosity and willingness to engage with the subject will determine how far you go.

So rather than asking, “Which is the best college?” try asking, “Which college is the best fit for the way I want to learn?” That question usually leads to a much better decision.

Hindi (Bollywood) and pan-Indian

*   Darsheel Safary — Famous child-actor in Taare Zameen Par; subsequently continued in films/TV.
*   Harish Kumar — Child actor in many Telugu, Tamil and Hindi films; later adult roles as well.

One of the most popular actresses of Bollywood who acted for more than 3 decades was Nanda. She is among some actresses like Nargis, Sarika, Neetu Singh, Padmini Kolahpure, Hansika Motwani who acted as a child artist and also as a leading actress in Bollywood.

Nanda had appeared on the silver screen for the first time as a child artist, baby Nanda at the age of 9 in the film Mandir in 1948. From 1948 to 1956 she had acted as a child artist in the films like Madir, Jaggu and Angaarey.

![Image 125](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-a78a9185472123286095cee0f85cdac3)

As a leading actress she had worked in some popular films like Chhoti Bahu, Dhool Ka Phool, Bhabhi, Kala Bazar, Kanoon, Hum Dono, Jab Jab Phool Kile, The Train, Prem Rog and Gumnaam.

The well known filmmaker V. Shantaram was her paternal uncle, he gave her a big break by casting her in the film Toofan Aur Diya in 1956.

She was nominated for Filmfare Best Actress Award for five times for the films Bhabhi, Aanchal, Ittefaq, Ahista Ahista, and Prem Rog. She had won the Filmfare Best Supporting Actress Award for the film Aanchal.

Ask ten people to name the best economics college in India, and you'll get ten different answers. It really just comes down to the kind of career you want and the type of campus environment you prefer.

On the government side, Delhi University is still the go-to for a BA (Hons.) Economics. Places like SRCC, St. Stephen’s, Hindu, Hansraj, and LSR have built huge reputations because of intense academics and a super competitive cohort.

If you are looking at private universities, the options look quite different. One of the names that comes up often is O.P. Jindal Global University. They blend economics with fields like public policy, international relations, business, or data science, rather than studying it as a single subject. It’s also a good option because economics today extends well beyond supply and demand graphs.

One mistake I often see is students choosing a college based only on popularity. I would suggest that you look at the curriculum, faculty, internship opportunities, research exposure, exchange programs, and the kind of careers graduates pursue after finishing the degree.

The good news is that a BA (Hons.) Economics can open doors to consulting, finance, public policy, analytics, research, higher education, and even entrepreneurship. The right college gives you the foundation, but your curiosity and willingness to engage with the subject will determine how far you go.

So rather than asking, “Which is the best college?” try asking, “Which college is the best fit for the way I want to learn?” That question usually leads to a much better decision.

What if I say he debuted in a movie named ‘Premada Kaanike' when he was just 6 months old, as an infant, and followed it up in ‘Sanaadi Appanna' when he was just a year-old..!

*   ‘Thaayige takka maga'

*   ‘Bhagyavantha'

‘Parashuram' was his last movie as a child artist.

One of the most popular actresses of Bollywood who acted for more than 3 decades was Nanda. She is among some actresses like Nargis, Sarika, Neetu Singh, Padmini Kolahpure, Hansika Motwani who acted as a child artist and also as a leading actress in Bollywood.

Nanda had appeared on the silver screen for the first time as a child artist, baby Nanda at the age of 9 in the film Mandir in 1948. From 1948 to 1956 she had acted as a child artist in the films like Madir, Jaggu and Angaarey.

![Image 125](https://qph.cf2.quoracdn.net/main-qimg-a78a9185472123286095cee0f85cdac3)

As a leading actress she had worked in some popular films like Chhoti Bahu, Dhool Ka Phool, Bhabhi, Kala Bazar, Kanoon, Hum Dono, Jab Jab Phool Kile, The Train, Prem Rog and Gumnaam.

The well known filmmaker V. Shantaram was her paternal uncle, he gave her a big break by casting her in the film Toofan Aur Diya in 1956.

She was nominated for Filmfare Best Actress Award for five times for the films Bhabhi, Aanchal, Ittefaq, Ahista Ahista, and Prem Rog. She had won the Filmfare Best Supporting Actress Award for the film Aanchal.

She Wore a Saree Before She Wore a School Bag

A tiny girl, barely four years old dressed in a crisp beige saree, walks confidently onto one of India's grandest stages. No nerves. No hesitation. Just quiet, unshakeable grace. She collects the National Film Award for Best Child Artist from the President of India and in that single moment, rewrites history forever.

Her name is Treesha Vivek Thosar.

And she just broke a record that stood for over six decades.

![Image 1: 🎬](https://static.xx.fbcdn.net/images/emoji.php/v9/t2d/1/16/1f3ac.png) She acted at three. She won at four. Treesha played Chimi in the Marathi film Naal 2 an innocent rural child, full of wonder. She wasn't performing. She was living the role. At an age when most children are learning alphabets, she was moving a national jury with raw, natural emotion.

![Image 2: 🏆](https://static.xx.fbcdn.net/images/emoji.php/v9/tbe/1/16/1f3c6.png) She broke Kamal Haasan's 60-year-old record. The legend himself posted publicly "You've beaten my record! I was already six when I got my first award.

She Wore a Saree Before She Wore a School Bag

A tiny girl, barely four years old dressed in a crisp beige saree, walks confidently onto one of India's grandest stages. No nerves. No hesitation. Just quiet, unshakeable grace. She collects the National Film Award for Best Child Artist from the President of India and in that single moment, rewrites history forever.

Her name is Treesha Vivek Thosar.

And she just broke a record that stood for over six decades.

![Image 1: 🎬](https://static.xx.fbcdn.net/images/emoji.php/v9/t2d/1/16/1f3ac.png) She acted at three. She won at four. Treesha played Chimi in the Marathi film Naal 2 an innocent rural child, full of wonder. She wasn't performing. She was living the role. At an age when most children are learning alphabets, she was moving a national jury with raw, natural emotion.

![Image 2: 🏆](https://static.xx.fbcdn.net/images/emoji.php/v9/tbe/1/16/1f3c6.png) She broke Kamal Haasan's 60-year-old record. The legend himself posted publicly "You've beaten my record! I was already six when I got my first award.

Sridevi started her acting journey at a very young age. She was just a child when she first appeared in films. One of her early roles was in the Tamil film Thunaivan, where she played a mythological character, showing strong screen presence even as a kid. She also did similar roles in South Indian films, often playing divine or emotional characters that needed expressive acting.

As a child artist, Sridevi worked in Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, and Kannada films. Even at that age, people noticed how naturally she performed in front of the camera. It felt like acting came to her without effort. Many believe she showed early signs of becoming a great actress because of her expressions, confidence, and ability to handle different emotions.

Her journey to Bollywood was also very interesting. She first appeared in Hindi films as a child artist, but her big breakthrough came later with movies like Himmatwala. After that, she became one of the biggest stars in Hindi cinema. Her performances in films like Mr. India, Chandni, and Sadma made her a household name.

There are many fun stories about her. It is said that she was very shy in real life and didn’t talk much, but once the camera started rolling, she completely transformed. Directors loved working with her because she could do emotional scenes, comedy, and dance equally well.

Sridevi showed from her childhood itself that she was special. Over time, she truly proved why she is called the “Queen of Acting.”

Sridevi started her acting journey at a very young age. She was just a child when she first appeared in films. One of her early roles was in the Tamil film Thunaivan, where she played a mythological character, showing strong screen presence even as a kid. She also did similar roles in South Indian films, often playing divine or emotional characters that needed expressive acting.

As a child artist, Sridevi worked in Tamil, Telugu, Malayalam, and Kannada films. Even at that age, people noticed how naturally she performed in front of the camera. It felt like acting came to her without effort. Many believe she showed early signs of becoming a great actress because of her expressions, confidence, and ability to handle different emotions.

Her journey to Bollywood was also very interesting. She first appeared in Hindi films as a child artist, but her big breakthrough came later with movies like Himmatwala. After that, she became one of the biggest stars in Hindi cinema. Her performances in films like Mr. India, Chandni, and Sadma made her a household name.

There are many fun stories about her. It is said that she was very shy in real life and didn’t talk much, but once the camera started rolling, she completely transformed. Directors loved working with her because she could do emotional scenes, comedy, and dance equally well.

Sridevi showed from her childhood itself that she was special. Over time, she truly proved why she is called the “Queen of Acting.”

Indra Sen Johar was born on 16 February 1920 in Talagang City, Talagang Tehsil, Jhelum District, Punjab, British India (now within modern-day Talagang District, Punjab, Pakistan). He did an MA degree in Economics and Politics before completing his LLB. In August 1947, during the Partition of India, Johar was visiting Patiala with his family for a wedding when serious rioting broke out in Lahore, resulting in the Shah Alami Bazaar, once the largely Hindu quarter of the Walled City, being entirely burnt down. Johar never returned to Lahore. For a period he worked in Jalandhar while his family remained in Delhi, before he eventually moved to Bombay, where he made his acting debut in the 1949 Hindi comedy action film Ek Thi Ladki. Johar married Ramma Hoon in 1943 in Lahore. The couple became parents to two children, a son named Anil and a daughter named Neelam, who adopted the stage name Ambika Johar. Both his children worked in a handful of films in the late 1970s, including Nasbandi (1978) and 5 Rifles. Ramma herself acted in small roles in a couple of films, most notably as Balraj Sahni's cunning sister in Garam Hawa. Johar and Ramma were divorced; theirs was one of the earliest legal divorces in the country. After this divorce, Johar married and divorced no less than four more women (five marriages in all, and as many divorces). One of his later wives was the actress Sonia Sahni, who had made her film debut in Johar's production Johar-Mehmood in Goa (1965). With his arms cut off by Gabbar years earlier, Thakur fights using spiked shoes and ultimately pins Gabbar onto a sharp nail — completing his long-awaited revenge. **Shashi Kapoor** (pronounced[[ʃəʃi kəpuːɾ]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Help:IPA/Hindi_and_Urdu "Help:IPA/Hindi and Urdu"); born **Balbir Raj Kapoor**; 18 March 1938 – 4 December 2017) was an Indian actor and producer known primarily for his work in [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi "Hindi") films. He is considered as one of the greatest actors in the history of [Hindi cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-top_actor-1)[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-2) and is a recipient of [several accolades](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor,_roles_and_awards "Shashi Kapoor, roles and awards"), including four [National Film Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Awards "National Film Awards") and two [Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Awards "Filmfare Awards"). The [Government of India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Government_of_India "Government of India") honoured him with the [Padma Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Padma_Bhushan "Padma Bhushan") in 2011, and the [Dadasaheb Phalke Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dadasaheb_Phalke_Award "Dadasaheb Phalke Award") in 2014, for his contribution to Indian cinema.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-3)

Born into the [Kapoor family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapoor_family "Kapoor family"), he was the third and the youngest son of [Prithviraj Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prithviraj_Kapoor "Prithviraj Kapoor"). He began his career as a child actor in 1948 with his brother [Raj Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Kapoor "Raj Kapoor")'s maiden directorial _[Aag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aag\_(1948\_film) "Aag (1948 film)")_, and had his first role as an adult in 1961 with [Yash Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yash_Chopra "Yash Chopra")'s political drama _[Dharmputra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharmputra "Dharmputra")_.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-4) He established himself in 1965 with two blockbusters - _[Waqt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waqt\_(1965\_film) "Waqt (1965 film)")_ and _[Jab Jab Phool Khile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jab\_Jab\_Phool\_Khile "Jab Jab Phool Khile")_.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-auto-5) This was followed by a period of further success, with _[Kanyadaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyadaan\_(1968\_film) "Kanyadaan (1968 film)")_, _[Sharmeelee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmeelee "Sharmeelee")_ and _[Aa Gale Lag Jaa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aa\_Gale\_Lag\_Jaa\_(1973\_film) "Aa Gale Lag Jaa (1973 film)")_.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-6) His career reached new heights in 1974 with _[Chor Machaye Shor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chor\_Machaye\_Shor "Chor Machaye Shor")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-auto1-7) With its success, Kapoor became the top five to six saleable stars of the time and starred in top–grossing Hindi films from the early-1970s to 1980s, such as _[Roti Kapada Aur Makaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roti\_Kapada\_Aur\_Makaan "Roti Kapada Aur Makaan")_, _[Deewaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deewaar "Deewaar")_, _[Chori Mera Kaam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chori\_Mera\_Kaam "Chori Mera Kaam")_, _[Kabhi Kabhie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabhi\_Kabhie "Kabhi Kabhie")_, _[Fakira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fakira "Fakira")_, _[Trishul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trishul\_(film) "Trishul (film)")_, _[Suhaag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suhaag\_(1979\_film) "Suhaag (1979 film)")_, _[Kaala Patthar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaala\_Patthar "Kaala Patthar")_, _[Kranti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kranti "Kranti")_ and _[Namak Halaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namak\_Halaal "Namak Halaal")_.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-auto1-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-NK-8) He received critical acclaim for his portrayal of a reckless chieftain in _[Junoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junoon\_(1978\_film) "Junoon (1978 film)")_, a businessman in _[Kalyug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalyug\_(1981\_film) "Kalyug (1981 film)")_, a strict father in _[Vijeta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijeta\_(1982\_film) "Vijeta (1982 film)")_ and an upright journalist in _[New Delhi Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Delhi\_Times "New Delhi Times")_ for which he won [National Film Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Actor last film that he appeared in, was the much delayed _[Ghar Bazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghar\_Bazar "Ghar Bazar")_ which was released in
