## Early life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Kapoor&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Early life")]

See also: [Kapoor family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kapoor_family "Kapoor family")

[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/Shashi_Kapoor%2C_Baby_Madhuri_in_Bachpan.jpg/250px-Shashi_Kapoor%2C_Baby_Madhuri_in_Bachpan.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Shashi_Kapoor,_Baby_Madhuri_in_Bachpan.jpg)

Shashi Kapoor (left) with Baby Madhuri (centre) and Baby Shakuntala (right)

Shashi Kapoor was born as Balbir Raj Kapoor[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-12) to [Prithviraj Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prithviraj_Kapoor "Prithviraj Kapoor") and his wife in [Calcutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta "Calcutta"), British India, on 18 March 1938. He was the youngest brother of [Raj Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Kapoor "Raj Kapoor") and [Shammi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shammi_Kapoor "Shammi Kapoor"). Actor [Trilok Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trilok_Kapoor "Trilok Kapoor") was his paternal uncle.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-13)

Kapoor acted in plays, directed and produced by his father [Prithviraj Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prithviraj_Kapoor "Prithviraj Kapoor"), while travelling with [Prithvi Theatres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prithvi_Theatres "Prithvi Theatres"). He started acting in films as a child in the late 1940s under the name of Shashiraj, as there was already another actor by the same name who used to act in mythological films as a child. His best-known performances as a child actor were in _[Aag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aag\_(1948\_film) "Aag (1948 film)")_ (1948) and _[Awaara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Awaara "Awaara")_ (1951), where he played the younger version of the characters played by his older brother [Raj Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Kapoor "Raj Kapoor"),[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-14) and in _[Sangram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangram\_(1950\_film) "Sangram (1950 film)")_ (1950), where he played the younger version of [Ashok Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ashok_Kumar "Ashok Kumar") and _[Dana Paani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daana\_Paani\_(1953\_film) "Daana Paani (1953 film)")_ (1953) where he acted with [Bharat Bhushan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bharat_Bhushan "Bharat Bhushan"). He worked in four Hindi films as a child actor from 1948 to 1954.

## Career

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Kapoor&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Career")]

### Rise to prominence & Stardom (1961–1973)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Kapoor&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Rise to prominence & Stardom (1961–1973)")]

After appearing as a child artist in some highly successful films like _[Sangram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sangram\_(1950\_film) "Sangram (1950 film)")_ (1950), _[Samadhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samadhi\_(1950\_film) "Samadhi (1950 film)")_ (1950) and _[Awaara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Awaara "Awaara")_ (1951), Shashi Kapoor made his debut as a leading man in 1961 with [Yash Chopra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yash_Chopra "Yash Chopra")'s [partition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Partition_of_India "Partition of India") drama _[Dharmputra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dharmputra "Dharmputra")_.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-15) This was followed by another film released the same year, _Char Diwari_. Both _Dharmputra_ and _Char Diwari_ did not do well financially.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-auto1-7) From 1962 to 1964, Kapoor had minor successes with - [Bimal Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bimal_Roy "Bimal Roy")'s _[Prem Patra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem\_Patra "Prem Patra")_ (1962) and Kanak Mishra's _[Yeh Dil Kisko Doon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeh\_Dil\_Kisko\_Doon "Yeh Dil Kisko Doon")_ (1963).[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-16) He also made his [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language "English language") film debut in 1963 with [James Ivory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Ivory "James Ivory")'s acclaimed [family drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_film "Family film")_[The Householder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Householder "The Householder")_.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-IvoryLong2005-17)

The year 1965 changed his fortune as he starred in two highest grossing films of that year with Yash Chopra's [masala film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masala_film "Masala film")_[Waqt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waqt\_(1965\_film) "Waqt (1965 film)")_ and Suraj Prakash's [romantic musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance_film "Romance film")_[Jab Jab Phool Khile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jab\_Jab\_Phool\_Khile "Jab Jab Phool Khile")_.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-18)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-auto-5)_Waqt_ went on to become a massive box office success, receiving praise for cast performances, Chopra's direction and cinematography. Today, it is widely regarded as an evergreen classic.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-19) The huge box office success of _Waqt_ was followed by another, _Jab Jab Phool Khile_ which had Kapoor paired opposite [Nanda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nanda_(actress) "Nanda (actress)").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-21) It too opened to highly positive response from critics, especially for its soundtrack composed by [Kalyanji–Anandji](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalyanji%E2%80%93Anandji "Kalyanji–Anandji"), which was the fourth best-selling Hindi film album of the 1960s with a number of melodious songs, like "Ye Samaa Samaa Hai Pyar Ka", "Affoo Khudaya", "Ek Tha Gul Aur Ek Thi Bulbul", "Na Na Karte Pyar Tumhin Se", "Pardesiyon Se Na Ankhiyan Milana".[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-23)_Jab Jab Phool Khile_ made Kapoor a star and won him that year's [BFJA Award for Best Actor (Hindi)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BFJA_Award_for_Best_Actor_(Hindi) "BFJA Award for Best Actor (Hindi)") for his moving performance of an innocent boatman in the film.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-25)

In spite of establishing himself, Kapoor had only a few major hits and some lukewarm successes in the late-1960s.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-auto1-7)

In 1966, he starred alongside [Kishore Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kishore_Kumar "Kishore Kumar"), [Mehmood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mehmood_(actor) "Mehmood (actor)"), [Kalpana Mohan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalpana_Mohan "Kalpana Mohan"), [Rajasree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajasree "Rajasree") and [Mumtaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumtaz_(Indian_actress) "Mumtaz (Indian actress)") in [C. V. Sridhar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C._V._Sridhar "C. V. Sridhar")'s [romantic comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_comedy "Romantic comedy")_[Pyar Kiye Jaa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pyar\_Kiye\_Jaa "Pyar Kiye Jaa")_.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-26)_Pyar Kiye Jaa_ proved to be a hit, but his other release _[Neend Hamari Khwab Tumhare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neend\_Hamari\_Khwab\_Tumhare\_(1966\_film) "Neend Hamari Khwab Tumhare (1966 film)")_ again opposite Nanda did only average business at the box office.[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-27) After seeing two more moderate successes in 1967 with _Dil Ne Pukara_ and _[Aamne Samne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aamne\_Samne\_(1967\_film) "Aamne Samne (1967 film)")_, the following year, he delivered a superhit in _[Kanyadaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kanyadaan\_(1968\_film) "Kanyadaan (1968 film)")_ opposite [Asha Parekh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asha_Parekh "Asha Parekh"), followed by a hit film _[Haseena Maan Jayegi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haseena\_Maan\_Jayegi "Haseena Maan Jayegi")_ co-starring [Babita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babita "Babita").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-28) The soundtrack of _Kanyadaan_ composed by [Shankar-Jaikishan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shankar-Jaikishan "Shankar-Jaikishan") was also very successful with two chartbuster [Mohammed Rafi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammed_Rafi "Mohammed Rafi") solos - "Likhe Jo Khat Tujhe" and "Meri Zindagi Mein Aate".[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-29) In the beginning of the 1970s, Kapoor delivered two notable commercial successes, [Samir Ganguly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Samir_Ganguly "Samir Ganguly")'s [romantic thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_thriller "Romantic thriller")_[Sharmeelee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sharmeelee "Sharmeelee")_ (1971) opposite [Rakhee Gulzar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rakhee_Gulzar "Rakhee Gulzar") and [Manmohan Desai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manmohan_Desai "Manmohan Desai")'s [romantic drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance_film "Romance film")_[Aa Gale Lag Jaa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aa\_Gale\_Lag\_Jaa\_(1973\_film) "Aa Gale Lag Jaa (1973 film)")_ (1973) co-starring Sharmila Tagore.[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-32)

### Further success & Continues as a Top Star (1974–1982)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Kapoor&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Further success & Continues as a Top Star (1974–1982)")]

The year 1974 changed the trajectory of Kapoor's career, elevating him to a new level.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-auto1-7) It started with Ashok Roy's [action comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_film "Action film")_[Chor Machaye Shor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chor\_Machaye\_Shor "Chor Machaye Shor")_ which also had [Mumtaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumtaz_(Indian_actress) "Mumtaz (Indian actress)"), [Asrani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asrani "Asrani") and [Danny Denzongpa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danny_Denzongpa "Danny Denzongpa") in the lead.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-33)_Chor Machaye Shor_ proved to be a blockbuster in India as well as overseas, putting a line of producers outside Kapoor's house and making him top five to six saleable stars of the time.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-bo25y-34)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-auto1-7) The huge box office success of _Chor Machaye Shor_ was followed by [Manoj Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manoj_Kumar "Manoj Kumar")'s social drama _[Roti Kapada Aur Makaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roti\_Kapada\_Aur\_Makaan "Roti Kapada Aur Makaan")_.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-35)_Roti Kapada Aur Makaan_ went on to become an _All Time Blockbuster_ and is regarded as one of the most influential movies of its time.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-bo25y-34)[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-36)_Roti Kapada Aur Makaan_ and _Chor Machaye Shor_ took first and second spot, respectively at the box office in 1974.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-37) Apart from commercial success, both the films had highly successful music and were two of the best-selling [Bollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_film_music "Hindi film music") albums of the decade.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-boi70s-38) The song "Le Jayenge, Le Jayenge Dilwale Dulhaniya Le Jayenge" from _Chor Machaye Shor_ was so popular that it went on to inspire the title of [Shah Rukh Khan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shah_Rukh_Khan "Shah Rukh Khan") starrer _[Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dilwale\_Dulhania\_Le\_Jayenge "Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge")_.[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-39) 1975 proved to be another iconic year for Kapoor as he formed a hit pair with megastar [Amitabh Bachchan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amitabh_Bachchan "Amitabh Bachchan") and together both of them gave many successful and iconic films to [Hindi cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_language "Hindi language").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-40) His first release _[Anari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anari\_(1975\_film) "Anari (1975 film)")_ underperformed commercially, but his second release, _[Deewaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deewaar "Deewaar")_ directed by Yash Chopra, written by [Salim-Javed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salim-Javed "Salim-Javed") and co-starring Bachchan, [Parveen Babi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parveen_Babi "Parveen Babi"), [Neetu Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neetu_Singh "Neetu Singh"), proved to be a widespread critical and commercial success, eventually emerging a major blockbuster.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-41) Today, it is considered one of the best films ever made in the history of [Indian cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_cinema "Indian cinema") and got featured in the book [1001 Movies You Must See Before You Die](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1001_Movies_You_Must_See_Before_You_Die "1001 Movies You Must See Before You Die").[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-43)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-44) One of Kapoor's dialogue "Mere paas maa hai" ("I have mother"), is widely known in India and has become part of Indian popular culture.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-45) His impactful portrayal of a police officer torn between love for his brother and duty met with acclaim and won him [Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor").[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-46) His next release was [Raj Khosla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Raj_Khosla "Raj Khosla")'s [romantic drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romance_film "Romance film")_[Prem Kahani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prem\_Kahani\_(1975\_film) "Prem Kahani (1975 film)")_ which also had [Rajesh Khanna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rajesh_Khanna "Rajesh Khanna") and Mumtaz in the lead.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-47) The film received good response from reviewers as well as the audience and proved to be a hit at the box office.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-48) Kapoor delivered another huge hit that year with [Brij Sadanah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brij_Sadanah "Brij Sadanah")'s action comedy _[Chori Mera Kaam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chori\_Mera\_Kaam "Chori Mera Kaam")_ opposite [Zeenat Aman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zeenat_Aman "Zeenat Aman"), followed by a semi-hit film, _[Salaakhen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salaakhen\_(1975\_film) "Salaakhen (1975 film)")_ alongside [Sulakshana Pandit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulakshana_Pandit "Sulakshana Pandit") to go with the huge grossers.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-49)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-FI1976-50) He began 1976 with Yash Chopra's romantic musical _[Kabhi Kabhie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabhi\_Kabhie "Kabhi Kabhie")_.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-51) It had a massive star cast comprising [Waheeda Rehman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waheeda_Rehman "Waheeda Rehman"), Bachchan, [Rishi Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rishi_Kapoor "Rishi Kapoor"), Rakhee and [Neetu Singh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neetu_Singh "Neetu Singh").[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-52) Despite its heavy theme, _Kabhi Kabhie_ went on to become a superhit.[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-53) It also had a chartbuster soundtrack composed by [Khayyam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Khayyam "Khayyam") with lyrics written by [Sahir Ludhianvi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sahir_Ludhianvi "Sahir Ludhianvi").[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-boi70s-38) Rakesh Budhu of _Planet Bollywood_ gave 9.5 stars out of 10 to the album stating, "_Kabhi Kabhie_ will remain an ode to brilliant melody".[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-54) For his performance in the film, Kapoor received a nomination in the [Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Supporting_Actor "Filmfare Award for Best Supporting Actor") category.[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-55) After the huge success of _Kabhi Kabhie_, he reunited with the team of _Chor Machaye Shor_ and delivered another blockbuster in _[Fakira](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fakira "Fakira")_, which was also remade in [Telugu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_language "Telugu language") as _[Dongalaku Donga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Krishna\_(Telugu\_actor) "Krishna (Telugu actor)")_ (1977).[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-FI1976-50) This was followed by two more successes in [Shibu Mitra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shibu_Mitra "Shibu Mitra")'s _[Shankar Dada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shankar\_Dada "Shankar Dada")_ and [Mohan Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohan_Kumar_(director) "Mohan Kumar (director)")'s _[Aap Beati](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aap\_Beati "Aap Beati")_.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-FI1976-50)

The following year, Kapoor reunited with Bachchan for Desh Mukherjee's highly anticipated actioner _[Immaan Dharam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immaan\_Dharam "Immaan Dharam")_, which took a bumper opening, but collections dropped afterwards due to poor reception and it ended up as a flop venture by the conclusion of its run.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-56) His most of the other releases that year, such as _[Hira Aur Patthar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hira\_Aur\_Patthar "Hira Aur Patthar")_, _[Farishta Ya Qatil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farishta\_Ya\_Qatil "Farishta Ya Qatil")_, _[Chakkar Pe Chakkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chakkar\_Pe\_Chakkar "Chakkar Pe Chakkar")_ met the same fate, with the exceptions being Prayag Raj's _[Chor Sipahee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chor\_Sipahee "Chor Sipahee")_ and Raj Tilak's _[Mukti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mukti\_(1977\_film) "Mukti (1977 film)")_.[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-57) This changed in 1978 as he delivered a string of successes with _[Phaansi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phaansi "Phaansi")_, _[Satyam Shivam Sundaram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satyam\_Shivam\_Sundaram "Satyam Shivam Sundaram")_, _[Trishul](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trishul\_(film) "Trishul (film)")_, _[Trishna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trishna\_(1978\_film) "Trishna (1978 film)")_, _[Amar Shakti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amar\_Shakti "Amar Shakti")_ and _[Aahuti](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aahuti\_(1978\_film) "Aahuti (1978 film)")_.[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-59) Kapoor also set up his own production house, Film-Valas, the same year.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-60) In 1979, he reunited with Bachchan for two big-budget actioners, The first one was Yash Chopra's _[Kaala Patthar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kaala\_Patthar "Kaala Patthar")_ and the second was Manmohan Desai's _[Suhaag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suhaag\_(1979\_film) "Suhaag (1979 film)")_.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-62)_Kaala Patthar_ written by Salim-Javed went on to become a hit.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-63) One song from the film, "Ek Raasta Hai Zindagi" sung by Kishore Kumar and filmed on Kapoor remains highly popular till date.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-64)_Suhaag_, on the other hand, was a blockbuster as well as the highest-grossing film of 1979.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-auto1-7) That same year, he produced and starred in [Shyam Benegal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shyam_Benegal "Shyam Benegal")'s art-house film _[Junoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junoon\_(1978\_film) "Junoon (1978 film)")_ which also had [Nafisa Ali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nafisa_Ali "Nafisa Ali"), [Shabana Azmi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shabana_Azmi "Shabana Azmi"), [Jennifer Kendal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Kendal "Jennifer Kendal") and [Naseeruddin Shah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naseeruddin_Shah "Naseeruddin Shah") in the lead.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-TH-65)_Junoon_ met with acclaim, winning Kapoor [National Award for Best Feature Film (Hindi)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_for_Best_Feature_Film_in_Hindi "National Film Award for Best Feature Film in Hindi") as well as [Filmfare Award for Best Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Award_for_Best_Film "Filmfare Award for Best Film").[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-66)

In 1980, Kapoor delivered a hit with _[Swayamvar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moushmi\_Chatterjee "Moushmi Chatterjee")_, but his other releases, such as _[Do Aur Do Paanch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Do\_Aur\_Do\_Paanch "Do Aur Do Paanch")_ and _[Neeyat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neeyat\_(1980\_film) "Neeyat (1980 film)")_ failed to leave a mark while [Ramesh Sippy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramesh_Sippy "Ramesh Sippy")'s mega-budget [action crime](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_Film "Action Film") film _[Shaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shaan\_(1980\_film) "Shaan (1980 film)")_ ended up as an average grosser owing to huge costs.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-67) The following year, he co-starred alongside [Dilip Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dilip_Kumar "Dilip Kumar"), Manoj Kumar, Hema Malini, [Shatrughan Sinha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatrughan_Sinha "Shatrughan Sinha") and [Parveen Babi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parveen_Babi "Parveen Babi") in the [epic historical Gaye Ustaad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maan\_Gaye\_Ustaad "Maan Gaye Ustaad")_ and received acclaim for his performances in Yash Chopra's romantic drama _[Silsila](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silsila\_(1981\_film) "Silsila (1981 film)")_ and Shyam Benegal's [crime drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_film "Crime film")_[Kalyug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalyug\_(1981\_film) "Kalyug (1981 film)")_ (which he also produced).[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-72) Kapoor had five releases in 1982. He found no success in _[Vakil Babu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vakil\_Babu "Vakil Babu")_ and _[Sawaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawaal\_(film) "Sawaal (film)")_.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-TG1982-73) However, [Bapu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bapu_(director) "Bapu (director)")'s [crime drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crime_film "Crime film") film _[Bezubaan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bezubaan "Bezubaan")_ opposite [Reena Roy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reena_Roy "Reena Roy") was a hit and [Prakash Mehra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prakash_Mehra "Prakash Mehra")'s [masala film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masala_film "Masala film")_[Namak Halaal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Namak\_Halaal "Namak Halaal")_ co-starring Bachchan, [Smita Patil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smita_Patil "Smita Patil") and Parveen Babi went on to become a blockbuster.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-NK-8) His other notable release that year was [Govind Nihalani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Govind_Nihalani "Govind Nihalani")'s [coming-of-age war](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coming_of_age "Coming of age") film _[Vijeta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijeta\_(1982\_film) "Vijeta (1982 film)")_, which had his son [Kunal Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunal_Kapoor_(actor,_born_1959) "Kunal Kapoor (actor, born 1959)") in his acting debut.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-74) The film flopped commercially, but received immense critical acclaim and won three awards at the [31st Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/31st_Filmfare_Awards "31st Filmfare Awards").[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-75)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-76)[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-77)

### Later career (1983–1998)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Kapoor&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Later career (1983–1998)")]

Post-1982, Kapoor's star power began to wane as he shifted his focus majorly towards parallel cinema and limited his work in mainstream films, accepting only few offers.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-auto1-7) After not seeing any success in 1983, the next year, he produced and starred in [Girish Karnad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Girish_Karnad "Girish Karnad")'s critically acclaimed [erotic drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_in_film "Sex in film")_[Utsav](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utsav "Utsav")_.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-78) It was filmed in Hindi and [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_language "English language") simultaneously, the [post-production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Post-production "Post-production") work of latter version was done in London.[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-79) He also played a supporting role in [K. Bapayya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._Bapayya "K. Bapayya")'s superhit drama film _[Ghar Ek Mandir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghar\_Ek\_Mandir\_(film) "Ghar Ek Mandir (film)")_.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-80) In 1985, he appeared in [Babbar Subhash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Babbar_Subhash "Babbar Subhash")'s _[Aandhi-Toofan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aandhi-Toofan "Aandhi-Toofan")_ and [Shakti Samanta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shakti_Samanta "Shakti Samanta")'s _[Alag Alag](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alag\_Alag "Alag Alag")_. While _Aandhi-Toofan_ emerged a success, _Alag Alag_ flopped at the box office.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-81)

1986 proved to be a notable year for Kapoor as he won his first [National Award for Best Actor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Award_for_Best_Actor "National Award for Best Actor") and second [BFJA Award for Best Actor (Hindi)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/BFJA_Award_for_Best_Actor_(Hindi) "BFJA Award for Best Actor (Hindi)") for the extraordinary portrayal of an honest journalist in Ramesh Sharma's highly acclaimed [political thriller](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_thriller "Political thriller")_[New Delhi Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New\_Delhi\_Times "New Delhi Times")_.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-83) His another major release of the year was Shibu Mitra's multi-starrer actioner _[Ilzaam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ilzaam "Ilzaam")_ co-starring [Shatrughan Sinha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shatrughan_Sinha "Shatrughan Sinha"), [Govinda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Govinda_(actor) "Govinda (actor)"), [Neelam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neelam_Kothari "Neelam Kothari") and [Anita Raj](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anita_Raj "Anita Raj").[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-84) The film proved to be a huge hit and also one of the top grossers of the year.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-85)

In 1987, he reunited with Govinda and Neelam for [K. Ravi Shankar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/K._Ravi_Shankar "K. Ravi Shankar")'s actioner _[Sindoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sindoor\_(1987\_film) "Sindoor (1987 film)")_ which also had [Jaya Prada](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaya_Prada "Jaya Prada") in the lead.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-86) He also did a guest appearance in [Gulzar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulzar "Gulzar")'s [romantic musical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romantic_film "Romantic film")_[Ijaazat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ijaazat "Ijaazat")_.[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-87) Although _Ijaazat_ was a commercial failure, it won massive critical acclaim.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-88) On the other hand, _Sindoor_ emerged a hit and also proved to be Kapoor's last box office success.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-89) In 1988, he acted with [Pierce Brosnan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierce_Brosnan "Pierce Brosnan") in _[The Deceivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Deceivers\_(film) "The Deceivers (film)")_.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-90) The following year, he appeared in films, such as _[Farz Ki Jung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Farz\_Ki\_Jung "Farz Ki Jung")_, _[Gair Kanooni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gair\_Kanooni "Gair Kanooni")_ and _[Clerk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clerk\_(1989\_film) "Clerk (1989 film)")_, none of which performed well critically or commercially.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-91)[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-92)

Shashi Kapoor requested Amitabh Bachchan to star in his ambitious directorial debut film _[Ajooba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ajooba "Ajooba")_ (1991).[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-93) Bachchan made a notable exception and agreed to do the film due to their friendship, even though at the time Amitabh was not signing any new films.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-Salazkina-94) Despite having a lavish budget and a huge star cast, the film flopped miserably at the box office.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-95) Kapoor also won [Special Jury Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Film_Award_%E2%80%93_Special_Jury_Award_(Feature_Film) "National Film Award – Special Jury Award (Feature Film)") for his performance in the 1993 film _[In Custody](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In\_Custody\_(film) "In Custody (film)")_ and played the Rajah in the TV miniseries _[Gulliver's Travels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gulliver's\_Travels\_(miniseries) "Gulliver's Travels (miniseries)")_ (1996).[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-96)

In 1998, he retired from acting after his final film appearances in _[Jinnah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jinnah\_(film) "Jinnah (film)")_, _[Side Streets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Side\_Streets\_(1998\_film) "Side Streets (1998 film)")_ and the much delayed _[Ghar Bazar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghar\_Bazar "Ghar Bazar")_.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-auto2-11)

### Post-retirement (2007–2010)

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Kapoor&action=edit&section=6 "Edit section: Post-retirement (2007–2010)")]

He was seen in the limelight at the _Shashi Kapoor Film Festival_ held in [Muscat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscat,_Oman "Muscat, Oman"), [Oman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oman "Oman") (September 2007). At the [55th Annual Filmfare Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/55th_Filmfare_Awards "55th Filmfare Awards") in 2010, Shashi Kapoor received the [Filmfare Lifetime Achievement Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filmfare_Lifetime_Achievement_Award "Filmfare Lifetime Achievement Award").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-97)

## Personal life

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Kapoor&action=edit&section=7 "Edit section: Personal life")]

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/eb/ShashiKapoor02.jpg/250px-ShashiKapoor02.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:ShashiKapoor02.jpg)

Shashi Kapoor with daughter [Sanjana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjana_Kapoor "Sanjana Kapoor") in 2010

Kapoor attended [Don Bosco High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Don_Bosco_High_School_(Matunga) "Don Bosco High School (Matunga)") in [Matunga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matunga "Matunga"), [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai"). He met [English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/English_people "English people") actress [Jennifer Kendal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Kendal "Jennifer Kendal") in [Calcutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta "Calcutta") in 1956 while both were working for their respective theatre groups. Shashi was both assistant stage manager as well as an actor for his father's theatre group, [Prithvi Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prithvi_Theatre "Prithvi Theatre"). [Geoffrey Kendal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoffrey_Kendal "Geoffrey Kendal")'s Shakespearean group was also present at the same time in [Calcutta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcutta "Calcutta") and [Jennifer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Kendal "Jennifer Kendal") was Geoffrey's daughter. After their subsequent meeting, the couple fell in love and after facing initial opposition from the Kendals and support from sister-in-law [Geeta Bali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geeta_Bali "Geeta Bali"), they got married in July 1958.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-98)[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-99) They acted in a number of films together, most notably in [Merchant Ivory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merchant_Ivory "Merchant Ivory") productions. They had three children: [Kunal Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunal_Kapoor_(Kapoor_family) "Kunal Kapoor (Kapoor family)"), [Karan Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karan_Kapoor "Karan Kapoor") and [Sanjana Kapoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjana_Kapoor "Sanjana Kapoor"). [Jennifer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Kendal "Jennifer Kendal") and Shashi established [Prithvi Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prithvi_Theatre "Prithvi Theatre") on 5 November 1978 in [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai"). [Jennifer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jennifer_Kendal "Jennifer Kendal") died of cancer in 1984 which shattered him. After losing her to cancer, Shashi Kapoor fell into a deep depression that he never recovered from. English actress [Felicity Kendal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felicity_Kendal "Felicity Kendal") is his sister-in-law.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-100)

His eldest son [Kunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunal_Kapoor_(actor,_born_1959) "Kunal Kapoor (actor, born 1959)") is married to director [Ramesh Sippy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramesh_Sippy "Ramesh Sippy")'s daughter. [Kunal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kunal_Kapoor_(actor,_born_1959) "Kunal Kapoor (actor, born 1959)") moved on to ad film direction and established his production house Adfilm-Valas. Shashi's daughter [Sanjana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sanjana_Kapoor "Sanjana Kapoor"), is a theatre personality and married to wildlife conservationist [Valmik Thapar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valmik_Thapar "Valmik Thapar").[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-101) They have a son named Hamir. Shashi's younger son [Karan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karan_Kapoor "Karan Kapoor") became successful in modeling and later settled down in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London "London") and runs a photography company. His grandson [Zahan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zahan_Kapoor "Zahan Kapoor") who is son of Kunal made his debut in _[Faraaz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Faraaz\_(film) "Faraaz (film)")_ (2023).[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-102)

## Reception and legacy

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Kapoor&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Reception and legacy")]

[![Image 7](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d1/The_Union_Minister_for_Finance%2C_Corporate_Affairs_and_Information_%26_Broadcasting%2C_Shri_Arun_Jaitley_presented_the_Dada_Saheb_Phalke_Award_to_the_Renowned_Actor%2C_Producer%2C_Shri_Shahsi_Kapoor%2C_at_Prithvi_Theatre_%281%29.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:The_Union_Minister_for_Finance,_Corporate_Affairs_and_Information_&_Broadcasting,_Shri_Arun_Jaitley_presented_the_Dada_Saheb_Phalke_Award_to_the_Renowned_Actor,_Producer,_Shri_Shahsi_Kapoor,_at_Prithvi_Theatre_(1).jpg)

Shashi Kapoor receiving Dada Saheb Phalke Award in 2013

Kapoor is regarded as one of the greatest and most successful actors of Indian cinema.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-top_actor-1) Apart from his work in mainstream [Hindi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hindi_cinema "Hindi cinema") films, he is known for acting and producing several acclaimed films of [parallel cinema](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parallel_cinema "Parallel cinema") such as, _[Junoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junoon\_(1978\_film) "Junoon (1978 film)")_ (1979), _[Kalyug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kalyug\_(1981\_film) "Kalyug (1981 film)")_ (1981), _[36 Chowringhee Lane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/36\_Chowringhee\_Lane "36 Chowringhee Lane")_ (1981), _[Vijeta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vijeta\_(1982\_film) "Vijeta (1982 film)")_ (1982) and _[Utsav](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utsav "Utsav")_ (1984).[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-103)[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-104)

Commenting on Kapoor's career, [Shubhra Gupta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shubhra_Gupta "Shubhra Gupta") noted: "Kapoor belonged to a gentler, kinder era, when Hindi cinema was moving away from the nation-building stories of the ‘50s, he was gentle, debonair, and the ultimate sophisticate. Kapoor wore his looks, and his understated acting ability lightly, sometimes so lightly that you often overlooked his skills."[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-105) Dinesh Raheja of _[Rediff.com](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rediff.com "Rediff.com")_ noted, "The actor who became the 1960s-1970s icon of suave, believed in pushing the envelope, while remaining rooted in commercial cinema."[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-106)_[Times Now](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Times\_Now "Times Now")_ placed him 4th in its list of the “Most Good Looking Actors on Indian Screen".[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-107) In 2022, he was placed in _[Outlook India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outlook\_India "Outlook India")_'s "75 Best Bollywood Actors" list.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-108)

Kapoor has been the solo lead in 61 films and among the lead protagonist in 116 films, more than his nephews, brothers, grand-nephews and grand-nieces.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-109) Kapoor's deep attachment and commitment to theatre which started in childhood remained almost untouched even when he was immobile due to age-related complications. After renovating [Prithvi Theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prithvi_Theatre "Prithvi Theatre") in the western part of Mumbai, he was able to successfully create an environment congenial for creative pursuits. Even today, Prithvi Theatre oozes out an infectious creative energy which can compel people to become dedicated theatre artists and earn a decent living, due to the consistent efforts of Kapoor who would be present for special theme-based theatre festivals at the theatre.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-110)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-111) In 2016, Aseem Chhabra wrote his biography "Shashi Kapoor: The Householder, the Star".[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-112)

## Death and tributes

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Shashi_Kapoor&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Death and tributes")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b8/Ambika_Soni_presented_lifetime_achievement_award_to_veteran_Actor_Shashi_Kapoor%2C_at_the_inaugural_function_of_11th_Mumbai_film_festival_%28MAMI_2009%29%2C_in_Mumbai_on_October_29%2C_2009.jpg/250px-thumbnail.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Ambika_Soni_presented_lifetime_achievement_award_to_veteran_Actor_Shashi_Kapoor,_at_the_inaugural_function_of_11th_Mumbai_film_festival_(MAMI_2009),_in_Mumbai_on_October_29,_2009.jpg)

Kapoor at an event in 2009, photographed wearing [Ajrak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ajrak "Ajrak")

Kapoor was admitted to the [Kokilaben Hospital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kokilaben_Hospital "Kokilaben Hospital"), [Versova, Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Versova,_Mumbai "Versova, Mumbai"), for what was speculated to be chest infection, and died on 4 December 2017.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-114) According to _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_, he was in hospital for treatment from long-standing liver and heart complications, and was always helping other patients.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-115) Officially, his cause of death was attributed to [liver cirrhosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cirrhosis "Cirrhosis").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-India's_problem-116)[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-Times-117) His body was cremated on 5 December 2017, at the [Santacruz Hindu Crematorium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Santacruz,_Mumbai "Santacruz, Mumbai") in Mumbai.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-DNA-118)

Kapoor and actress [Sridevi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sridevi "Sridevi"), who died in 2018, were the only two Indians to be honored posthumously in memoriam at the [90th Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/90th_Academy_Awards "90th Academy Awards").[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-119) In his honour, his autograph was inducted into the [Bollywood Walk of Fame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walk_of_the_Stars "Walk of the Stars") at [Bandra Bandstand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bandstand_Promenade "Bandstand Promenade").[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shashi_Kapoor#cite_note-120)
